entry.title: Semantic Cooperative Games for Contribution Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Pengyi Jiang, Xiaoguang Zhu, Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: Semantic Cooperative Games attribute contributions of individual agents in LLM multi-agent workflows by modeling a realized language flow as a semantic generation hypergraph and inducing agent-level values. It aims to replace high-variance counterfactual removal methods that require repeated model calls.

entry.title: FindStatBench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Combinatorial Code Synthesis

author.name: Soham Dan

entry.summary: FindStatBench is an execution benchmark of over two thousand tasks for evaluating LLMs on combinatorial code synthesis, covering statistic and map synthesis over combinatorial objects with hidden test instances. Eleven closed and open systems are graded by exact sandboxed execution.

entry.title: The Open Ant: A Robot Platform for Reinforcement Learning Research

author.name: Elena Sorina Lupu, Patrick Spieler, Khurram Javed, Kris De Asis, John D. Martin, Martha Steenstrup, Joseph Modayil

entry.summary: Presents the Open Ant, a physical robot variant of the Gymnasium Ant environment plus simulation, designed to ease sim-to-real transition for reinforcement learning research. Demonstrates learning competent walking policies from scratch in about an hour directly on the physical robot with both SARSA-lambda and Soft Actor-Critic.

entry.title: Is EEG-to-Text Feasible in Real-World Scenarios? An In-Depth Analysis Using a Neuropsychology-Inspired Benchmark

author.name: Zihan Zhang (Research Center for Social Computing and Interactive Robotics, Harbin Institute of Technology), Yu Bao (Research Center for Social Computing and Interactive Robotics, Harbin Institute of Technology, Shanghai Innovation Institute), Xiao Ding (Research Center for Social Computing and Interactive Robotics, Harbin Institute of Technology), Tianyi Jiang (State Key Laboratory for Novel Software Technology, Nanjing University), Kai Xiong (Zhongguancun Laboratory)

entry.summary: Critically examines whether non-invasive EEG-to-text is feasible in real-world settings, showing that existing models depend on teacher-forcing and fail without it, using a neuropsychology-informed benchmark. It contributes to the debate over whether EEG contains decodable linguistic information.

entry.title: BatchDAG: LLM-Planned Execution Graphs for Scalable Ad-Hoc Analysis Over Enterprise Data

author.name: Anupreet Walia

entry.summary: BatchDAG has an LLM plan a typed directed acyclic graph of operations that a deterministic engine executes with parallelism, targeting cross-entity analytical queries over enterprise datasets. An entity-aware batching optimization reportedly cuts LLM calls up to 47x, addressing context overflow and latency in large-scale analysis.

entry.title: Cross-Dialect Generalization Without Retraining: Benchmarks and Evaluation of Schema-Derived Constrained Decoding for MLIR

author.name: Plawan Kumar Rath

entry.summary: Investigates whether inference-time priors derived mechanically from MLIR dialect specifications can substitute for per-dialect fine-tuning in natural-language-to-MLIR generation. It releases four benchmarks and studies schema-derived constrained decoding for cross-dialect generalization without retraining.

entry.title: Wisdom of LLM Crowds: Aggregation and Contamination in Language Model Ensembles

author.name: Igor Douven

entry.summary: Tests whether the wisdom of crowds emerges when the crowd is composed of LLMs, eliciting probability estimates from fifteen models on binary prediction-market questions and comparing aggregation methods. Learned aggregators outperformed all individual models and classical methods, with logistic regression matching a neural network.

entry.title: PhoenixRepair: Rethinking Repair Strategy Exploration in Software Agents

author.name: Tianyue Jiang, Yanlin Wang, Xin He, Daya Guo, Jiachi Chen, Ming Wen, Ensheng Shi, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: PhoenixRepair is a multi-agent software repair framework that expands the strategy search space by sampling multiple candidate edit locations, optionally augmented with graph structure, and performing iterative reflection and refinement on patches. It addresses insufficient exploration of both edit locations and repair attempts in existing agents.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Dimensional Compression: The Compound Sparsity Frontier of Large Language Models

author.name: Chao Han, Haozhe Hu, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Studies combining static parameter pruning (low-rank plus channel pruning) with dynamic per-token layer skipping to push LLM sparsity further before performance collapses. The claim is that distributing the compression burden across two mechanisms delays degradation past the essential sparsity boundary.

entry.title: HALLMARK: Diagnosing Three Failure Modes in LLM Citation Verifiers

author.name: Patrik Reizinger, Wieland Brendel

entry.summary: Introduces HALLMARK, a benchmark of 2,526 BibTeX entries spanning 14 hallucination types and three difficulty tiers to diagnose failure modes of LLM citation verifiers, and evaluates DOI lookup, frontier LLMs, tool-augmented agents, and a rule-based verifier. Motivated by the growing prevalence of fabricated references in academic writing.

entry.title: Estimating Rare Events in Language Models with Proper Evaluation

author.name: Nikita Y. Parulekar, Anqi Liu

entry.summary: Introduces GA-AMLS, adapting rare-event Monte Carlo multi-level splitting with a gradient-based MCMC kernel to the continuous activation space of language models to estimate probabilities of rare failures too small for random sampling. Addresses zero-estimate collapse and unstable evaluation losses in low-probability estimation.

entry.title: RRPO: Reference-Relative Policy Optimization with Stratified Conditional Rollouts

author.name: Yuxin Xiong, Xunyi Jiang, Rohan Surana, Xintong Li, Sheldon Yu, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Ryan A. Rossi, Jingbo Shang, Tong Yu, Julian McAuley, Junda Wu

entry.summary: Proposes RRPO, generalizing GRPO to non-verifiable reinforcement learning settings by replacing correctness-based advantages with reference-relative contrastive comparisons, using stratified conditional rollouts to build positive and negative anchor sets and training a metric projection head. Aims to extend group-relative optimization where a single correctness signal is unavailable.

entry.title: LatentMT: Machine Translation with Latent Reasoning

author.name: Wei-Rui Chen, Samar M. Magdy, Chiyu Zhang, Wenhui Zhu, Zhipeng Wang, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed

entry.summary: Introduces LatentMT, the first systematic study of latent-reasoning looped language models for machine translation, spending extra recurrent computation in hidden states rather than emitting chain-of-thought tokens. A 2.6B backbone matches models three to five times larger across 32 directions, reaching state of the art on mid- and low-resource languages.

entry.title: Attributes Should Come from Images, Not Class Names: Distribution-Conditioned Attribute Selection for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Gautam Rajendrakumar Gare, Jia Shi, Zhiqiu Lin, Deepak Pathak, John Galeotti, Deva Ramanan

entry.summary: Shows that LLM-generated class descriptors for zero-shot CLIP classification carry little visual evidence, collapsing ImageNet accuracy from 59.5% to 15.5% when the class name is removed, because descriptors are conditioned on the label rather than the images. Proposes selecting attributes from the target image collection instead of from class names.

entry.title: Contraction-Gauge Preconditioning for Quantized Matrix Multiplication

author.name: Piyush Sao, Narasinga Miniskar, Pedro Valero-Lara, Keita Teranishi, Sudip Seal

entry.summary: Derives an exact error identity for low-precision matrix products with both factors quantized and proposes contraction-gauge preconditioning that reshapes factor representations before quantization to reduce product error. It formalizes tradeoffs between error reduction and extra transformed copies.

entry.title: H$^2$SD: Hybrid Hindsight Self-Distillation

author.name: Qiye Cai, Yichuan Ma, Linyang Li, Peiji Li, Yongkang Chen, Qipeng Guo, Yicheng Zou, Tao Gui, Xiaocheng Feng, Bing Qin

entry.summary: Proposes H2SD, hybrid hindsight self-distillation for RL with verifiable rewards, providing denser token-level supervision by conditioning the same model on privileged information without a separate teacher or shared vocabulary. It addresses sparse trajectory-level rewards in LLM reasoning.

entry.title: One Model, Many Graphs: Learning over Attributed Graphs across Heterogeneous Modalities with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiayi Yang, Yifang Chen, Yuanfu Sun, Jiajin Liu, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: Presents OMG-VLM, a unified framework using vision-language models as backbones for attributed graphs spanning textual, visual, or mixed node modalities, enabling one model to handle heterogeneous modality schemas. It targets cross-graph generalization that fixed-schema graph learners lack.

entry.title: CircuitKIT : Circuit Discovery, Evaluation, and Application Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Pratinav Seth, Hem Gosalia, Aditya Kasliwal, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: Introduces CircuitKIT, a source-available library unifying circuit discovery, evaluation, and intervention for mechanistic interpretability through a typed serializable representation, including automated contrastive-prompt handling. It reduces the fragmentation that hinders comparing and applying circuit-analysis methods.

entry.title: ROMS-IMLE: A Minimalist Approach to Competitive Single-Step Generative Modelling

author.name: Chirag Vashist, Ke Li

entry.summary: Presents ROMS-IMLE, a minimalist single-step generative model challenging the belief that gradual noise-to-data transformation is necessary, achieving competitive performance with just a simple objective and model. It questions core assumptions behind diffusion and flow matching.

entry.title: On Incentivized Exploration beyond Bayesianism and Full-Information

author.name: Dimitar Chakarov, Lee Cohen, Nathan Srebro

entry.summary: Extends incentive-compatible exploration beyond the Bayesian full-information setting to agents with unknown external information and without a single common prior, introducing definitions where agents choose any undominated action. It provides a more robust treatment of ties and multiple potential priors.

entry.title: 1-Lipschitz Neural Networks on Hadamard Manifolds

author.name: Davide Murari, Marta Ghirardelli, Ben Adcock, Elena Celledoni, Brynjulf Owren, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb

entry.summary: The authors construct 1-Lipschitz neural network layers that operate on Hadamard manifolds such as hyperbolic space and SPD matrices, using Busemann functions and gradient flows to preserve geometry while ensuring robustness. It extends Lipschitz-constrained robustness techniques beyond Euclidean space.

entry.title: PathReportEval: A Systematic Benchmark for Pathology Report Generation

author.name: Suryakant Singh, Sejuti Majumder, Beatrice Knudsen, Joel Saltz, Prateek Prasanna

entry.summary: PathReportEval introduces a standardized benchmark and evaluation framework for generating pathology reports from whole-slide images, arguing that lexical metrics like BLEU and ROUGE miss clinically consequential errors. It evaluates representative methods across three datasets with pathology-focused metrics.

entry.title: Dual Attention Residuals

author.name: Xingda Yu, Yining Li, Xinzhang Liu, Zhihao Yang, Haowei He, Chao Wang, Yongxiang Li, Shuangyong Song

entry.summary: Dual Attention Residuals introduces reciprocal cross-stream addressing so that multiple residual trajectories in a Transformer can influence each other's depth selection during historical retrieval. It unifies two previously separate axes of residual pathway extension.

entry.title: DeforM: Reasoning-Guided Physics-Aware Video Generation via Spatial-Temporal Masking

author.name: Yunyi Li, Yu Qiao, Yaohui Wang, Xinyuan Chen

entry.summary: DeforM is a reasoning-guided image-to-video framework that uses a VLM-based physical reasoning module to localize physics-critical deformation regions and applies spatial-temporal masking to focus generation there. It targets the difficulty of synthesizing complex deformation dynamics beyond rigid-body motion.

entry.title: MissingBench-Verified: Probing Vision-Language Models' Inability to Detect Missing Object Parts

author.name: Wenqi Marshall Guo, Qingyun Qian, Shiyu Zhou, Guoping Luo, Shan Du

entry.summary: MissingBench-Verified evaluates whether vision-language models can detect that an essential part of an object has been removed, finding consistent high failure rates across ten leading models that persist even when tools contradict the model's perception. It probes a hallucination-adjacent failure rooted in real-world knowledge bias.

entry.title: Wave2Body: Rethinking mmWave Human Pose Estimation as Radar-to-Body Token Translation

author.name: Bo Liang, Chen Gong, Wei Gao, Chenren Xu

entry.summary: Wave2Body reframes mmWave radar human pose estimation as radar-to-body token translation, decoupling radar perception, body structure, and alignment learning through self-supervision to avoid dataset-specific shortcuts. It addresses the under-constrained recovery of full 3D pose from sparse, view-dependent radar reflections.

entry.title: NGPS: GPS-Denied Aerial Geo-Localization and 2.5D Reconstruction via Deep Satellite Image Matching and Multi-Rate Sensor Fusion

author.name: Sanket Sharma

entry.summary: NGPS provides GPS-free absolute positioning for high-altitude UAVs by matching downward images to georeferenced satellite imagery with deep features, fused via a confidence-weighted UKF and an asynchronous multi-rate sensor queue. It also produces 2.5D reconstruction from the fused poses.

entry.title: Integrity-Gated Eco-CACC: Epistemic Admissibility for Cooperative Driving at Signalized Intersections

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud, Moussa Ayyash

entry.summary: This letter proposes an integrity-gated eco-cooperative cruise control framework for signalized intersections that monitors consistency between internal vehicle beliefs and external sensing via a unified integrity metric combining positional innovation, observability loss, and semantic inconsistency. The resulting trust score regulates control authority when sensing degrades.

entry.title: Differential acceleration of alignment-relevant capabilities is a bad bet

author.name: Zephaniah Roe

entry.summary: This post argues against deliberately accelerating alignment-relevant capabilities so AIs can help with safety research, warning that safety and general AI R&D are bottlenecked by the same factors and that speeding one likely speeds both. It also questions whether such acceleration reliably improves handoff and superalignment prospects.

entry.title: Mixing-Free and Signal-Optimal Learning of Gaussian Graphical Models from Glauber Dynamics

author.name: Vignesh Tirukkonda, Gautam Dasarathy

entry.summary: Studies exact recovery of Gaussian graphical model structure from a single trajectory of random-scan Glauber dynamics, proposing two mixing-free algorithms that attain information-theoretically optimal dependence on the minimum edge strength. It avoids inheriting the chain mixing time that can be super-polynomial.

entry.title: Calibrated Selective Fact-Checking via Evidence Chain Evaluation

author.name: Dekun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Evidence Chain Evaluation, a selective fact-checking framework that lets a tool-using verification agent abstain with an uncertain verdict rather than forcing a binary true or false decision. Reported results show high accuracy and coverage on a custom benchmark, addressing overconfident verdicts when evidence is weak.

entry.title: SAAG: Structured Agent Assessment and Grounding

author.name: Ritvik Garimella, Vedant Khandelwal, Anvi Kohli, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: SAAG is a cascaded diagnostic framework that breaks agent tool-calling evaluation into registry conformance, structural completeness, and argument grounding, surfacing distinct failure modes hidden by binary scoring. The stage-specific signals also enable targeted iterative self-repair.

entry.title: When JSON Is Not Enough: Semantic Reliability of Schema-Constrained LLM Ordering Agents

author.name: Yin Li

entry.summary: OrderBench is a deterministic benchmark for restaurant ordering agents that separates syntactic validity, schema validity, item semantics, constraint preservation, and unsafe acceptances. It demonstrates that schema-valid structured output can still be semantically wrong or unsafe.

entry.title: Trajectory-Aware Clinical Risk Prediction via Severity-Grounded Knowledge Graphs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Kyunghoon Jeon, Youmin Ko, Woohwan Jung, Hyunjoon Kim

entry.summary: TRACER is a trajectory-aware clinical risk prediction framework that builds a severity-enriched medical knowledge graph from literature, retrieves severity-weighted patient progression paths, and uses retrieval-augmented generation to capture disease severity and clinical progression. It aims to overcome data sparsity and underused clinical notes in EHR-based prediction.

entry.title: Black-Mamba: Biologically-Inspired Leaky Accumulation for Conceptual Knowledge under Distribution Drift

author.name: Giuseppe Soriano, Nicola Tonellotto, Alberto Gotta

entry.summary: Black-Mamba is a test-time adaptive forecasting architecture that formulates online adaptation as evidence-gated state tracking, updating a dynamic memory only when accumulated surprisal provides sufficient evidence of persistent distribution drift rather than reacting to instantaneous errors. This aims to avoid unnecessary updates from stochastic innovations.

entry.title: OntoBook: Ontology-Grounded Synthetic Textbooks for Medical Encoder Pretraining

author.name: Rian Touchent (ALMAnaCH), \'Eric de la Clergerie (ALMAnaCH)

entry.summary: OntoBook converts medical ontology structure into pretraining signal by taking random walks over ontology graphs, having an LLM rewrite them as fluent textbook prose, and training a French encoder with masked language modeling plus code-pair relation prediction. It reports significant gains on French medical coding benchmarks over MLM-only pretraining.

entry.title: Mi-Memory: A Lifecycle Memory Framework for Personal AI

author.name: Xule Liu, Hanlin Teng, Chao Li, Yanan Ni, Shuo Lu, Audrey Wang, Yijun Liu, Yunfei Wang, Xiaofeng Li, Xian Yi, Yuanfa Li, Kang Zhao, Jian Liang, Yuxuan Chen, Jinyuan Chen, Heng Qu, Kun Shao, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Mi-Memory is a lifecycle memory framework for personal AI spanning phones, cars, homes, and wearables, organized around four roles (Structure, Expansion, Evolution, Deployment) with a shared audit contract for correction, forgetting, and bounded policy evolution. It targets memory as a continuity and governance substrate deployable under latency, privacy, and edge-cloud constraints.

entry.title: Vector-Bench: Can Models Surgically Edit SVG Code?

author.name: Yug Aditi Gupta, Prannay Hebbar

entry.summary: Vector-Bench is a compact benchmark of 40 SVG repair tasks that tests whether models can make a requested edit while leaving everything else unchanged, evaluated at the code level with attribute-aware perceptual tolerances and many protected objects. It exposes the often-missed requirement of not disturbing unrelated elements when editing vector code.

entry.title: CodeRescue: Budget-Calibrated Recovery Routing for Coding Agents

author.name: Qijia He, Jiayi Cheng, Chenqian Le, Rui Wang, Xunmei Liu, Yixian Chen, Jie Mei, Zhihao Wang, Xupeng Chen, Yuhuan Chen, Tao Wang

entry.summary: CodeRescue formulates the post-failure decision for coding agents as recovery routing over heterogeneous actions, deciding whether to spend more cheap compute or escalate to a stronger model after execution feedback. It trains a supervised router from execution rollouts and adds conformal calibration to keep the router usable under changing budgets.

entry.title: FALCON-Discover: Discovering Concentrated False-Confidence Regions for Calibration

author.name: Filippo Cenacchi, Longbing Cao, Runze Yang

entry.summary: FALCON-Discover is a post-hoc, model-agnostic framework that studies false-confidence concentration, the degree to which confident errors occupy compact discoverable regions of prediction space, ranking predictions using confidence, local support, neighborhood agreement, and perturbation stability. Across seven tabular datasets with strong learners, it finds false-confidence concentration recurrent but regime-dependent.

entry.title: Binding Drift in Multi-Step Tool-Augmented Agents

author.name: Rahul Suresh Babu, Shashank Indukuri

entry.summary: Formalizes binding drift in multi-step tool-augmented agents, where an entity that was resolved correctly at step one silently shifts to a wrong entity later, distinguishing it from error propagation. Scores the two on disjoint workflow sets in a controlled testbed to prevent conflation.

entry.title: Decode-Time Grammars: Constrained LLM Generation over a Refinement Order of Grammar Fragments

author.name: Shuoming Zhang, Ruiyuan Xu, Haofeng Li, Qiuchu Yu, Yangyu Zhang, Chunwei Xia, Xiaobing Feng, Chenxi Wang, Huimin Cui, Jiacheng Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces decode-time grammars, where grammar fragments are instantiated during generation from the live runtime environment so that constrained decoding cannot emit references invalid in the current context, such as undeclared buffers or missing schema columns. Targets low-resource programming surfaces like DSLs, custom APIs, and CLIs.

entry.title: Structured Output Collapses Answer Diversity Across 44 Language Models

author.name: Tapan Parikh

entry.summary: Shows that simply requesting JSON-formatted replies, without schema enforcement or constrained decoding, sharply collapses answer diversity across 44 language models on wide-answer-space prompts, raising the modal answer share and lowering surprisal. The effect is progressive, with the most distinctive models moving most toward the mode.

entry.title: Operational Proto-Introspection in Looped Language Models: Process-Quality Taps, Executable Branching, and the Readout-Control Boundary

author.name: Jan Kirin

entry.summary: Tests whether a frozen 2.6B looped transformer can read the quality of its ongoing computation, showing a pre-answer probe that excludes the answer region still predicts eventual GSM8K success above shortcut baselines. Also finds low-capacity taps read role-specialized properties like branch survival and content ranking, probing a readout-control boundary.

entry.title: The Story Shapes the Agent: Narrative Priors in LLM Behavior

author.name: Yixuan Wang, James Lester, Shashank Srivastava

entry.summary: Uses structurally isomorphic investigation games (disease, IT, murder mystery) that share action space and structure but differ only in narrative to isolate narrative priors in LLM agent behavior. Across 1,890 sessions, three models, and ten personas, narrative framing explains far more behavioral variance than assigned persona.

entry.title: Broken Gates: Re-evaluating Web Bot Defenses in the Age of LLM Agents

author.name: Behzad Ousat, Nikita Turkmen, Lalchandra Rampersaud, Dillan Bailey, Amin Kharraz

entry.summary: Systematically measures the resilience of web bot-management defenses against both commercial CAPTCHA-solving services and LLM-based browser agents that autonomously navigate and reason about pages. Spans interactive challenge-based and non-interactive trust-based defenses across seven systems.

entry.title: Conditioned Direct Feedback Alignment via Activity and Error Geometry

author.name: Houman Safaai, Varun Reddy, Bernardo L. Sabatini

entry.summary: Analyzes a failure mode in direct feedback alignment where anisotropy in either the presynaptic activity or local error factor degrades learning, and proposes conditioning strategies that recover substantial accuracy. It advances biologically plausible alternatives to backpropagation.

entry.title: PertReason: A Knowledge-Grounded Benchmark and Framework for Cell-State-Conditioned Mechanistic Reasoning of Perturbation Effects

author.name: Dongkwan Kim, Yiming Gao, Yining Yang, Yang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces PertReason and PertReasonQA, a knowledge-grounded benchmark testing whether models produce mechanistically faithful, cell-state-conditioned explanations of perturbation effects while remaining robust to distribution shifts. It emphasizes separating correct predictions from correct reasons.

entry.title: Adopting Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Molecular Generation

author.name: Mingxuan Ouyang, Hao Lan, Wanyu Lin

entry.summary: Proposes LLMol, a reinforcement learning framework incorporating verifiable rewards to steer LLM-based molecular generation toward target properties via goal-conditioned sequence prediction. It addresses the lack of direct optimization in prior molecular generation methods.

entry.title: Recti-Q: Feature-Space Rectification for Out-of-Distribution-Robust Quantized Perception in Edge Robotics

author.name: Hamidreza Yaghoubi Araghi, Parastoo Pilevar, Ming C. Lin

entry.summary: Identifies a quantization-induced robustness gap where post-training-quantized vision backbones lose reliability under distribution shifts despite negligible clean-accuracy loss, and proposes Recti-Q, a lightweight feature-space rectification framework. It targets robust quantized perception for edge robotics.

entry.title: PLAID-PRF: Pseudo-Relevance Feedback with Centroid-like Tokens in PLAID

author.name: Xiao Wang, Sean MacAvaney, Craig Macdonald

entry.summary: PLAID-PRF performs pseudo-relevance feedback over the PLAID multi-vector retrieval index by reusing internal centroid vectors as pseudo-tokens to reformulate ColBERT query vectors. It adds feedback-based query expansion while keeping computational costs low.

entry.title: Physics Closure Matters for Machine Olfaction: A Maxwell--Stefan Graph Solver for Identifiable Dynamic Gas Unmixing

author.name: Yue Shi, Liangxiu Han, Xin Zhang, Tam Sobeih

entry.summary: This paper formulates machine olfaction gas unmixing as a physics-constrained inverse problem governed by Maxwell-Stefan transport PDEs, adsorption ODEs, and sensor transduction, and proposes a graph solver addressing physics closure misspecification. It emphasizes physically closed inference over merely fitting sensor traces.

entry.title: Seeing Before Generating: Object Perception Enhances Single-View 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Y Huynh, Duc Thanh Nguyen, Mohamed Abdelrazek

entry.summary: This paper shows that learned object perception, via semantic and geometric signals from pretrained perception models, can significantly improve single-view 3D object reconstruction in a plug-and-play, model-agnostic manner. It draws on the human-vision link between perceiving and reconstructing objects.

entry.title: Fluid-SDF: Ultra-Lightweight and Editable Implicit Shape Representation via Differentiable Primitives

author.name: Pradyumna Sripada, Chinmay Nadgir, Ksheer Agrawal, Krishna Kanth Kodanganti

entry.summary: Fluid-SDF is a differentiable constructive solid geometry framework that represents 2D shapes with explicit geometric primitives blended by a smooth minimum, achieving comparable or better IoU using under 100 parameters. It offers editability and noise robustness that black-box implicit neural representations lack.

entry.title: Continual Video-MLLM Adaptation over Evolving Domains

author.name: Rui Cheng, Meixing Shi, Yuxiang Cai, Jingcai Guo, Jianwei Yin, Zhi Chen

entry.summary: This work proposes Distribution-Aware Expert Routing for continually adapting video multimodal LLMs to sequentially evolving domains, maintaining domain-isolated lightweight experts to avoid cross-domain interference and catastrophic forgetting. It targets the underexplored continual-learning setting for video MLLMs.

entry.title: Posterior Samplings are Missing Modalities Generators for Medical Image Translation

author.name: Jonghun Kim

entry.summary: This work formulates missing-modality MRI generation as a linear inverse problem under a joint distribution and solves it via posterior sampling with a flow-matching model, learning a joint prior over the complete modality set. This lets a single model reconstruct arbitrary missing modalities without retraining per source-target pair.

entry.title: UVFaceFusion: Fast Multi-view Topologically Consistent Face Reconstruction in the Wild via UV-space Neural Fusion

author.name: Xin Ming, Yuxuan Han, Junhai Yong, Feng Xu

entry.summary: UVFaceFusion is a feed-forward framework for multi-view, fixed-topology face reconstruction from everyday images that replaces heuristic topological optimization with learnable neural fusion in canonical UV space. It combines dense point maps and facial UV correspondences via a mask-aware fusion network.

entry.title: ZeroSplat: Generalized Referring Segmentation in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiayu Ding, Meilu Song, Xiaoyi Zhang, Hongbo Jin, Yichen Jin, Xiangtian Si

entry.summary: ZeroSplat introduces the generalized referring 3D Gaussian Splatting segmentation task, requiring segmentation of zero, one, or many targets, and builds two benchmarks plus a method with intrinsic 3D point-level understanding. It addresses the single-target limitation of prior referring 3DGS methods.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary Gaze Object Prediction: Benchmark and Method

author.name: Binglu Wang, Sensen Niu, Ying Chen, Guangyu Guo

entry.summary: This paper introduces the DiSG benchmark with 86 in-the-wild categories to enable open-vocabulary gaze object prediction, moving beyond closed-vocabulary, scene-specific evaluation. It proposes a text-driven object discovery framework to localize gaze targets including unseen categories.

entry.title: Think Sparse, Predict Dense: Continuous Thought Machines for Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Zekai Shi

entry.summary: This paper extends Continuous Thought Machines, which have an internal temporal thinking dimension, to dense visual prediction for image super-resolution by producing per-window thought summaries and transforming them into dense queries via a low-rank compact-to-dense mechanism. It adapts a sequential thinking mechanism to spatially detailed outputs.

entry.title: TAP-RAG: Task-Aware Policy Control for Long-Document Multimodal Question Answering

author.name: Zhong Ji, Keqi Jin, Yan Zhang, Jiasheng Li

entry.summary: TAP-RAG is a task-aware, policy-controlled retrieval-augmented framework for long-document multimodal question answering that predicts a task prior and routes queries through query-guided flow diffusion and visual enhancement executors. It replaces query-agnostic evidence strategies with per-query adaptive evidence behavior.

entry.title: Motion Primitive Discovery in a Humanoid Robot via Self-Organising Maps for Phase Recognition

author.name: Radovan Gregor, Igor Farka\v{s}

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-level architecture inspired by the mirror neuron system for motor primitive discovery and online phase recognition on the NICO humanoid, using self-organizing maps for arm and hand kinematics and an echo state network for phase recognition. It links action recognition to social cognition and human-robot interaction.

entry.title: The Twist Decomposition of Serial Robots Under Lower-Mobility Tasks

author.name: Luc Baron (IICiMed), Damien Chablat (LS2N - \'equipe RoMas, LS2N)

entry.summary: This paper introduces a twist decomposition framework for serial manipulators performing lower-mobility tasks, separating the end-effector twist into task and redundant components with geometrically defined projectors rather than Jacobian null-space projections. It yields a compact inverse kinematics scheme handling both manipulator and task redundancy.

entry.title: Design and stability analysis of an underactuated hand with passively rotating fingers

author.name: L\'eonie Plancoulaine (LS2N, LS2N - \'equipe RoMas), Sylvain Gu\'egan (LGCGM), Franck Plestan (ECN, LS2N), Damien Chablat (LS2N, LS2N - \'equipe RoMas)

entry.summary: This paper presents an underactuated robotic finger with a base revolute joint enabling passive spatial rotation for both cylindrical and spherical grasping, using only two phalanges to simplify kinematics. It introduces contact-force-based stability criteria and a differential mechanism to distribute a single actuation torque.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Meta-Policies for Temporal Knowledge-Graph Memory under Partial Observability

author.name: Taewoon Kim, Vincent Fran\c{c}ois-Lavet, Michael Cochez

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic meta-policy that learns which symbolic memory heuristic to apply at each decision point while keeping execution symbolic, using temporal knowledge-graph memory represented as RDF triples in a RoomKG environment. The controller supports question answering, exploration, and forgetting under partial observability.

entry.title: One Rewrite to Fix Them All? Type-Aware Repair Allocation for Text-to-Image Prompt Optimization

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Xiaoyu Ma, Ye Chen, Shuguang Cui, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Reframes text-to-image prompt optimization as atomic repair allocation, routing each failed proposition (wrong counts, swapped attributes, ambiguous relations, illegible text) to a type-conditioned repair operator before compiling constraints into one executable prompt. This targets the mismatch between uniform prompt expansion and heterogeneous failure types.

entry.title: Distribution-First Population Simulation: Collapse, Calibration, and Recall in Non-WEIRD LLM Persona Modeling

author.name: Gurkan Ozkan

entry.summary: Shows that running each survey respondent as an independent LLM persona fails to reproduce real population response distributions, collapsing onto modal defaults, using World Values Survey microdata from a non-WEIRD (Turkey-first) setting. Proposes a distribution-first corrective measured with a deterministic verifier.

entry.title: Federated Lightweight Fine-Tuning

author.name: Radhakrishna Achanta, Will Reed

entry.summary: Proposes federated fine-tuning through mapping networks that generate weights from a small trainable latent via a frozen affine projection, so averaging latents exactly averages generated weights, giving a low-bandwidth channel. Adds a seed-regenerable low-rank factorization and an additive delta formulation to slash generator memory.

entry.title: An Analysis of Residual-Stream Geometry Across Transformer Depth

author.name: Sunit Bhattacharya, Ravi Shankar Kolli

entry.summary: Provides a geometric analysis of transformer residual streams by measuring relative displacement between layers and using orthogonal Procrustes to split each transition into rigid rotation and non-rigid residual. Finds reproducible depth regularities across six instruction-tuned models on code and translation.

entry.title: AutoIndex: Learning Representation Programs for Retrieval

author.name: Sam O'Nuallain, Nithya Rajkumar, Ramya Narayanasamy, Hanna Jiang, Shreyas Chaudhari, Andrew Drozdov

entry.summary: Presents AutoIndex, which learns representation programs, executable transformations that slice, enrich, normalize, or reorganize documents before indexing, via validation-guided program search where agents diagnose failures and synthesize updates. Evaluated on the CRUMB heterogeneous retrieval benchmark with BM25 held fixed.

entry.title: Spaghetti Architect: A Contamination-Resistant, By-Construction-Labelled, Multi-Language Code Dataset Generator

author.name: Yuxiang Ji

entry.summary: Introduces Spaghetti Architect, a tool that mints correct-by-construction, contamination-resistant multi-language code datasets from a clean intermediate representation via an anti-optimization transpiler with tunable messiness. It provides known-optimal references absent from mined code corpora.

entry.title: Decafs: Disentangled Conditional adversarial Flows

author.name: Anirudh jain, Sakshi Varshney, Samuel Kaski, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: Proposes Decafs, a conditional generative model using Lie-group structure to disentangle a latent space aligned with a flow model via adversarial loss, enabling interpretable controlled generation without expanding flow dimensionality. It targets the entanglement problem in flow-based models.

entry.title: HindsightBench: A Black-Box Behavioral Audit Protocol for Parametric Hindsight in Time-Indexed LLM Decision Tasks

author.name: Haozhe Jia

entry.summary: Presents HindsightBench, a black-box audit protocol that cheaply profiles how much LLMs leak parametric knowledge of realized outcomes into time-indexed financial decision tasks, using date-manipulation arms and per-model metrics. It offers practitioners a probe-level way to detect lookahead bias.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Super-Resolution of Atmospheric Data

author.name: Chang Xu, Gencer Sumbul, Hugo Porta, Manon B\'echaz, Sebastian Schemm, Devis Tuia

entry.summary: Constrains super-resolution models of atmospheric data with physical laws to ensure downscaled fields remain physically consistent, improving trustworthiness for climate applications. It addresses whether ML-super-resolved atmospheric outputs still satisfy governing physics.

entry.title: Breaking Feedback-Blindness: Utility-Augmented Transformer for Sequential Decision Making

author.name: Yuyang Shen, Shan Dai, Daimin Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes feedback-blind retrieval in transformer decision models, proving observation-only attention cannot distinguish histories with different action-reward outcomes, and proposes the Utility-Augmented Transformer to remedy it. It targets rapid adaptation in non-stationary, partially observable settings.

entry.title: Real-time optimal control with shallow recurrent decoder networks

author.name: Matteo Tomasetto, Francesco Braghin, J. Nathan Kutz, Andrea Manzoni

entry.summary: Uses shallow recurrent decoder-based reduced-order modeling to synthesize real-time closed-loop controllers for high-dimensional parametric dynamics from limited sensor readings, learning from a few expert-provided optimal examples. It enables fast adaptive control across scenarios.

entry.title: Disentangling Forced and Internal Climate Variability in Single Realizations using Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control

author.name: Nathan Mankovich, Andrei Gavrilov, Gustau Camps-Valls

entry.summary: Shows a single climate realization can be decomposed into forced and internal variability components using dynamic mode decomposition with control, treating external forcing as a dynamical driver grounded in pullback attractor theory. It advances detection and attribution without requiring large ensembles.

entry.title: Computational models of pragmatic reasoning with flexible generation of meaning and expression alternatives

author.name: Polina Tsvilodub, Fausto Carcassi, Michael Franke

entry.summary: The authors propose SAGE, a framework combining cognitive model transparency with language model generation to flexibly produce the alternative meanings and expressions needed for pragmatic reasoning. It addresses the common problem of manually specifying alternative sets in pragmatics models.

entry.title: RF-Agent: A Practical Framework for Building Language Agents for RFIC Design

author.name: Yueqi Xing, Houbo He, Jolie Wang, Erin Ni, Shikai Wang, Qiufeng Li, Weidong Cao, Taiyun Chi

entry.summary: RF-Agent builds a language agent for radio-frequency integrated circuit design by distilling knowledge from seven RF textbooks into an 11,000-sample reasoning dataset with a multiple-choice benchmark. It compares supervised fine-tuning against retrieval-augmented generation strategies for this underserved domain.

entry.title: Disentangling Curriculum Learning in NLP: Towards a Unifying Taxonomy

author.name: Vanessa Toborek, Florian Seiffarth, Sebastian M\"uller, Tam\'as Horv\'ath

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fine-grained taxonomy for curriculum learning in NLP that separates difficulty evaluation from training scheduling and offers the first formalization of schedulers in terms of expected training contribution. It aims to explain why the field lacks principled guidance on choosing difficulty functions.

entry.title: Confidence-Gated Vision-Only Heading Alignment for UAV-UGV Cooperative Systems

author.name: Reza Ahmari, Vahid Hemmati, Parham Kebria, Olusola Odeyomi, Kaushik Roy, Abdollah Homaifar

entry.summary: This paper studies when a fixed vision-based heading predictor should be trusted to issue direct control commands in UAV-UGV cooperation, using bounding-box area and short-window heading variation as interpretable reliability proxies. It compares a freeze-hold policy with a bounded-blend fallback during low-confidence periods.

entry.title: Two-Stage Extrinsic Calibration of a Static Line-Scanning Lidar with a Rotary Platform

author.name: Vikram Shree, Hike Danakian, Long Nguyen, Rajanish Gokidi, Patrick Nercessian

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage extrinsic calibration method to identify the rotation axis of a rotary platform relative to a static line-scanning lidar so that accurate 3D point clouds of scanned objects can be reconstructed. It targets precise industrial scanning and inspection.

entry.title: Pose-Parameterized Motion Planning and CBF-QP Self-Collision Filtering for a Long-Reach Drilling Boom

author.name: Mehdi Heydari Shahna, Tuomo Kivel\"a, Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: This paper integrates pose-parameterized motion planning with a capsule-based control barrier function quadratic program for self-collision-free motion of a long-reach drilling boom, using offline detour planning and online joint-velocity filtering. It moves the Sandvik SB60 from operator supervision toward autonomy without target-specific retuning.

entry.title: Some cautionary tales about Bayesian predictive inference

author.name: Emanuela Dreassi, Fabrizio Leisen, Luca Pratelli, Pietro Rigo

entry.summary: This short paper discusses two common misunderstandings in Bayesian predictive inference, concerning the data-generating mechanism and overestimation of asymptotic exchangeability, illustrating their consequences with examples. It serves as a cautionary conceptual note.

entry.title: Epistemics and Coordination: It’s complicated!

author.name: Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: This post examines AI for epistemics and coordination as a funding and strategy area, arguing the best version could be a legitimate theory of victory but that existing plans are shallow and prone to backfiring, especially when scaling with inference. It cautions that better-epistemics interventions can be more hostile and distrusted than proponents expect.

entry.title: Structured Synthetic Reasoning Data for Arithmetic Fine-Tuning of Small Language Models

author.name: Jake O'Grady, Effirul Ramlan

entry.summary: Examines whether structured synthetic reasoning data improves multi-step arithmetic in small language models under consumer-hardware constraints, generating a corpus from GSM8K variants using a stronger model. LoRA fine-tuning of small Qwen3 models yielded substantial GSM8K accuracy gains.

entry.title: Using LLMs for Explainable, Data-Driven Insight Generation from Time Series

author.name: Ria Mundhra, Gustavo Sato dos Santos, Michael Benedikt

entry.summary: Proposes a domain-agnostic framework for generating grounded natural-language explanations of time-series forecasts, extracting structured explanatory factors from analyst-written explanations and conditioning generation on evidence to reduce hallucination. It also includes scalable evaluation for readability, consistency, and persuasiveness.

entry.title: Semantic Primes as Explanans for Emotion in Large Language Models

author.name: Frank Xing

entry.summary: Investigates whether the semantic primes of the Natural Semantic Metalanguage can serve as more primitive, non-circular internal variables explaining emotion in LLMs, testing four instruction-tuned models. It finds the primes are recoverable internal elements that provide a candidate explanatory basis for emotion representations.

entry.title: SkillSight: Seeing Through Shared Descriptions for Accurate Skill Retrieval

author.name: Jinying Xiao, Bin Ji, Shasha Li, Xiaodong Liu, Ma Jun, Jiacheng Jie, Chao Wang, Nyima Tashi, Jie Yu

entry.summary: SkillSight is a training-free retrieval framework for LLM-agent skill libraries that calibrates the shared descriptive background across skill descriptions, which otherwise inflates dense relevance scores and obscures distinguishing signals. It improves accurate skill retrieval as libraries grow large.

entry.title: Supra Cognitive Modes: A Routed Architecture for Agent Memory

author.name: Joshua Tobkin, David Yang

entry.summary: Supra Cognitive Modes is an agent-memory architecture that maps per-query modes (factual lookup, relation-chain reasoning, broad synthesis) to different retrieval and synthesis pipelines over one shared ingest substrate combining embeddings, extracted triples, and fact-version metadata. A frozen classifier and runtime gates dispatch queries among fused lexical/dense lookup, multi-hop handling, and long-form synthesis.

entry.title: OpenRTAG: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Robust Text-Attributed Graph Learning under Data Quality Degradation

author.name: Yuze Dai, Zhihan Zhang, Yan Zhao, Ruoyu Wu, Xunkai Li, Zekai Chen, Qiangqiang Dai, Hongchao Qin, Ronghua Li

entry.summary: OpenRTAG is a robustness benchmark for text-attributed graph learning that organizes text, structure, and label quality issues into nine representative degradation scenarios covering sparsity, noise, and imbalance. It consolidates fragmented evidence to systematically assess how data-quality degradation affects TAG models.

entry.title: MechAInistic: An LLM-guided Multi-Agent System for Reasoning over Genome-Scale Constraint-Based Metabolic Models

author.name: Josh Loecker, Narayna Puraja, William Bryan, Bhanwar Lal Puniya, Ahmed Abdeen Hamed, Tom\'a\v{s} Helikar

entry.summary: MechAInistic is an LLM-guided multi-agent system organized around an Architect-Reviewer pattern that converts natural-language biological questions into executable, model-grounded workflows over genome-scale constraint-based metabolic models. It supports tasks like pathway comparison, perturbation analysis, and drug-target exploration with literature-grounded reports.

entry.title: Assistant or Actor? Student Trust, Control, and Delegation Regret When Using a General-Purpose AI Agent

author.name: Shiva Pochampally, Shengwei An, Yan Chen

entry.summary: A controlled study of 20 students using a general-purpose AI agent for daily tasks introduces the concept of delegation regret, where users regret not that the agent erred but that it acted beyond what they would have authorized. It measures trust, perceived control, transparency, and supervision burden across tasks varying in privacy, stakes, and reversibility.

entry.title: Multi-layer MIMO Relay as Deep Physical Neural Networks: Power Amplifiers as Activation Functions

author.name: Meng Hua, Itsik Bergel, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: Frames a multi-hop MIMO relay network as a deep physical neural network where each relay applies a trainable complex linear gain and the amplifier nonlinearity acts as an activation function, trained end-to-end over the air. Develops transceiver designs for different channel-state-information scenarios.

entry.title: Relay-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Multi-Domain Reasoning Chains

author.name: Liam Swayne

entry.summary: Introduces Relay-Bench, a text-only benchmark of composite multi-domain problems chaining subproblems across visual reasoning, coding, math, information extraction, and more, with added prompt encoding and context bloat. Reports the leading model scoring 43.3%, indicating the benchmark remains unsaturated.

entry.title: ChainMark: Model-Free LLM Watermarking with Closed-Form Calibration

author.name: Chengheng Li-Chen, Kyuhee Kim

entry.summary: Proposes ChainMark, an active LLM watermark that partitions the vocabulary into states via keyed SHA-256 and forces Markov transitions on a fraction of positions, detectable in linear hash operations without model access. Derives closed-form calibration for state count and a universal robustness threshold.

entry.title: Planning as Emergent Behavior in Reinforcement Learning with Relational Hidden States

author.name: Armin Sommer

entry.summary: Investigates when planning emerges from model-free reinforcement learning, arguing that a network of relational hidden states, each anchored to an environment state and exchanging messages along learned relations, is the deciding architectural factor. Presents evidence that hidden-state structure, not the objective, enables emergent planning.

entry.title: KALE: Kernel Alignment with Loss Equilibration for Stable CLIP-DINOv2 Alignment at Web Scale

author.name: Micha{\l} Paw{\l}owicz

entry.summary: Introduces KALE, a loss-equilibration controller that adaptively rescales the kernel-alignment weight when distilling CLIP toward a DINOv2-style vision teacher at noisy web scale, where fixed weights become effectively inert. It restores alignment signal without per-dataset tuning.

entry.title: In-Context Time Series Classification with Random Convolutional Features

author.name: Joscha C\"uppers, Jilles Vreeken

entry.summary: Proposes MASHT, pairing random convolutional time-series features (MultiRocket and Hydra) with a pretrained tabular foundation model used in-context, testing whether such models better exploit rich random features than linear classifiers. It bridges random-feature transforms and tabular foundation models for time-series classification.

entry.title: Scalable Policy Optimization for Networked Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Continuous State-Action Spaces

author.name: Dongming Wang, Pengcheng Dai, Wenwu Yu, Wei Ren

entry.summary: Develops the Continuous Distributed Coupled Policy Gradient algorithm for cooperative networked MDPs with continuous states and actions, using localized actors and spectral random-feature LSTD critics with a well-posed truncated Bellman theory. It provides scalability analysis for large agent networks.

entry.title: End-to-end Conditional Diffusion for Realistic and Controllable Visual Traffic Scenario Generation

author.name: Jingzheng Li, Yufei Ge, Zhijun Chen, Qianren Mao, Zizhe Wang, Binhang Qi, Bing Li, Keyu Chen, Baochang Zhang, Xianglong Liu, Philip S Yu

entry.summary: Presents E2E-CDiff, an end-to-end conditional diffusion framework that jointly denoises future motion states and executable low-level controls for route-interacting vehicles conditioned on front-view observations, aiming to balance realism and controllability in traffic scenario generation. It targets evaluation of autonomous driving under rare safety-critical interactions.

entry.title: Algebraic Signatures for Structural Learning in Probability Tensors

author.name: Akihiro Maeda, Shohei Hidaka, Satoshi Aoki

entry.summary: Uses algebraic statistics to identify probabilistic structure from vanishing binomials in empirical probability tensors, treating a toric model's vanishing binomials as an algebraic signature matched without parameter estimation. It restricts to a tractable Kronecker-stack class to make signatures enumerable.

entry.title: Enhanced NQS via Annealed Gradient Descent

author.name: Shiwei Zhou, Yiming Huang, Xiao Yuan, Xiaoxia Cai

entry.summary: Identifies a finite-sample subspace-trapping instability in neural quantum state optimization where important configurations get underestimated and starved of gradient feedback, and introduces annealed gradient descent to counteract it. It improves accuracy limited by stochastic optimization rather than representational capacity.

entry.title: Boundary-Adapted PINNs for Elliptic Dirichlet Problems: $H^2(\Omega)$ A Priori Error Bounds with Application to Mean Escape Time Computation

author.name: Nathanael Tepakbong, Jun Fan, Xiang Zhou, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: Derives a priori H2 error bounds for boundary-enforced physics-informed neural networks solving elliptic Dirichlet problems, showing that exact boundary enforcement alone is insufficient and making explicit the dependence on the distance-to-boundary function, with application to mean escape time computation. It analyzes ReQU and tanh networks.

entry.title: ECoNGS: Efficient Compressive Neural Gaussian Splats for Volume Visualization

author.name: Kaiyuan Tang, Chaoli Wang

entry.summary: ECoNGS is a neural Gaussian splatting framework for volume visualization that uses lightweight networks to predict implicit editable Gaussian splats from anchor points, reducing redundancy across scenes. It combines the compactness of implicit representations with high-quality primitive-based rendering.

entry.title: SkyEV: RGB-Event UAV detection and tracking dataset and baseline

author.name: Jakub Mandula, Sebastian Heusinger, Julian Moosmann, Christian Vogt, Michele Magno

entry.summary: SkyEV is an open-source RGB-event dataset for UAV detection and tracking that captures realistic counter-UAV factors like camera ego-motion, extremely small targets, and diverse lenses with synchronized uncompressed streams. It addresses shortcomings of prior datasets that introduce compression artifacts and unrealistic conditions.

entry.title: Cross-Modal UAV Object Tracking: State-Aware Representation Learning and A Unified Benchmark

author.name: Yun Xiao, Zhihong Hong, Jiandong Jin, Chenglong Li, Jin Tang, Amir Hussain

entry.summary: This paper introduces SARLA, a state-aware representation learning approach for cross-modal UAV object tracking that handles the appearance changes and spatial shifts caused by switching between visible and thermal-infrared sensors. It also provides a unified benchmark for this modality-switching scenario.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware 3D Geometric Injection for Universal Person Re-identification

author.name: Bohan Su, Jiashuo Wang, Fangyi Liu, Mang Ye

entry.summary: UniGeo is a universal person re-identification framework that injects monocular 3D geometric priors while using a consistency-aware reliability gate and dual-stream residual fusion to avoid negative transfer from noisy depth estimates under degradation. It targets occlusion, clothing changes, and cross-modality shifts in one model.

entry.title: DobicVLM: Aligning Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Clinically-Grounded Programmatic Rewards via Group Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Thanni Adewuyi, Angelica Obayi, Andem Aniekan, Samuel Okoko, Angel Ezendu, Ephraim Usani, Ademide Animasaun, Philip Chibundu, Christian Maurice, Mary Donald Essien, Oluwaseun Odunsi, Oluwasegun Oguntuase, Abiodun Adereni

entry.summary: DobicVLM combines supervised fine-tuning of MedGemma-4B with Group Relative Policy Optimization using interpretable, rule-based clinical rewards for structural, anatomical, semantic, and length constraints in chest X-ray report generation. It enforces clinical standards without neural reward models on a small private dataset.

entry.title: Mitigating Modality and Language-Style Gaps for Zero-Shot Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Jihyun Lee, Cheol-Ho Cho, Woojin Jun, Woojin Jeong, Jae-Pil Heo

entry.summary: This paper proposes self-similarity-based moment proposal and scoring for zero-shot video moment retrieval, deriving proposals from intrinsic video content rather than query-to-video similarity to avoid modality and language-style gaps. It aims for more robust span generation without large annotated datasets.

entry.title: Gaze-DETR: Top-Down Guidance Through Priority Maps for Infrared Weak-Small UAV Detection with DETR

author.name: Nian Liu, Yuxin Yang, Shubo Lin, Sikui Zhang, Liang Li, Boyu Cai, Yizheng Wang, Weiming Hu, Jin Gao

entry.summary: Gaze-DETR is a bio-inspired infrared small-target UAV detector that learns an internal spatial priority map before localization, mimicking task-driven visual search to prioritize candidate regions and preserve weak-target evidence. It addresses the lack of explicit guidance in bounding-box-only supervision for tiny low-contrast targets.

entry.title: Towards chemistries in dynamical systems

author.name: Martin Biehl, Nathaniel Virgo

entry.summary: This exploratory theoretical paper proposes a way to describe arbitrary dynamical systems in chemistry-like terms of species, places, and reactions, requiring three modeling choices to align with state updates. It aims to generalize a chemical description language beyond molecules.

entry.title: From Agent Failure Paths to Quantified Residual Risk: A Compositional Framework for Resilient Agentic AI

author.name: Hassan Karim, Sai Sitharaman, Deepti Gupta, Danda B. Rawat

entry.summary: Presents CPSAINT, a seven-layer integrity decomposition for agentic systems, paired with FRIESA-K, a residual-risk functional that maps failure paths to quantified risk using an absorbing Markov model. The goal is to bridge failure-mechanism descriptions and transferable residual-risk estimates for resilient agentic AI.

entry.title: Gradient-Energy Guided Block-Wise Perturbations for Sharpness-Aware Minimization

author.name: Zhen Huang, Jiaxin Deng, Junbiao Pang

entry.summary: Proposes GEAR-SAM, which allocates the sharpness-aware minimization perturbation budget across parameter blocks using an EMA of squared block gradients as a lightweight curvature signal instead of noisy instantaneous norms. Preserves the global SAM radius without Hessian-vector products.

entry.title: Quantum Cryptanalysis on IBM Quantum Hardware: Extending Even--Mansour Period Recovery from $N=4$ to $N=10$

author.name: Taebong Kim, Youngsik Hong, Minsik Kim, Sunyoung Choi, Jaewon Jang, Junghoon Shin, Minseo Kim

entry.summary: Reports quantum cryptanalysis on real IBM quantum hardware, using Simon's algorithm to recover the hidden period of the Even-Mansour cipher up to security parameter N=10, beyond the previous N=4 hardware record, and Feistel periods at small block sizes. Includes a benchmark of five quantum attacks across cipher paradigms.

entry.title: CANDOR: Chance-Calibrated Discordance in Frozen Foundation Encoders

author.name: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: Introduces CANDOR, a chance-calibrated discordance measure for frozen foundation encoders using equal-size, label-swap-symmetric banks so its chance level sits at exactly one half, correcting prevalence bias in nearest-neighbor discordance. Across 22 encoders, 20 datasets, and 605k images it reverses prior conclusions, finding encoders are weak rather than blind.

entry.title: Trusted Credentials, Untrusted Behavior: Benchmarking LLM-Agent Security in High-Performance Computing

author.name: Jie Li

entry.summary: Benchmarks LLM-agent security in high-performance computing, where agents act under a user's credentials and inherit their access, exposing a hijacked authorized agent problem in which adversarial instructions in logs, tool descriptions, or shared files redirect the agent while every command remains authenticated. Highlights a failure mode that account-level controls miss.

entry.title: Now We Know? A Systematic Comparison of TerraMind and THOR

author.name: Frederick Schindlegger, Kenzo Bounegta, Eva Gmelich Meijling, Johannes Jakubik, Arnt-B{\o}rre Salberg, Theodor Forgaard, Nicolas Longepe, Valerio Marsocci

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled comparison of two ESA-developed geospatial foundation models, THOR (compute-adaptive, variable patch sizes, native-resolution Sentinel fusion) and TerraMind (multimodal generative with any-to-any cross-modal generation), to disentangle how much of performance gaps comes from architecture versus decoder capacity versus use-case artifacts. Aims to move beyond aggregate leaderboard rankings.

entry.title: CPInj: Uncovering Prompt Injection Risks in Textual Collaborative Prompt Optimization

author.name: Xinting Liao, Behnoosh Zamanlooy, Masoumeh Shafieinejad, David B. Emerson, Ruinan Jin, Deval Pandya, Xiaoxiao Li

entry.summary: Introduces CPInj, uncovering prompt-injection risks in textual collaborative prompt optimization where multiple clients jointly improve prompts, showing malicious instructions can be injected locally and propagate through server-side aggregation. Notes the attack is harder because it must survive aggregation, persist through benign optimization, and evade detection.

entry.title: QScheduler: Adaptive Gradient Sampling for Zeroth-Order On-Device Training on INT8 NPUs

author.name: Victor Felipe Domingues Do Amaral (GeePs), Pierre Demaj (GeePs), Erwan Libessart (GeePs), Laurent Folliot (GeePs), Anthony Kolar (GeePs), Philippe B\'enab\`es (GeePs)

entry.summary: Introduces QScheduler, an adaptive algorithm that adjusts the number of gradient samples for zeroth-order on-device learning based on training progress, and demonstrates INT8 quantized on-device training on a microcontroller NPU. It reduces costly hyperparameter search for edge training.

entry.title: From a Multilingual Streaming ASR Backbone to Kenyan-Language Systems: Data-Centric Adaptation of Nemotron 3.5 for Kikuyu, Dholuo, and Kalenjin

author.name: Mark Gatere

entry.summary: This engineering study adapts NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 streaming ASR to three Kenyan languages (Kikuyu, Dholuo, Kalenjin) through careful data auditing, Unicode normalization, and full-parameter fine-tuning. It emphasizes deployment-realistic streaming evaluation for low-resource African languages.

entry.title: Selection Shapes the Boundary: A Preregistered Replication of Monotonicity and Label Agreement in Unselected NLI Populations

author.name: Haram Choi

entry.summary: This preregistered replication tests whether non-upward monotonicity operators lower label agreement in natural language inference, using unselected SNLI and MultiNLI development sets rather than disagreement-selected data. The registered prediction fails, suggesting the original effect stemmed from selection on disagreement.

entry.title: Staged Depth-Pruning Distillation of a Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech Teacher: A Compact Hindi Speech Synthesizer

author.name: Sivateja Trikutam

entry.summary: This paper distills a large flow-matching Hindi TTS teacher into a compact student under a severe 17.6-hour data budget by pruning transformer depth while keeping other dimensions fixed and re-fine-tuning progressively. It measures how much depth can be removed before quality collapses.

entry.title: Privileged Lesion-Context Relational Distillation for Mask-Free Skin Lesion Classification

author.name: Abu Mukaddim Rahi, Md Mithun Hossain, Md Zulficar Hasan Joy, M. F. Mridha, Md. Jakir Hossen

entry.summary: PLCRD is a teacher-student framework for skin lesion classification that uses lesion segmentation masks only during training, letting a privileged teacher learn lesion-context representations while an image-only student is distilled for practical mask-free inference. It preserves the diagnostic benefit of masks without their inference-time cost.

entry.title: State Compression in Two-Agent LLM Relays: A Closed-World Study of Constraint Preservation

author.name: Anantha Sharma, Sheeba Elizabeth John, Kaarthik Senthil Kumar, Saratsuhas Vijayababu

entry.summary: Studies hand-off state compression in a two-agent LLM travel-planning relay, where a Researcher audits an inventory and a Booker decides using only a compressed payload. It compares no compression, narrative summarization, and schema-constrained conditions to see how omissions break strict numeric or categorical constraints.

entry.title: Engineering Trustworthy Agentic AI for Critical Systems

author.name: Omar Al-Refai, Ibrahim Shahbaz, Adam Ali Husseinat, Michael Mandulak, Jaewon Kim, Eman Hammad

entry.summary: A survey that treats trustworthiness of agentic AI as a first-class engineering property for critical systems, organized around dimensions like safety and constraint satisfaction, robustness, transparency, and accountability. It argues capability-only evaluation is insufficient when decisions carry physical or economic consequences.

entry.title: Do AI-Native Biotechs Need Departments? Benchmarking Company World Models for AI-Driven Drug Development

author.name: Yinan Wang

entry.summary: Argues that AI-native biotech companies should be organized around a Company World Model, a persistent asset-to-value state representation with transition models and value functions, rather than mimicking human departmental org charts. It introduces a dry-lab benchmark of retrospective decision cases to compare organizational designs for AI agents.

entry.title: NaviAIS: A Scenario-Level Vessel Trajectory Prediction Dataset withVectorized Lane Priors and the NaviLane Forecasting Framework

author.name: Yuan Gui, Hongchen Luo, Liqi Qu, Longyue Fu, Jiao Wang

entry.summary: NaviAIS is a standardized scenario-level AIS dataset for vessel trajectory prediction that adds vectorized lane priors and navigable-region constraints, addressing inconsistent sampling and missing waterway structure in existing datasets. It is paired with the NaviLane forecasting framework for environment-aware prediction.

entry.title: Enhancing Transformer-based Routing by Encoding Distance via Relative Positional Encoding

author.name: Leyre Enc\'io, Daniel Fuertes, Carlos R. del-Blanco, Fernando Jaureguizar

entry.summary: Enhances Transformer-based routing for the Team Orienteering Problem by adding relative positional encoding as an additive attention bias that embeds pairwise spatial relationships among graph nodes. Experiments on instances up to 100 nodes show consistent improvements in collected rewards and optimality gaps over vanilla Transformers.

entry.title: From Dependency to Compositionality: A Neurosymbolic Lifting of LLM Outputs via Combinatory Categorial Grammar

author.name: Remo Pareschi

entry.summary: Proposes a neurosymbolic framework that lifts autoregressive LLM outputs into typed compositional derivations using Combinatory Categorial Grammar, arguing that prefix-driven, type-completing generation aligns with CCG's incremental processing model. It offers a compositional grammatical account of LLM generation without claiming LLMs internally implement CCG.

entry.title: Quality Action Assurance: Multimodal Verification of Examiner Claims in VR OSCEs

author.name: Harry Rogers, Sally Shiels, Ashley Tomlinson, James Thomas, James Aylward, Nathan Gauge, Helen Higham, Alison Noble

entry.summary: Quality Action Assurance is a multimodal framework that verifies examiner claims in VR pediatric clinical exams by aligning claimed actions against a true event sequence reconstructed from video, VR logs, and actor data. It addresses examiner subjectivity and bias in OSCE scoring beyond inter-rater statistics.

entry.title: On the Effectiveness of Pretraining for Graph Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: David Aguado, Daniel Fuertes, Carlos R. del-Blanco, Fernando Jaureguizar

entry.summary: Introduces a self-supervised pretraining framework for graph combinatorial optimization using graph contrastive learning with geometric augmentations like rotations and reflections to learn invariant structural representations for routing problems. It reports pretraining improves tour lengths over non-pretrained models, notably on large TSP instances.

entry.title: Compressing What Matters: Neuron Importance Meets Data-Aware Low Rank Approximation for Language Model Compression

author.name: Athanasios Ntovas, Alexandros Doumanoglou, Petros Drakoulis, Dimitris Zarpalas

entry.summary: Combines neuron importance scoring with data-aware low-rank approximation for compressing language model weight matrices via SVD, integrating two perspectives previous work treated separately. Aims to reduce compression error while preserving downstream task performance.

entry.title: Competitive and Complementary Tools

author.name: David C. Krakauer

entry.summary: Models the agent, tool, and task as one dynamical system where user competence and reliance co-evolve, finding the outcome is bistable with hysteresis. Above a critical tool availability competence collapses toward a dependent floor, and lowering availability does not reverse it until a far lower threshold.

entry.title: Querying Multimodal Scientific Papers with AI: Practices and Preferences Across Blind, Low-Vision, and Sighted Scientists

author.name: Arnavi Chheda-Kothary, Lucy Lu Wang, Joseph Chee Chang, Jonathan Bragg

entry.summary: Interviews five blind or low-vision and five sighted scientists about how they use ChatGPT and Gemini to query figures, tables, and diagrams in multimodal scientific papers, characterizing practices and accessibility gaps in visual question answering. Aims to inform more accessible AI-assisted document exploration.

entry.title: EduPanel: A Three-Agent LLM Judge for Teaching Videos -- Reliability, Complementarity, and Human Trust Calibration

author.name: Jia-Kai Dong, Yi-Cheng Lin, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Presents EduPanel, a rubric-grounded, learner-conditioned multi-agent LLM judge that decomposes teaching-video evaluation across specialized agents to produce interpretable pedagogical assessments. Reports reliability comparable to a median human expert with feedback that improves scoring.

entry.title: AgentTrails: Towards Trust and Reuse for Agentic Tasks

author.name: Eden Wu, Sonia Castelo, Yurong Liu, Cl\'audio T. Silva, Juliana Freire

entry.summary: Presents AgentTrails, a prototype that converts raw agent trajectories into structured provenance graphs modeling tool calls as computational actions and inputs/outputs as data artifacts, to reveal dataflow dependencies obscured by chronological logs. Supports understanding, comparing, debugging, and reusing agent executions.

entry.title: A Self-Evolving Default Action for Cooperative Tasks with Continuous Action Space

author.name: Shuangyao Huang

entry.summary: Proposes SAFE, a multi-agent RL framework extending counterfactual credit assignment to continuous action spaces via a self-evolving default action drawn from experience buffers. It avoids the Monte Carlo baseline bias that plagues prior continuous cooperative methods.

entry.title: Unsupervised Multi-kernel Learning for Automated Algorithm Selection

author.name: Yihang Lu, Tome Eftimov, Carola Doerr

entry.summary: Studies an unsupervised alternative to supervised algorithm selection using multi-kernel clustering over heterogeneous landscape features, with clusters mapped post hoc to solver recommendations under a strictly separated evaluation protocol. It aims for label-free generalization to unseen problem classes.

entry.title: GEqTrain: A Configuration-Driven Framework for Retargeting Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Across 3D Scientific Tasks

author.name: Daniele Angioletti, Marco Nobile, Vittorio Limongelli

entry.summary: Presents GEqTrain, a configuration-driven framework that separates dataset semantics, model composition, and training objectives so a shared equivariant GNN backbone can be retargeted across 3D scientific tasks via Hydra configs. It reduces implementation lock-in for equivariant models.

entry.title: Conservative Query and Adaptive Regularization for Offline RL Under Uncertainty Estimation

author.name: Li-Rong Zhou, Qin-Wen Luo, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes conservative query selection and adaptive regularization for offline RL, improving how informative preference queries are chosen and how collected feedback is exploited under uncertainty. It addresses instability from fixed constraints and poor value-regularization integration.

entry.title: S3: Stable Subgoal Selection by Constraining Uncertainty of Coarse Dynamics in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kshitij Kumar Srivastava, Kshitij Jerath

entry.summary: Proposes S3, a hierarchical RL method that stabilizes high-level subgoal selection using dynamics-aware intrinsic motivation that constrains uncertainty over coarse dynamics rather than requiring broad state-action coverage. It addresses the sparse, delayed feedback problem for high-level agents.

entry.title: Position: The Inevitable Transition to Machine Learning in Quantum Chemistry

author.name: Karen Sargsyan, Chao-Ping Hsu

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that machine learning is the most promising path forward for quantum chemistry, framed as a decision-theoretic bet that succeeds whether the underlying problems are truly hard or merely lack simple analytical solutions. It reframes recent traditional-method saturation as motivation.

entry.title: Local Label-Informed Feature Transfer for Generating Ground-Truth Medical Images: A Comparison of GAN- and Diffusion-Based Approaches

author.name: Rick Wilming, Irem Ozseker, Luca Matteo Cornils, Ahc\`ene Boubekki, Benedict Clark, Danny Panknin, Stefan Haufe

entry.summary: Introduces LLIFT, a framework generating semi-synthetic brain MRIs with realistic lesions in user-controlled regions without pixel-level lesion annotations, implemented with both GAN and diffusion paradigms, to provide ground-truth for validating explainability methods. It compares generative approaches for creating XAI evaluation data.

entry.title: Building a European Multilingual Evaluation Dataset: The MMLU Localisation Project within the EMT Network

author.name: Pilar S\'anchez-Gij\'on, Susana Valdez, Sof\'ia Calvo Del Barrio, Florence Bellemont, Anna Kokkinidou, Mihai Cristian Brasoveanu

entry.summary: This project reports on localizing the MMLU benchmark into 11 European languages through a collaboration between EU translation bodies and translation masters programs. It aims to make LLM evaluation more inclusive while giving students professional training.

entry.title: Using Fine-Tuned LLMs to Identify Indicators of Vulnerability in UK Police Incident Logs

author.name: Sam Relins, Daniel Birks

entry.summary: This work adapts an LLM classification pipeline built on US police data to estimate the prevalence of vulnerability indicators like mental illness, substance misuse, and homelessness in UK police incident logs. It combines repeated inference, label aggregation, and human review to gauge when outputs are defensible measurements.

entry.title: Constrained CTC Decoding for Efficient Diacritic Restoration

author.name: Rufael Marew, Amr Keleg, Hanan Aldarmaki

entry.summary: The authors propose a non-autoregressive CTC-based method for Arabic diacritic restoration from speech that enforces hard constraints during decoding by building a character-level diacritization lattice. It restricts hypotheses to valid diacritized realizations for efficiency.

entry.title: Enabling Multilingual Privacy Policy Audits: Large-Scale Analysis of Spanish Mobile Apps

author.name: Marcos Moran, David Rodriguez, Luka Nenadic, Norman Sadeh, Jose M. Del Alamo

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether LLMs can extend privacy-policy analysis to all 24 official EU languages without language-specific adaptation, using translated expert-annotated corpora. It aims to enable large-scale multilingual privacy audits beyond English-centric pipelines.

entry.title: Text-conditioned Segmentation for Tomato Phenotyping via Procedural Synthetic Data

author.name: Samy Mounir, Mikolaj Cieslak, Najmeddine Dhieb, Hakim Ghazzai, Jonathan Klein, Katja Froehlich, Soeren Pirk, Wojciech Palubicki, Gianluca Setti, Ahmed M. Eltawil, Dominik L. Michels

entry.summary: This work presents a sim-to-real framework for tomato plant segmentation that generates a large procedural synthetic greenhouse dataset and fine-tunes a foundation model to overcome the scarcity of annotated agricultural data. It uses text-conditioned segmentation for phenotyping under diverse conditions.

entry.title: Dual-Edged Homogeneous-Modality Similarity: Towards Visible-Infrared Modality-Incomplete Person Re-Identification with Modality Adaptive Matching

author.name: Xin Xu, Shuhao Zhan, Wei Liu, Zheng Wang, Kui Jiang, Chia-Wen Lin

entry.summary: This paper tackles open-world visible-infrared person re-identification where queries and galleries can mix homogeneous and heterogeneous modalities, proposing modality-adaptive matching to handle matching conflicts and modality uncertainty. It moves beyond the closed-world heterogeneous-retrieval assumption.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Pathology-Informed Representation Learning for PET-Based Content Retrieval of Intra-Tumour Heterogeneity

author.name: Rajat Vashistha, Sandra Brosda, Lauren G. Aoude, Christine Jestin Hannan, James M. Lonie, Jessica Ng, Andrew Nathanson, Ellie Vloedmans, Caroline Cooper, Andrew P. Barbour, Viktor Vegh

entry.summary: This paper proposes a weakly supervised PET representation-learning framework for content-based medical image retrieval that uses H&E histology information during training while keeping PET-only inference via a teacher-student strategy. It generates embeddings and intra-tumor heterogeneity maps for an esophageal cancer test case.

entry.title: STS-NET: Spatio-Temporal Stress Network for Self-Supervised Crop Stress Detection using Satellite Image Time Series

author.name: Pradeep Dalal, Rajiv Ranjan, Sushil Ghildiyal, Shashank Tamaskar, Neeraj Goel

entry.summary: STS-NET is a self-supervised 3D convolutional autoencoder that detects crop stress from satellite image time series using four vegetation indices, avoiding the need for large labeled datasets. It captures spatiotemporal stress patterns from high-resolution PlanetScope imagery.

entry.title: In-Context Learning for Wound Classification with Small Multimodal Language Models

author.name: George Martvel, Oskar Gustafsson, John Pavia, Ernst Ahlberg

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether small multimodal language models from the Qwen, Ministral, and Gemma families can classify wound images training-free via retrieval-based in-context learning, comparing zero-shot, random few-shot, and kNN-retrieved examples. It targets a training-free alternative to task-specific supervised wound classifiers.

entry.title: SynGallery: A Synthetic Gallery of Real Paintings for Instance-Level Artwork Recognition

author.name: Patryk Bartkowiak, Jakub Markil, Bartosz Kotrys, Dominik Michels, S\"oren Pirk, Wojtek Palubicki

entry.summary: SynGallery is a synthetic gallery dataset for instance-level artwork recognition that places catalog images of real paintings into procedurally generated 3D gallery scenes rendered under varied viewpoints, lighting, and reflections. It bridges the gap between clean training catalogs and messy visitor-photo queries without collecting new real photos.

entry.title: Learning Semantic-Robust Change Detection via Semantic-Invariant Self-Distillation

author.name: Jiuhe Qu, Yingping Liang, Ying Fu

entry.summary: SCDistill improves remote-sensing change detection robustness by using semantic-invariant self-distillation that learns from perturbed but semantically consistent data, making features resistant to non-semantic variations like illumination, shadows, and atmospheric changes. It aims to reduce false alarms and improve real-world generalization.

entry.title: IMMoE: Incomplete Multi-View Anomaly Detection via Mixture of View Experts Fusion

author.name: Lei Hu
