entry.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid augmented Lagrangian method combining evolutionary algorithms with constraint-handling for general constrained optimization, aiming to blend gradient-free global search with the feasibility guarantees of numerical methods. It targets high-dimensional engineering and robotics problems.

entry.title: Real-Time sEMG-Based Telecontrol of an Assistive Robotic Arm Using a 1D Convolutional Neural Network

author.name: Edgar Manacorda, Mena Samir Kama Abouseffien, Olivier Lecompte, Amandine Gesta, Abolfazl Mohebbi

entry.summary: This work proposes a real-time surface-electromyography interface for teleoperating an assistive robotic arm, using four-channel sEMG acquisition, preprocessing, sliding-window segmentation, and a 1D convolutional neural network for classification. It targets intuitive, responsive control for users with upper-limb motor impairments.

entry.title: SHAPE: Simultaneous Water Hydraulic Actuation and Position Estimation of a Sensorless Remote Actuator through a Thin and Long Flexible Tube

author.name: Yuki Nakamura, Shuto Yoshimura, Tomoyuki Noda, Yoshihiro Nakata

entry.summary: SHAPE enables simultaneous water-hydraulic actuation and position estimation of a sensorless remote actuator through a thin, long flexible tube, transmitting both drive power and actuator-side information without local sensors. This supports robot operation in harsh environments where electronics fail.

entry.title: Finite-Time Curvature-Constrained Vector Field for Saturation-Free Motion Planning of Nonholonomic Robots

author.name: Zhouru Xiao, Sha Luo, Yang Lu, H\'ector Garc\'ia de Marina, Zhenyang Xu, Chaosong Gong, Yaonan Wang, Weijia Yao

entry.summary: This work develops a finite-time curvature-constrained vector field for saturation-free motion planning of nonholonomic robots, generating trajectories that satisfy curvature limits without relying on input saturation. It provides an explicit settling-time bound rather than only asymptotic convergence.

entry.title: Receiver-Centered Robot-to-Human Handover with Grasp-Aware Object Orientation

author.name: Federico Biagi, Dario Onfiani, Simone Silenzi, Luigi Biagiotti

entry.summary: This paper presents a receiver-centered voice-driven adaptive handover system for mechanical tools built on a Franka cobot, using an LLM for intention recognition and MediaPipe for 3D hand tracking to dynamically orient tools handle-first in ergonomically optimal poses. A within-subjects study shows improvements over an object-agnostic static baseline.

entry.title: Lifelong Localization in Dynamic Indoor Environments Combining Odometry with Sparse Distance Sampling

author.name: Michael M. Bilevich, Tomer Buber, Dan Halperin

entry.summary: This work proposes a robust lifelong localization framework for dynamic planar indoor environments that fuses odometry with sparse distance sampling to provide a robust location prior, solving the kidnapped-robot problem in real time up to symmetry. It accounts for dynamic obstacles based on real-world data insights.

entry.title: xperception -- Making Robotic Grasping Easier

author.name: Matteo Bortolon, Andrea Caraffa, Alice Fasoli, Fabio Poiesi

entry.summary: xperception is a zero-shot 6D pose-estimation technology for robotic grasping that uses CAD models and foundation-model features (DINOv2, GeDi) to achieve millimeter-accurate pose estimation without object-specific fine-tuning or annotation. It shows robustness against severe occlusions in industrial bin-picking.

entry.title: Relative Entropy-Bounded Ambiguous Chance Constraints for Robust Planning in Nonlinear Systems

author.name: Trevor N. Wolf, Jay W. McMahon

entry.summary: This paper defines risk probability in stochastic control under distribution ambiguity by constructing a relative-entropy-bounded ambiguity set and using a variational expression for exponential integrals to bound expected risk under unknown distributions near a nominal Gaussian reference. The bound recovers the reference risk in the zero-divergence limit.

entry.title: Tracing causal structure in LLM-generated text: a different lens on the Dallas circuit

author.name: yun dong

entry.summary: This post reinterprets Anthropic's Dallas circuit by analyzing causal structure in the generated reasoning text rather than hidden activations, using gradient attribution, DAG tracing, and sparse pruning on Qwen3-1.7B to produce reasoning-trajectory graphs. It proposes context-attribution DAGs as a complementary interpretability lens requiring little semantic prior knowledge.

entry.title: From Overload to Insights: How AI Agents Can Support Scientists in Analyzing Complex Data

author.name: Tim Fuchs, Luca Gelisio, Steffen Hauf, Walid Maalej

entry.summary: Using design science research, this paper builds and evaluates an agentic AI system integrated with European XFEL's HPC environment to help scientists analyze very large experimental datasets. It combines a literature review, tool evaluation, interviews, and a user study to develop two prototypes.

entry.title: When LLMs Over-Answer: Measuring and Mitigating Quality Issues in LLM-Based Hardware Description Language Question Answering

author.name: Ziteng Hu, Jiachi Chen, Wenhao Lv, Huan Zhang, Yingjie Xia

entry.summary: This work measures the quality of LLM answers to hardware description language questions against human experts, curating over 6000 Stack Overflow Q&A posts into a taxonomy and identifying an over-answering problem where redundancy can cause synthesis issues. It proposes mitigations for HDL-specific answer quality.

entry.title: Bridging the Information Gap: Semantic Densification and Hindsight Distillation for Cold-Start Prediction

author.name: Hao Duong Le, Yifei Gao, Huan Li, Lun Jiang, Chen Bai, Ke Xing, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: SemRaD is a cold-start prediction framework combining structured LLM-based semantic densification with hindsight distillation to predict user lifetime value and conversion for new users with sparse history. It addresses noisy LLM rationales and the heterogeneous information gap in privileged-teacher distillation.

entry.title: The Curvature Shadow: An Apparent Failure of Maximum-Entropy Equilibrium Selection is a Removable Artifact

author.name: Luis Leal

entry.summary: This paper investigates why Regularized Nash Dynamics slightly misses the maximum-entropy equilibrium in Kuhn poker despite attaining nearly maximal entropy, showing the small coordinate gap is a removable curvature artifact rather than a genuine selection bias. It provides a quantitative factorization of the gap on a one-dimensional Nash manifold.

entry.title: A${}^2$BM: Alignment-Aware Bridge Matching for Image-to-Image Translation

author.name: Aimi Okabayashi (UBS Vannes), Georges Le Bellier (LIP, CEDRIC - VERTIGO), Nicolas Audebert (LaSTIG, IGN, CEDRIC - VERTIGO), Charlotte Pelletier (OBELIX), Thomas Corpetti (LETG - Rennes), Nicolas Courty (OBELIX)

entry.summary: Alignment-Aware Bridge Matching extends bridge and flow matching for paired image-to-image translation to handle weakly aligned training pairs caused by asynchronous captures, illumination changes, or misregistration. It weights source-target correspondences by reliability rather than assuming perfect alignment.

entry.title: Zero Hallucination, by Construction: Hallucination-Aware Layered Oversight for Trustworthy Enterprise AI

author.name: Bogdan Raduta, Horia Velicu, Alexandru Preda, Serban Chiricescu

entry.summary: HALO argues that zero hallucination should be a system property enforced by layered oversight rather than a model property, presenting a hallucination-aware architecture for enterprise agents. It reframes trustworthiness as engineering constraints around retrieval and faithfulness checks.

entry.title: DeLIVeR: Decomposed Learning for Information-grounded Veracity Recognition via Reinforced Knowledge Graph Exploration

author.name: Cong Hoan Nguyen, Thomas Hoang, Hieu Minh Duong, Long Nguyen

entry.summary: DeLIVeR treats fact-checking evidence retrieval as reinforced strategic exploration, using a planner LLM to decompose claims into targeted questions that traverse knowledge graphs, optimized with GRPO. It reports gains over prior methods on LIAR, FEVER, and PolitiFact.

entry.title: Harness Engineering for LLM-Driven GPU Kernel Generation

author.name: Yue Shui, Chenyu Ma, Hangfei Xu, Shengzhao Wen, Yanpeng Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents a harness-centered system for LLM-driven GPU kernel generation on NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs, separating an evaluation harness that enforces compilation, correctness, and timing from a profile-backed optimization controller. It was built for the MLSys 2026 FlashInfer kernel-generation contest.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Just-In-Time Memory for Proactive Embodied Safety

author.name: Bingrui Sima, Lizhong Wang, Xiaoya Lu, Kun He, Xiao Yang

entry.summary: This work reframes embodied safety from progress-stalling runtime guardrails to proactive hazard mitigation via a self-evolving just-in-time memory framework, using a risk-sufficient topological belief graph for persistent safety-relevant state tracking under partial observability. It aims to break the safety-progress trade-off for VLM-driven household agents.

entry.title: The Third Competition on Document Forgery Detection on ID-Cards and Passports

author.name: Juan E. Tapia, Mario Nieto, Juan M. Espin, \'Alvaro S. Rocamora, Javier Barrachina, Naser Damer, Christoph Busch

entry.summary: This paper reports results of the third international competition on document forgery detection for ID cards and passports across two tracks with synthetic and heterogeneous attack scenarios. It analyzes winning approaches and generalization challenges.

entry.title: Multi-Resolution Voxelized Map-Based Stereo Visual-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Shuyi Pan, Hangtian Wang, Zhaoxing Zhang, Chengliang Zhang, Zikang Yuan, Xin Yang

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-resolution voxelized prior-map construction method and a corresponding map-based stereo visual-inertial odometry system that keeps a single point per voxel and uses a cone-shaped indexing strategy to associate 2D features with 3D map points. It targets bandwidth-limited edge deployment of prior maps.

entry.title: Predicting Grasping Compliance in Robotic Hands through Analytical-Model-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Qianwen Zhao, Long Wang

entry.summary: This paper predicts grasp compliance in underactuated robotic hands using analytical-model-informed neural networks, moving beyond binary grasp success to model how a grasped tool and compliant hand jointly respond to external loading. Compliance arises from coupled kinematics, configuration, passive mechanics, and contact.

entry.title: Stability and Comfort in Mobile Robot-Pedestrian Interactions

author.name: Alireza Jafari, Hong-Son Nguyen, Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: This paper develops socially aware navigation algorithms for nonholonomic mobile robots that model pedestrian comfort and subjective safety using social force and time-to-collision social force models, with stability proofs and experimental validation. It statistically analyzes reported comfort in robot-pedestrian interactions.

entry.title: SLAM in Low-Light Environments: Project Report

author.name: Oleh Basystyi, Anna Stasyshyn, Oleksandr Kosovan, Yaroslav Prytula

entry.summary: This project report benchmarks six SLAM systems spanning feature-based, direct, filter-based, and learning-based paradigms on low-light sequences to assess how far standard RGB-camera SLAM can be pushed in the dark. It highlights how reduced contrast, sensor noise, and motion blur degrade feature extraction and matching.

entry.title: Constrained Path Reasoning: Measuring When Committed Stages Earn Their Cost

author.name: Honglin Li (ShanghaiTech University)

entry.summary: Constrained Path Reasoning provides stage-level accounting to measure when a committed intermediate stage in an LLM reasoning pipeline earns its computational cost, distinguishing hard constraints from soft revisable proposals. It measures effective branching, endpoint concentration, and cost per usable output across generated optimization problems.

entry.title: Coordinated Disentanglement with Iterative Mode Discovery Under Hidden Correlations

author.name: Rong Hu, Ling Chen

entry.summary: CoDID is a disentangled representation learning framework that jointly discovers latent modes and enforces mode-based conditional independence to handle hidden correlations where data under an attribute value exhibit modes correlated with other attributes. It uses a dynamic architecture and a coordination mechanism to avoid error amplification during iteration.

entry.title: An Explicit World Model Based on Data-First Ontology: DaoQL Multimodal Storage Validation and Counterfactual Reasoning Evaluation

author.name: Zhanbo Li, Shifeng Wu, Xiangjin Meng, Wenjie Cai

entry.summary: This paper proposes data-first ontology, treating LLMs as reasoning engines while moving deterministic knowledge into an explicit multimodal database called DaoQL to mitigate hallucination, frozen knowledge, poor explainability, and poor modifiability. It formalizes an explicit world model and argues explicit models enable composable counterfactual decomposability.

entry.title: GenSyn10: A Multi-Generative AI Dataset For Benchmarking Image Classification

author.name: Md Faraz Kabir Khan, Saeed Anwar, Ghulam Mubashar Hassan

entry.summary: GenSyn10 is a CIFAR-10-aligned synthetic image dataset of 60k images generated by three architecturally diverse contemporary generators to study cross-generator generalization in AI-generated image detection. It targets the known failure mode where detectors degrade on unseen generators.

entry.title: Falsification-Based Verification of LLM-Generated Optimization Models: Sound Test Batteries and Their Detection Limits

author.name: Haifeng Li, Mo Hai

entry.summary: This paper develops a falsification-based verification theory for LLM-generated optimization models, testing candidate models only through solver calls on slot-transformed instances without any reference model or label. It derives sound test batteries from duality and comparative statics whose violations certify unfaithfulness, while analyzing detection limits.

entry.title: SGN: A Similarity-based Generative Network for Data Generation under Distribution Shift

author.name: Jiaqi Zhu, Xincheng Chen, Yuncheng Wu, Zhaojing Luo, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: SGN is a reusable generative network trained once on labeled source data and applied to shifted target domains without parameter updates by structuring a latent space via label-induced pairwise similarities. A small labeled target set guides generation for data augmentation under distribution shift.

entry.title: Sparse Evidence Can Suffice: Agentic Evidence Seeking for Multimodal Video Misinformation Detection

author.name: Haochen Zhao, Yongxiu Xu, Xinkui Lin, Dong Xie, Jiarui Lu, Yuqi Qian, Yubin Wang, Hongbo Xu, Gaopeng Gou

entry.summary: SIEVE reframes multimodal video misinformation detection by decoupling evidence acquisition from verification, first identifying sparse decision-relevant clues then judging veracity, rather than exhaustively processing entire videos. It argues that sparse compositional evidence often suffices.

entry.title: A Continual Validation, Updating, and Decision-Making Framework for Self-Adaptive Digital Twins via Robust Model Predictive Control: A Case Study in Additive Manufacturing

author.name: Yi-Ping Chen, Ying-Kuan Tsai, Vispi Karkaria, Seul Lee, Daniel Apley, Wei Chen

entry.summary: This framework maintains digital-twin surrogate fidelity under concept drift by combining a Fisher-score drift detector, LoRA-based parameter-efficient continual updates, and statistical certification that updates genuinely improve prediction, demonstrated in additive manufacturing. It also captures aleatoric uncertainty via robust model predictive control.

entry.title: Learning Adaptive Safety Margins for Visual Navigation

author.name: Junyi Hu, Shuaihang Yuan, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Anthony Tzes, Yi Fang

entry.summary: This work learns a context-conditioned safety critic that adaptively ranks diffusion-planner trajectory proposals by clearance preference, combining a control-barrier-function safety term with efficiency terms for cluttered indoor visual navigation. It targets mis-calibrated fixed safety margins that cause detours or collisions.

entry.title: More Than Memory: Task-Conditioned Signed FFN Writes in Long-Context Retrieval

author.name: Zhibo Yang

entry.summary: This interpretability study scales a model's own feed-forward network write one layer at a time in long-context retrieval, finding these native residual writes are signed, layer-specific, and task-conditioned, with the final FFN typically acting as a suppressor. It shows many layers switch role between literal and semantic retrieval modes.

entry.title: Feedback Attribution and Representation Geometry: Metrics for Comparing Individual and Shared Rewards in MARL

author.name: Tasha Pais, Richard Higgins

entry.summary: This work proposes low-overhead diagnostics, effective rank normalized by agent count and mean pairwise action-distribution divergence, to detect whether team-averaged versus individual rewards leave geometric or behavioral signatures on learned MARL representations. It tests them on MAPPO agents in a StarCraft II combat scenario.

entry.title: CLDRoute: Conditional Latent Diffusion for Routability Map Generation in Physical Design

author.name: Kiran Thorat, Nicole Meng, Caiwen Ding, Yingjie Lao, Zhijie Jerry Shi

entry.summary: CLDRoute reformulates chip routability estimation as conditional latent diffusion generation of spatially structured congestion and design-rule-check fields, using physics-aware conditioning and task-specific latent modeling. It supports sample-based inference producing both mean predictions and uncertainty.

entry.title: BG4Sea: Biogeochemical Seasonal Forecastability via Progressive Information Scaling

author.name: Gabriela Martinez Balbontin, Anastase Charantonis, Dominique Bereziat, Stefano Ciavatta

entry.summary: BG4Sea is presented as the first global data-driven system for multivariate seasonal forecasting of marine biogeochemical state, using a column autoencoder, a latent forecaster, and FiLM-based surface-forcing conditioning. It targets a domain that lags physical oceanography due to complexity and data scarcity.

entry.title: qZACH-ViT: Quantization-Aware Intrinsic Explanations with Recursive Attribution-Stabilized Optimization

author.name: Athanasios Angelakis

entry.summary: qZACH-ViT is a quantization-aware extension of a CLS-token-free, position-free ViT for compact medical-image classification, paired with Recursive Attribution-Stabilized Optimization that aligns classification and attribution gradients. It produces INT8 ONNX models with intrinsic patch-level explanations across MedMNIST datasets.

entry.title: Linear Stability Analysis of an INDI Pitch-Rate Controller under Model Mismatch for a Tilt-Rotor VTOL UAV

author.name: Lorenzo Schenk, Guillaume Ducard, Christopher Onder

entry.summary: This paper presents the control design for a rideable two-wheeled robot with a quadruped form intended as a partner-mobility concept for public events, balancing rider safety, expressive limb movements, and dynamic quadrupedal gait. It addresses matching robot weight and size to a character while managing motor output.

entry.title: Task-Space Constrained Stochastic Trajectory Optimization for Time-Optimal Forestry Crane Motion Planning

author.name: Marc-Philip Ecker, Christoph Fr\"ohlich, Bernhard Bischof, Wolfgang Kemmetm\"uller, Tobias Gl\"uck

entry.summary: This paper presents a task-space constrained stochastic trajectory optimization method for time-optimal forestry crane motion planning that avoids pre-committing to a single inverse-kinematics terminal configuration under nonlinear pump-flow constraints. It extends via-point stochastic trajectory optimization to exploit kinematic redundancy.

entry.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Articulation Angle Estimation of Truck-Semitrailer Combinations

author.name: Qixuan Zhang, Jonas Boettcher, Simon F. G. Ehlers, Marvin Stuede

entry.summary: This work presents hybrid machine learning models that estimate truck-semitrailer articulation angles directly from visual and kinematic inputs, integrated with a kinematic model in an extended Kalman filter, eliminating the need for manual initialization, trailer-mounted sensors, or prior trailer parameters. It targets autonomous driving and ADAS with real-world validation.

entry.title: AI 2040: Is it Actually a Deal?

author.name: 1a3orn

entry.summary: This LessWrong post critiques the AI Futures Project's normative AI 2040 Plan A scenario, raising both within-frame objections that the plan would fail its own goals and personal objections that it would harm things the author values, while praising its recommendation to limit the gap between internal and external model deployments. It is policy-oriented commentary.

entry.title: Banana in, Bostrom out: paperclip maximization is one token-direction swap away (in Qwen 3.6-27B)

author.name: Jeffrey William Shorthill

entry.summary: This LessWrong post reports an amateur interpretability experiment using a global-workspace-style lens on the existing Qwen3.6-27B model, where swapping and ablating token directions under greedy decoding reportedly steers a superintelligence description toward paperclip-maximization themes. It documents exploratory activation-steering findings and their limitations.

entry.title: Frontier AI lab misalignment risk, lessons from trading post-2008

author.name: Peter Chatwell

entry.summary: A former macro trader proposes importing bank-style capital adequacy rules (like Basel III) and senior-management accountability regimes to frontier AI labs, so that firms must hold reserves proportional to their misalignment risk. The aim is to reduce moral hazard and align market incentives with catastrophic-risk mitigation.

entry.title: Should we benchmark conceptual capabilities using judgment prediction tasks?

author.name: Alex Mallen

entry.summary: A short methodological note asking whether subjective conceptual-reasoning capabilities should be benchmarked by having AIs predict a specified person's judgment, rather than relying on unresolvable ground truth. It aims to track progress on neglected conceptual reasoning that could reduce AI 'sloppiness'.

entry.title: Tractable Query Answering under Epistemic Confidentiality Policies in DL Ontologies (extended version)

author.name: Lorenzo Marconi, Daniela Rieti, Riccardo ROsati

entry.summary: This extended paper studies Controlled Query Evaluation for confidentiality-preserving data access over Description Logic ontologies with epistemic-dependency policies. It establishes intractability results and works toward computationally easier semantics that preserve indistinguishability.

entry.title: Supporting Autonomous Process Execution within a Multi-Perspective Constraint Frame via Numeric Planning

author.name: Paul Wittlinger, Giacomo Acitelli, Anti Alman, Fabrizio Maria Maggi, Andrea Marrella

entry.summary: This paper extends framed autonomy in business process management beyond control-flow constraints by using numeric planning to support what-if analysis across multiple constraint perspectives. It introduces a tool for autonomously advancing process execution within a predefined constraint frame.

entry.title: AEVAL: From Anecdotal to Deterministic Testing for Agentic Skill Workflows

author.name: Tejas Singh Anand, Yuet Ying Christina Wang, Wanting Jiang, Steve Masson, Tian Zheng, Bingjie Zhou

entry.summary: AEVAL is a CI-integrated framework that replaces anecdotal demo-based testing of installable agent skills with deterministic, reproducible test pipelines triggered on every change. It aims to provide comparable quality signals across skill versions in growing skill marketplaces.

entry.title: Geometry-Enhanced Portion Estimation for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Lin Liao, Peng Li

entry.summary: This paper adds an accurate food-portion-estimation head to a frozen commercial multimodal LLM using a small geometry-enhanced network on a frozen DINOv2 backbone with a structured softmax-ownership volume, requiring no depth sensor or MLLM fine-tuning. It measures and closes portion-estimation weaknesses of frontier Gemini, GPT, and Claude models.

entry.title: CLOSER-Bench: Evaluating Budgeted Cross-Stage Design Closure for Hardware Agents

author.name: Peilong Zhou, Zhirong Chen, Cangyuan Li, Haoyu Gao, Kaiyan Chang, Ziming Qu, Ying Wang

entry.summary: CLOSER-Bench is a controlled evaluation protocol for budgeted cross-stage hardware design closure that pairs spec-to-RTL, RTL-to-GDS, and spec-to-GDS tasks with a hidden objective to test whether agents can revise across abstraction boundaries. It targets the long-horizon, delayed-feedback nature of hardware engineering that pass-at-k cannot capture.

entry.title: Measuring and Improving Complex-Atomic Answer Consistency in Endoscopic VQA

author.name: Yuhao Liu, Cheng Zhao, Guanghui Yue

entry.summary: EndoCA is a paired complex-atomic answer consistency benchmark for endoscopic visual question answering, testing whether models that answer compound questions correctly also answer the underlying atomic sub-questions consistently. Eleven vision-language models across open, medical, and closed categories are evaluated.

entry.title: RT-SHCUA: Real-Time Self-Hosted Computer-Use Agent for UAV Control

author.name: Di Lu, Bo Zhang, Xiyuan Li, Yongzhi Liao, Xuewen Dong, Yulong Shen, Zhiquan Liu, Jianfeng Ma

entry.summary: RT-SHCUA restructures self-hosted computer-use agents for real-time, security-oriented UAV control, replacing direct flight-command issuance with a mediated architecture to handle timing, safety, and tamper accountability. It addresses the structural mismatch between interactive agent loops and continuous physical control.

entry.title: O-VAD: Industrial Video Anomaly Detection through Object-Centric Tracking and Reasoning

author.name: Mei Yuan, Qi Long, Qifeng Wu, Zhenyang Li, Yizhou Zhao, Lei Wang, Yang Liu, Min Xu

entry.summary: O-VAD is a training-free agentic framework for industrial video anomaly detection that emphasizes object-centric tracking and state-evolution reasoning to handle intricate object transformations and physics constraints where general VLMs falter. It mimics how human inspectors track spatial-temporal dynamics.

entry.title: Leakage-Robust Evaluation and Data-Scale Sensitivity of Attention-Enhanced Multi-Task Learning for Joint Fault Diagnosis and Remaining Useful Life Estimation

author.name: Md Mahamudur Rahaman Shamim, Md. Nuruzzaman, Zannatul Ferdus, Md Rajib Ahmed, Abieer Nwshad Anward, Mohammad Tooneer, Johir Uddin Khan, Khalid Hossen

entry.summary: This paper shows that how sliding-window sequences are split into train and test sets can drastically inflate or destroy reported accuracy in multi-task fault diagnosis and remaining-useful-life models, and introduces a leakage-audited chunk-based splitting protocol. It validates on three public predictive-maintenance benchmarks.

entry.title: Bridging battery design and health assessment through virtual sensing and physics-informed learning

author.name: Wendi Guo, S{\o}ren Byg Vilsen, Daniel Ioan Stroe, Yaqi Li, Yicun Huang, Ashima Verma, Daniel Brandell

entry.summary: This physics-informed learning framework with virtual sensing infers hard-to-measure lithium-ion battery design parameters, such as solid-state diffusion coefficient and electrode thickness, directly from standard battery-management-system measurements. It links battery design and health assessment across fast-charging and driving profiles.

entry.title: Reward-Driven LLM Agent Workflows: Synthesizing POMDP Routing and Self-Correction for Autonomous Decision-Making

author.name: Amez Amanj Ali, Kuo-Kun Tseng

entry.summary: This paper designs an LLM agent workflow synthesizing a POMDP routing mechanism with an internal self-correcting reward model that evaluates decision trajectories before execution, targeting long-horizon planning and sparse reward attribution. It combines several AI paradigms into one agent architecture.

entry.title: Fourier Geometric Wind Power Forecasting with Numerical Weather Prediction

author.name: Shiyuan Piao, Fan Zehui, Yang Liu, Hong Cheng, Juepeng Zheng, Jie Zhou, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multimodal wind power forecasting framework that fuses point-based SCADA turbine data with grid-based numerical weather prediction, decomposing inputs into scalar and vector features using Fourier geometric methods. It targets short-term forecasting for grid stability.

entry.title: Clarify Before Executing: A Self-Evolving Agent for Resolving Intent Asymmetry in 3D Tool Orchestration

author.name: Xiaoye Zhu, Weixin Li, Junan Huo, Bozhong Wang, Jia Zeng, Yi Yang, Cen Chen, Qi Liu

entry.summary: CLARE is a clarification-aware, self-evolving 3D agent that treats vague user instructions as an opportunity for strategic dialogue rather than executing blindly, decoupling generation into four specialized cognitive roles. It resolves underspecified intent before invoking expensive 3D tools.

entry.title: Capacity and Redundancy Trade-offs in Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Asif Khan

entry.summary: This paper studies capacity and redundancy tradeoffs in multi-task learning, introducing a Capacity-Redundancy identity that decomposes per-task predictive information into shared joint information and a residual interference term. It derives a clustering-gap condition for when clustered sharing beats global sharing and a gradient-total-correlation bridge.

entry.title: Vis2Reg: Visibility-Aware Landmark-Free Geometric 3D--2D Registration for Liver Laparoscopy

author.name: Jiaming Feng, Xukun Zhang, Shahid Farid, Sharib Ali

entry.summary: Vis2Reg is a visibility-aware, landmark-free framework for aligning preoperative 3D liver models to partial intraoperative laparoscopic surface views for AR-guided surgery. It derives self-supervision from intraoperative masks to handle severe occlusion.

entry.title: HAS: Highlight-guided Attention Steering for Multimodal LLM Video Summarization

author.name: Rui Chu, Yingjie Lao

entry.summary: HAS steers a multimodal LLM's attention using highlight guidance for video summarization, arguing that discrete key-frame selection loses global frame-importance context. It integrates highlight signals to improve summary quality.

entry.title: LLM Unlearning for Cyber Defense: A Survey on Methods, Challenges, and Emerging Threats

author.name: Ruppikha Sree Shankar, Abhishek Bhardwaj, Arnav Doshi, Anusri Nagarajan, Troy Paulus Asia, Saptarshi Sengupta

entry.summary: This survey reviews LLM unlearning as a cyber-defense tool, covering methods, challenges, and emerging threats around models that retain sensitive, copyrighted, or hazardous knowledge vulnerable to extraction and jailbreaks. It frames the inability to forget as a real security and compliance risk.

entry.title: Operator-Aware Mixed-Precision Tolerance Calibration for Tensor Kernels

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: This work mines element-wise error distributions from thousands of cloud GPU kernel runs to calibrate mixed-precision tolerance thresholds per operator, finding that current hand-picked absolute tolerances are far too loose. Some kernels justify tolerances hundreds to thousands of times tighter.

entry.title: Discrete Ricci Curvature on Protein Contact Graphs for Lightweight Fold Classification

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: This work uses discrete Ollivier-Ricci and Forman-Ricci curvature on protein contact graphs as a compact 22-dimensional structural descriptor for fold classification, benchmarked against geometry, persistent homology, and protein language model embeddings. It offers a lightweight alternative to heavy embeddings.

entry.title: A Framework for Early Sepsis Prediction via Self-Supervised (JEPA) and Federated Representation Learning

author.name: Umair bin Mansoor, Munaf Rashid, Roomi Naqvi

entry.summary: This paper compares four modeling paradigms for early sepsis prediction from irregularly sampled ICU records, including JEPA masked latent prediction, VICReg self-supervision, semi-supervised fine-tuning, and a supervised temporal convolutional network. The best combination pairs JEPA embeddings with gradient-boosted trees.

entry.title: Robust Losses from Univariate Base Functions for Noisy-Label Learning

author.name: Peng Hu, Jianwei Ma

entry.summary: This paper introduces a general framework that builds robust multiclass losses for noisy-label learning from univariate base functions, so robustness properties can be characterized through simple base-function properties. It develops two complementary construction schemes.

entry.title: Value-Monotonicity Matters: A Concordance Loss for Deep Survival Prediction

author.name: Meixu Chen, Kai Wang, Jing Wang

entry.summary: This paper argues that likelihood objectives used to train deep survival models are unreliable signals for the concordance index used to evaluate them, especially for small censored oncology cohorts where frequent C-index evaluation is costly. It proposes a value-monotone concordance loss with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Honest Physical-Support Inference after Latent Dictionary Learning: Collision Singularities and Minimax Resolution

author.name: Guan-Ju Peng

entry.summary: This theoretical paper develops honest uncertainty inference for active physical rays after latent dictionary learning, addressing overconfident conclusions near collisions of coherent atoms by retaining all dictionaries compatible with a robust training-moment region. It projects surviving configurations onto a permutation-invariant support space with minimax resolution.

entry.title: Multimodal Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition via Cross-Attention and Gated Fusion

author.name: Oussama Berhili, Yassine Ouzar, Larbi Boubchir

entry.summary: This is a multimodal framework for ambivalence and hesitancy recognition in video for the ABAW11 challenge, fusing text, audio, and facial features with cross-attention and gated fusion. Text features alone outperform a zero-shot Video-LLaVA baseline substantially.

entry.title: Handwritten and Printed Text Segmentation via Region-Aware Human-Writing Descriptor Engineering

author.name: Zhixian Lu, Jianwei Zhang, Lei Zhang, Fei Yuan, Jin Wang, Chang Liu, Rui Gao, Qiyu Lei

entry.summary: This work presents a lightweight framework for segmenting handwritten and printed text in document images for resource-constrained edge devices, using sentence-level connected-component segmentation and a region-aware handwriting descriptor. It targets efficient document digitization.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Semantic Segmentation of Electrolyzer Components for Sustainable Hydrogen Technologies: A Dual-Branch Deep Learning Approach

author.name: Wasimul Karim, Nur Mohammad Fahad, Abdul Hasib Siddique, Md Rafiqul Islam, Hooman Mehdizadeh-Rad, Asif Karim, Sami Azam

entry.summary: HREM-Net is a dual-branch deep learning framework fusing hyperspectral and RGB imaging for semantic segmentation of electrolyzer components, supporting sustainable hydrogen recycling and disassembly. It combines attention modules and ASPP to handle spectral overlap and class imbalance.

entry.title: Vision-Language Assistant for Emotional Reactions to Risky Driving

author.name: Harine Choi, Eun Hak Lee, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: This paper presents a vision-language pipeline (KYA) that detects risky driving maneuvers such as sudden cut-ins using YOLOv8 and generates emotionally expressive LLM responses to support driver awareness. It emphasizes the neglected emotional and user-experience dimension of driver assistance.

entry.title: Articulated Humanoid Head for a Robot Receptionist Capable of Natural Human Interaction

author.name: Tharusha Fonseka, Charuka Bandara, Moshintha Hewavitharana, Melisa Arukgoda, Wageesha N. Manamperi, Udaya S. K. Perera Miriya Thanthrige, Peshala Jayasekara

entry.summary: This paper describes an articulated humanoid robot head with 21 degrees of freedom and realistic silicone skin designed for a receptionist role, integrating mechanisms for mouth, eyes, eyebrows, and neck. It targets lower cost and greater adaptability than existing expressive humanoid heads.

entry.title: Polar Coordinate-based Differential Evolution for Moving Target Search Using Vision Sensor on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

author.name: Thu Hang Khuat, Duy-Nam Bui, Thuy Ngan Duong, Manh Duong Phung

entry.summary: This paper proposes a polar coordinate-based differential evolution algorithm for UAV search of moving targets, modeling target dynamics as a Markov process and detection likelihood as a function of image quality and observer vision, with a Bayesian fitness function. It targets improved detection probability within the search-and-rescue golden time.

entry.title: Isaac Sim-to-Real: Reinforcement Learning based Locomotion for Quadrupeds

author.name: Jordan Dowdy, Jean Chagas Vaz

entry.summary: This work presents a robust reinforcement learning locomotion framework for quadrupeds trained in NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab and deployed to physical hardware, aiming to bridge the sim-to-real gap for whole-body control. It documents the training and transfer pipeline using the newer simulation tools.

entry.title: Learning-Driven Adaptive Audit Scheduling: A Sequential Decision Approach to Off-Chain Data Integrity

author.name: Changting Lin, Fan Li, Weihang Yu, Keyang He, Mingyuan Yan, Yourong Chen, Meng Han

entry.summary: This work models cryptographic auditing of off-chain data as a constrained POMDP and proposes DRQN-CMDP, a deep recurrent Q-network with a GRU belief over latent node types paired with Lagrangian dual ascent to meet a miss-rate constraint. It reports strong results against 13 baselines with O(1) on-chain verification via a pairing-free homomorphic MAC.

entry.title: Position: Explanation Stability Is a Property of the Model Method Pair, Not the Model

author.name: Kabilan Elangovan, Daniel Ting

entry.summary: This position paper argues that explanation stability is a property of the model-method pair rather than the model alone, showing in chest X-ray experiments that stability rankings of high-accuracy models reverse across attribution methods. It calls for cross-method validation before making stability claims.

entry.title: Orthogonal Gradient Constraints Shape Noisy-Label Memorization Dynamics

author.name: Richard Mai

entry.summary: This paper studies OrthoGrad, which removes the gradient component parallel to the weight vector, as a geometric intervention against noisy-label memorization in image classification. It finds the strongest benefit for small-data CNNs, reducing corrupted-label fitting.

entry.title: Design and Validation of a Lightweight 1D CNN for Affective Touch Classification in Soft Plush Companions

author.name: Aleksandrs Vali\v{s}evskis, Aleksandrs Okss, Inese T\=i\c{g}ere, Aleksejs Kata\v{s}evs, Dina Bethere, Anete Hofmane, Airisa \v{S}teinberga, Und\=ine Gavri\c{l}enko, Santa Me\c{l}\c{k}e, Lucie Matou\v{s}kov\'a

entry.summary: The authors build a lightweight 1D CNN and release an open FAIR-compliant dataset of over 1300 labeled touch gestures for recognizing affective touch in soft, sensorized plush companions. The main contribution is a reusable dataset and MATLAB pipeline for socially assistive robotics.

entry.title: DS@GT ARC at eRisk 2026: Hybrid Multi-Agent LLM System with Structured Algorithmic Guidance for Conversational Depression Screening

author.name: Victor Gong, David Guecha

entry.summary: This system-description paper details a hybrid multi-agent LLM pipeline for conversational depression screening that infers BDI-II scores without directly asking sensitive questions, evolving from a monolithic prototype to a multi-agent design using an open Gemma model. It documents lessons from a shared-task submission.

entry.title: It Depends on the Dataset: When a Brain-Encoding Model's Predicted Responses Beat Their Visual Backbone for Video Memorability

author.name: Carson Rodrigues

entry.summary: This work tests whether predicted fMRI responses from a brain-encoding foundation model serve as useful features for forecasting short-video memorability, compared against the model's own visual backbone. It finds the answer is dataset-dependent, with the brain projection winning on one benchmark and losing on another.

entry.title: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Sensor-based Activity Recognition

author.name: Mohd Halim Mohd Noor, Abdulrahman M. A. Baraka

entry.summary: This work applies a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to sensor-based human activity recognition, learning representations from unlabeled data with an encoder modeling both fine-grained local and long-term temporal structure. It adds an improved variance-invariance regularization term.

entry.title: PRISM: Multimodal Terrain Mapping for Rover Navigation in Unstructured Environments

author.name: Raul Castilla-Arquillo, Carlos Perez-del-Pulgar, Levin Gerdes, Alfonso Garcia-Cerezo, Miguel A. Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: PRISM is a multimodal terrain-mapping perception system for rover navigation in unstructured environments, fusing aligned RGB, depth, and thermal imagery via OmniUnet, a vision-transformer segmentation network. Thermal fusion improves terrain differentiation for safer traversal.

entry.title: DataFlow-Harness: A Grounded Code-Agent Platform for Constructing Editable LLM Data Pipelines

author.name: Runming He, Zhen Hao Wong, Hao Liang, Zimo Meng, Chengyu Shen, Xiaochen Ma, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: DataFlow-Harness guides an LLM agent to build platform-native directed acyclic graph data pipelines through typed incremental mutations rather than free-form scripts, bridging what the authors call the natural-language-to-pipeline gap. It combines procedural skills, a Model Context Protocol layer exposing live pipeline state, and a synchronized web UI.

entry.title: Privacy Cost as Equity Input: A Group Fairness Criterion for Differentially Private Machine Learning

author.name: Rakshit Naidu

entry.summary: This paper reframes differential-privacy fairness by treating per-group privacy cost as itself a harm, introducing a compensatory Privacy-Cost Equity Ratio that normalizes a group's positive prediction rate by its overfitting gap. It argues groups bearing greater privacy exposure are owed proportionally greater benefit.

entry.title: A Causal Markov Condition for Value

author.name: Olav Benjamin Vassend

entry.summary: OFD-Net is a teacher-free semi-supervised medical segmentation framework using orthogonal foreground-background feature disentanglement to gauge pseudo-label reliability.

entry.title: Natural Language Access to Domain-Specific Metadata: A Reusable Framework for LLM Query Generation

author.name: Blake G. Fitch, Cato Elia Kurtz

entry.summary: NLKGQ enables natural-language querying of domain-specific archive metadata by leveraging a well-designed OWL ontology so LLMs can generate accurate structured queries zero-shot, without fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation. It provides a reusable framework and web interface.

entry.title: On the Potential of Graph Neural Networks as Metamodels for Supply Chain Optimization: Dataset, Architectures, and Directions

author.name: Tushar Lone, Neha Karanjkar

entry.summary: This paper explores graph neural networks as differentiable surrogate metamodels for supply-chain optimization, arguing their topology generalization enables combined structural and parametric optimization that classical metamodels cannot. It contributes a large public dataset of programmatically generated supply-chain graphs with performance metrics.

entry.title: Interpretable Anomaly and Drift Detection with Gaussian Mixture Models

author.name: Behnam Asadi

entry.summary: This work revisits Gaussian mixture models as a lightweight interpretable tool for anomaly and distributional-drift detection, automatically selecting components via the Bayesian Information Criterion, scoring by negative log-likelihood with extreme-value-theory thresholds, and naming each component a regime for drift tracking. It is evaluated on seven public benchmarks.

entry.title: Hardware-triggered Time Synchronization of Roadside Multi-lidar, Multi-camera Measurement System for Accurate Data Alignment

author.name: Shiva Agrawal, Savankumar Bhanderi, Zhiran Yan, Gordon Elger

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-source, modular, hardware-triggered time-synchronization circuit for roadside multi-lidar and multi-camera systems, generating programmable time-delayed trigger pulses per sensor. It improves temporal alignment for reliable perception in dense urban traffic.

entry.title: DebrisTracer: Reliable Tracking in Hypervelocity Impact Fast Imaging

author.name: Th\'eophane Loloum, Fabien Vivodtzev, David H\'ebert, Baptiste Reynier, Michel Arrigoni, Julien Tierny

entry.summary: DebrisTracer extends an off-the-shelf topology-tracking framework based on critical-point extraction and matching to reliably track debris fragments in noisy hypervelocity impact fast imaging, incorporating domain knowledge and physical assumptions. It enables interpretable estimation of debris mass and speed distributions for aerospace applications.

entry.title: How to Build Marcus's Algebraic Mind: From Thagard's Brain--Mind Viewpoint

author.name: Hiroyuki Chuma, Kanji Otsuka, Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: This paper proposes VaCoAl, a hyperdimensional architecture built on GF(2) XOR-and-shift as a single primitive, to satisfy Marcus's three requirements for algebraic cognition and Thagard's binding mechanism for perception, emotion, consciousness, and self. It argues one substrate answers both critiques of connectionism.

entry.title: Online path planning for kinematic-constrained UAVs in a dynamic environment based on a Differential Evolution algorithm

author.name: Elias J. R. Freitas, Miri Weiss Cohen, Frederico G. Guimar\~aes, Luciano C. A. Pimenta

entry.summary: This work presents an online UAV path planner handling dynamic obstacles and motion constraints such as maximum curvature and orientation, using a NURBS path representation and a differential evolution algorithm with velocity-obstacle-based constraints. Initial results show feasibility as a basis for 3D extensions.

entry.title: S.E.A.G.R: A Socially and Emotionally Aware Greeting Robot Framework with Dual-Layer Cultural and Affective Modulation

author.name: Sajjad Hussain, Ranveer Bhura, Amandip Dutta, Shwetangshu Biswas

entry.summary: SEAGR is a socially and emotionally aware greeting robot framework with dual-layer modulation where cultural identity selects the greeting type and affective cues shape how it is delivered. It addresses static greeting routines that ignore cultural variation, emotion, and interpersonal distance.

entry.title: A BIM-enabled, Agent-based Discrete-event Simulation Platform for Robotic Studies: A Method based on Graph Theory

author.name: Ping Xu, Xinghua Gao

entry.summary: This work presents a BIM-enabled, agent-based discrete-event simulation platform grounded in graph theory to give indoor robots access to building information for complex tasks like locating and repairing leaking pipes. It couples navigation with rich geometric, semantic, and operational building attributes.

entry.title: UMCP: A Unified Multi-Task Collaborative Perception Network for Luggage Trolley Pose Estimation

author.name: Zhirui Sun, Zhihao Jiang, Yao Wang, Jianwei Peng, Jiankun Wang

entry.summary: UMCP is a unified multi-task collaborative perception network built on YOLOv12 that simultaneously performs luggage-trolley detection, keypoint detection, and orientation estimation, fusing keypoint and orientation features to reduce cascaded-inference latency. It targets real-time robotic luggage-trolley collection in cluttered airports.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

author.name: Xiaomi Robotics Team, Jun Guo, Piaopiao Jin, Jason Li, Peiyan Li, Yingyan Li, Futeng Liu, Wanli Peng, Optimus Qin, Yifei Su, Nan Sun, Qiao Sun, Runze Suo, Heyun Wang, Yunhong Wang, Rujie Wu, Caoyu Xia, Lina Zhang, Jack Zhao, Guoliang Chen, Wenlong Chen, Xinze He, Bin Li, Qing Li, Zhuorong Li, Heng Qu, Wenxuan Song, Diyun Xiang, Yifan Xie, Peiran Xu, Hangjun Ye, Wen Ye, Han Zhao, Quanyun Zhou

entry.summary: As already featured in Research yesterday, Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a foundational vision-language-action model trained on over 100K hours of real-world manipulation trajectories collected via UMI devices, with a two-stage pretrain/post-train recipe and a scalable auto-labeling pipeline. It performs mobile manipulation in unseen environments and adapts with minimal fine-tuning.

entry.title: A Research Prototype for Closed-Loop Generative Design of Customized Foot Orthoses via Semantic-Physics Alignment

author.name: Rui Wang, Byungwon Min, Suxing Liu

entry.summary: TANS-FO is a research prototype pipeline that maps unstructured clinical prescriptions to patient-specific foot orthosis geometry using a text-aligned neural surrogate and a GNN biomechanics surrogate in a closed loop. It aims to bridge the semantic-physical gap in orthosis design without clinical validation.

entry.title: Drone WMDs Don’t Need Any New Technology

author.name: Felix Choussat

entry.summary: Written for a national-security audience, this piece argues that cheap, disposable drones already constitute accessible weapons capable of mass effect without any new technology, citing casualty and attrition data from recent conflicts. It contends AI is quietly raising the floor of accessible destructive capability.

entry.title: Efficient EEG Seizure Detection Using INT8 Quantization, Channel Pruning, and Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Kartikey Ahlawat

entry.summary: This study benchmarks three brain-inspired efficiency strategies for EEG seizure detection on wearable-class hardware: SNN conversion via parameter transfer, channel pruning with structured sparsity, and INT8 quantization with quantization-aware training. It uses a single 1D CNN baseline on the CHB-MIT dataset.

entry.title: GMoT: Gated Motion-Aware Tokenization for Fine-Grained Micro-Gesture Video Reasoning with Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Taorui Wang, Wei Xia, Hui Ma, Zijia Song, Jiayu Zhang, Zeheng Wang, Yong Xu, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: GMoT is a gated motion-aware tokenization module that distills sparse kinematic evidence for fine-grained micro-gesture recognition with multimodal LLMs, which otherwise rely on static posture priors. It spotlights action-relevant regions and captures inter-frame motion energy before temporal modeling.

entry.title: Automated Hardware Validation Test Plan Generation for Large Scale AI Datacenter Platforms Using a Generative AI Multi-Agents Architecture

author.name: Mohammed-Khalil Ghali, Saurabh Kulkarni, Prathamesh Kulkarni, Rohan Kulkarni, Sangwon Yoon, Daehan Won

entry.summary: This paper presents a generative multi-agent architecture that automates structured hardware validation test-plan generation for large-scale AI datacenter platforms from self-healing documents and bills of materials. It replaces labor-intensive, error-prone manual authoring with traceable structured outputs.

entry.title: How Formerly Incarcerated People Envision Technologies for Prison Parole

author.name: Saiph Savage, Jesse Nava, Wanqing Iris Zhou, Hwijoon Lee

entry.summary: This survey of 31 formerly incarcerated people examines their parole experiences and their visions for technologies to support parole preparation, finding they envision tools as resources for empowerment rather than instruments to dismantle the prison system. It critiques the framing of AI correctional tools as objective and inevitable.

entry.title: How Do You Choose Your AI Component? An Interview Study of Secure AI Integration in Practice

author.name: Mahzabin Tamanna, Elizabeth Lin, Sparsha Gowda, Laurie Williams, Dominik Wermke

entry.summary: This interview study examines how practitioners select and integrate LLM-based AI components and their security considerations, arguing rapid AI adoption has overlooked hard-learned software-supply-chain lessons. It identifies risks like malicious components, data leakage, and unintended behavior.

entry.title: Medical Imaging Fusing Vision Transformer: Laryngeal Cancer Screening with Explanation

author.name: Haiyang Wang, Luca Mainardi

entry.summary: A vision-transformer approach analyzes narrow-band-imaging endoscopy to distinguish benign from malignant laryngeal lesions, adding attention-based explanations to support clinicians. Reported F1 around 83 percent and accuracy around 82 percent are modest for a screening context.

entry.title: Human Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models for Optical Network Automation

author.name: Kiarash Rezaei, Omran Ayoub, Paolo Monti, Carlos Natalino

entry.summary: HuGLEN is a stepwise evaluation pipeline that pairs LLM-as-a-judge with a few expert ratings to rank candidate LLMs by a quality-efficiency score for translating XAI outputs into operator-friendly optical-network explanations. A twelve-billion-parameter model gave the best quality-efficiency trade-off.

entry.title: LLMs and Agentic AI Systems for Smart Grids: A Tutorial on Architectures and Applications

author.name: Daniela Rojas, Abdulwahab Albassam, Aidan G. Leung, Jett Ngo, Ryan Luo, Peter R. Quawas, Junpyung Kim, Kangkai Liang, Mansi Nanavati, Jonathan Mai, Meng-Chi Tsai, Yun-Tong Tsai, Yize Chen, Yuanyuan Shi

entry.summary: This tutorial surveys LLM and agentic AI architectures for smart grids and proposes a solver-grounded design principle where numerical results are reported only when produced by trusted solvers, not directly by the model. It addresses the risk of physically infeasible LLM outputs in grid control.

entry.title: PsiLogic: Chaos-Aware Active Cancellation for Adam with a Fair Cross-Domain Benchmark

author.name: Ali Sultonov

entry.summary: PsiLogic augments Adam with a dynamic active-cancellation damping term gated by a chaos detector based on dual EMAs of gradient norms, providing implicit warmup without a hand-tuned schedule. It is evaluated with a reproducible FairBench protocol including learning-rate sweeps and statistical tests.

entry.title: Multimodal Attention-based Deep Learning for Emergency Triage with Electronic Health Records

author.name: Hazqeel Afyq Athaillah Kamarul Aryffin, Kamarul Aryffin Baharuddin, Mohd Halim Mohd Noor

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal self-attention architecture for emergency triage that jointly models textual presenting complaints and numerical vital signs from electronic health records. It aims to capture temporal structure and cross-modal dependencies for timely prioritization.

entry.title: Examining the Associations between Visual and Non-Visual Elements and Cyclists' Route Choices for Various Trip Purposes

author.name: Heyang Hua, Koichi Ito, Filip Biljecki

entry.summary: This study examines how visual (street-view) and non-visual (socioeconomic) factors relate to cyclists' route choices for different trip purposes in Montreal. It combines spatiotemporal analysis with street-view image perception.

entry.title: Adaptive Contrast Enhancement and Optimised Feature Matching for RootSIFT-Based Palm-Vein Recognition

author.name: Kaveen Perera, Fouad Khelifi, Ammar Belatreche

entry.summary: This work proposes an intensity-limited adaptive contrast stretching method with bidirectional Gaussian-weighted overlapping tiles to enhance low-contrast palm-vein images, combined with RootSIFT features and distance-based filtering. It improves a secure biometric recognition modality.

entry.title: How to Build Marcus's Algebraic Mind: From Minsky's Emotion-Machine Viewpoint

author.name: Hiroyuki Chuma, Kanji Otsuka, Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: This companion paper reads the VaCoAl hyperdimensional architecture through Minsky's Emotion-Machine framework, presenting exact reversible variable binding, compositional bundling, and individual/kind separation with a collision-avoidance scheme. It reports implementations scaling to millions of records.

entry.title: Optimization of sim-to-real transfer in the humanoid robot NICO

author.name: Juraj Gavura, Igor Farka\v{s}

entry.summary: This paper extends a low-cost haptic calibration method from reaching to tabletop grasping on the humanoid robot NICO by adding YOLO-based object and hand detection and stereo vision localization with the robot's built-in fisheye cameras. It corrects small sim-to-real positioning errors that prevent successful grasping.

entry.title: The World According to a Social Robot -- Augmenting Human-Robot Dialogue With Vision Language Models

author.name: Thomas Sievers

entry.summary: This paper reports initial experiences applying a Mistral language model with a Pepper robot to augment human-robot dialogue with visual information from vision-language models, investigating how added visual context affects response time across models. It focuses on situational understanding appropriate to human customs for social robots.

entry.title: Current Limitations of LLMs

author.name: Eigenbraid

entry.summary: A survey of current LLM limitations as of mid-2026, emphasizing reliability as the main obstacle and using METR task-success-rate charts to argue that reliability gaps are the key barometer for timelines. The author contends today's models are far from posing world-domination risk but that closing these gaps would change that.

entry.title: Identity-Consistent Expression Fields: A Disentangled Neural Radiance Field Framework for Few-Shot Facial Expression Synthesis

author.name: Minh Tran

entry.summary: Identity-Consistent Expression Fields disentangle a static identity-specific radiance component from a dynamic expression-conditioned component in NeRF-based few-shot facial expression synthesis. This reduces identity drift when animating faces toward unseen expressions.

entry.title: A Predict-then-Correct Loop Based on Few-Shot Continuous Contextual Bandit for Demand Forecasting

author.name: Zhiwei Lei, Benedict Jun Ma, Ilya Jackson

entry.summary: This paper proposes a predict-then-correct framework for retail demand forecasting that keeps a first-stage ML forecast and applies a few-shot continuous contextual bandit correction with similar-SKU augmentation and top-p masked updates. It reports statistically significant error reductions on Walmart and beverage data.

entry.title: Autonomous VR-Based Risk Detection for Situational Awareness in Dangerous Settings

author.name: Mohammad Eskandari, Murali Krishna Varma Indukuri, Stephanie M. Lukin, Cynthia Matuszek

entry.summary: This paper presents a VR-based human-robot interaction framework in which a robot queries a vision-language model to identify and annotate hazards in simulated dangerous environments, presenting them to a human operator through an immersive interface. It studies VLM-assisted situational awareness for disaster response.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided NSGA-II Enhanced with Gray Relational Coefficient for Multi-Objective Optimization: Application to NASDAQ Portfolio Optimization

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang, Qinxu Ding, Ding Ding, Siying Zhu, Jing Ren, Yue Wang, Chong Hui Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes an RL-guided NSGA-II enhanced with gray relational coefficients for constrained multi-objective optimization, applied to NASDAQ portfolio risk-return trade-offs. An RL agent adapts evolutionary parameters online using hypervolume, feasibility, and diversity metrics.

entry.title: Endogenous Alignment

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: This post draws an analogy between how humans align children through exogenous conditioning versus the endogenous self-regulation expected of adults, and applies it to thinking about AI alignment. It argues for attending to endogenous alignment mechanisms rather than only external control.

entry.title: FST.ai 2.5: Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware AI for Olympic and Para-Taekwondo Decision Support, Athlete Digital Twins, and Federation-Scale Analytics

author.name: Keivan Shariatmadar, Ahmad Osman, Ramin Rey

entry.summary: FST.ai 2.5 is an explainable, uncertainty-aware AI framework for Olympic and Para-Taekwondo integrating referee decision support, athlete digital twins, and federation-scale analytics into a unified ecosystem. It targets fragmentation in current sports AI solutions.

entry.title: DAUPNet: Domain-Aware Uncertainty Modeling for Reliable Prototype Discrimination in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Lei Yuan, Zhongxu Hu, Jingyi Wen, Pengxing Yi

entry.summary: DAUPNet reformulates cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation as uncertainty-aware prototype discrimination, harmonizing hierarchical features and modeling boundary/appearance ambiguity with probabilistic prototypes. It aims to make prototype matching reliable under large domain shifts.

entry.title: Signal-based Model Access Risk Analysis for AI System Operations Security

author.name: Maria Mahbub, Steven Young, Amir Sadovnik, Edmon Begoli, Chris Rugenstein, Donald Coulter, Anthony Ayodele

entry.summary: This paper proposes a signal-based framework for analyzing model-access risk in deployed AI systems, organizing evasion and extraction attacks by the concrete signals adversaries observe rather than the coarse white/gray/black-box taxonomy. It aims to better characterize attack surfaces across varied exposure levels.

entry.title: Bluedot SF hackathon submission: A workable blueprint for a chip licensing regime

author.name: edpaulino

entry.summary: A hackathon-winning submission outlines a chip licensing regime for policymakers, focused on bootstrapping Flexible Hardware-Enabled Guarantees (flexHEG) and identifying which actors and legal rulemaking paths could accelerate compute governance. The author flags it as preliminary, half-a-day work not vetted by export-control experts.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Dropout Uncertainty and Entropy-Thresholded Selective Prediction for Architecture-Agnostic Brain Tumor MRI Triage

author.name: Medhansh Sharma

entry.summary: This work proposes an uncertainty-first pipeline for four-class brain tumor MRI that uses Monte Carlo Dropout entropy to defer uncertain cases to humans, arguing deterministic confidence heads collapse to uninformative outputs. It emphasizes trustworthy selective prediction over raw accuracy.

entry.title: Privacy-Aware Synthetic Video Benchmarking and Relational Evaluation for Worker-Under-Suspended-Load Detection

author.name: Anshu Singh, Alejandro Seif

entry.summary: SynthSite is a synthetic video benchmark for detecting workers under suspended loads, a relational construction hazard, together with a privacy-aware hybrid generation workflow supporting shareable and privacy-constrained data. It studies whether worker appearance can be suppressed without harming hazard detection.

entry.title: When to Use Which? Benchmarking Optimisers for Configurable Systems under Varying Budgets

author.name: Chao Jiang, Yulong Ye, Tao Chen, Miqing Li

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks configuration-tuning optimizers for software systems across varying measurement budgets, showing that the best optimizer depends heavily on the available budget and system measurement cost. It provides guidance on which optimizer to choose given a budget level.

entry.title: ReqGenX: An Empirical Study of Atomic Decomposition, Artifact Regeneration, and Reconstruction for Legacy SRS Documents

author.name: Ragib Shahariar Ayon, Rayed Fahmi, Sumon Biswas, Shibbir Ahmed

entry.summary: ReqGenX is an empirical pipeline that decomposes legacy software requirements specifications into source-grounded atomic statements, routes them to standards-inspired artifact types via multi-LLM plurality voting, and regenerates traceable synthetic pre-SRS artifacts. It enables fine-grained evaluation of LLM-based requirements generation.

entry.title: TellTale: Blending Multi-Instance LoRA Text Encoders and a Zero-Shot LLM Judge for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition in Videos

author.name: Abdel-Karim Al-Tamimi, Ali Rodan

entry.summary: TellTale is a text-only approach to ambivalence and hesitancy recognition in interview videos that blends two LoRA-fine-tuned text encoders under a multiple-instance learning objective with a zero-shot quantized LLM judge stream. It relies solely on transcripts for the BAH dataset challenge.

entry.title: EA-RMENet -- Path Loss Prediction in Urban Environments using Deep Learning

author.name: Jonathan O'Shea (DCU School of Electronic Engineering), Conor Brennan (DCU School of Electronic Engineering)

entry.summary: EA-RMENet is a U-Net with an EfficientNet encoder, attention-gated skip connections, and atrous spatial pyramid pooling for image-driven urban path-loss radio-map estimation. It aims to balance accuracy and computational efficiency in wireless network planning.

entry.title: Compact convolutional neural networks for AI-based drone detection system

author.name: G\'abor Farkas, G\'abor Fazekas, Karakai Patrik, Andr\'as N\'emeth, G\'abor Farkas

entry.summary: This study designs lightweight convolutional networks to detect drone radio-frequency video-transmitter emissions rendered as time-domain images, for compact electronic-warfare detection in complex electromagnetic environments. It targets embedded, computationally efficient deployment.

entry.title: Graph-Embedded Intuitionistic Fuzzy Broad Learning System: A Multi-view Framework

author.name: Yogesh Kumar, Manju, Mudasir Ganaie

entry.summary: MVGIFBLS integrates multi-view learning, graph embedding, and intuitionistic fuzzy theory into a Broad Learning System to reduce sensitivity to noise and outliers while modeling geometric data structure and multiple sources. It aims for more discriminative representations than standard BLS.

entry.title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO

author.name: Anastasiya Ihnatovich, Igor Farka\v{s}

entry.summary: This work develops a system for imitating human arm gestures on the semi-humanoid robot NICO using analytical geometry and a pretrained MediaPipe pose-estimation model, computing joint angles from detected 3D landmarks and mapping them to the robot's motors. It supports gesture imitation for human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Algorithmic Accuracy as a Motivational Driver in Robot-Mediated Learning: A Comparative Study of Cross-Correlation and CNN-Based Sound Detection in an Interactive Quiz Game

author.name: Rezaul Tutul, Ilona Buchem, Niels Pinkwart

entry.summary: This between-subjects study with forty students investigates whether the accuracy of sound-detection algorithms (a CNN versus cross-correlation) in a Pepper-robot-hosted quiz game affects student motivation, testing the link between algorithmic accuracy and perceived fairness and competence. It examines robot-mediated learning outcomes.

entry.title: From wantons to moral agents

author.name: Michele Campolo

entry.summary: A theoretical alignment piece exploring whether a class of reasoning agents converges on shared basic moral principles after enough knowledge and reflection, and focusing on the mechanisms by which agents transition from unreflective 'wantons' to moral agents. It builds on the author's prior moral-realism-adjacent arguments.

entry.title: K-IPO: Kendall-constrained Importance Preserving Oversampling for Imbalanced Tabular Data

author.name: Marios Tyrovolas, Argiris Sofotasios, Dimitris Metaxakis, Georgios Mermigkis, George Georgoulas, Panagiotis Hadjidoukas, Chrysostomos Stylios

entry.summary: K-IPO is a generator-agnostic generate-then-select oversampling framework for imbalanced tabular data that accepts synthetic minority samples only if they preserve the original feature-importance ranking above a Kendall-tau threshold. It aims to prevent oversampling from distorting model explanations.

entry.title: Mitigating Compiler Fusion-Induced Power Bursts in Mobile NPU Inference as the Battery Depletes

author.name: Ryoga Yuzawa, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: This measurement study on a commercial smartphone shows that aggressive operator fusion in a mobile NPU compiler creates monolithic superlayers whose concentrated execution causes peak-current bursts and voltage droop, triggering DVFS latency as the battery depletes. It evaluates a black-box mitigation.

entry.title: Hierarchical Specialised Ensembles for Classification of Zebrafish Phenotypes Using the Selected Image Recognition Methods

author.name: Piotr S. Maci\k{a}g, Monika Maci\k{a}g, Magdalena Majdan

entry.summary: This work evaluates three hierarchical ensemble setups for classifying zebrafish embryo phenotypes across ResNet18, ViT, and ConvNeXt backbones. ConvNeXt performs best overall, with a specialized hierarchical ensemble giving the best F1 balance.

entry.title: Bluedot Technical AI Safety Puzzle, submission that got me a second place

author.name: perduta

entry.summary: A newcomer to technical AI safety shares their second-place BlueDot puzzle solution involving a frozen MiniLM encoder with a small trained head predicting sentence features. It is primarily an accessible educational writeup of interpretability probing rather than novel research.

entry.title: Boundary-Seeking GAN-Augmented TabTransformer for Adversarially Robust Intrusion Detection

author.name: Raihan Sultan Pasha Basuki, Aliyah Kurniasih

entry.summary: This paper augments a TabTransformer with a Boundary-Seeking GAN for flow-based intrusion detection, using the GAN both to synthesize minority-class samples and to generate adversarial samples for robustness evaluation. It reports improved macro-F1 on CICIDS2017.

entry.title: A Quantum-Classical Hybrid Framework for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting Complexity-Fidelity Trade-offs and Limitations

author.name: Sanjay Chakraborty, Fredrik Heintz

entry.summary: This work presents a quantum-classical hybrid framework for multi-horizon multivariate time-series forecasting with a fixed reservoir variant and a variational variant, encoding signals via angle encoding and cross-channel entanglement. It analyzes complexity-fidelity tradeoffs under NISQ constraints.

entry.title: Back to the museum: Investigation of the acceptance of Android Andrea with and without emotion simulation in a museum

author.name: Marcel Heisler, Christian Becker-Asano

entry.summary: This study reports a second museum deployment of the autonomous android robot Andrea holding multilingual conversations with visitors, comparing acceptance across no-emotion, ChatGPT-determined emotion, and other emotion-simulation conditions. It examines how emotion simulation affects visitor perception of a humanlike robot.

entry.title: I wanted it to feel more personal: Customization of social AI as AI individualism in practice

author.name: Marita Skjuve, Anna Gr{\o}ndal Larsen, Asbj{\o}rn F{\o}lstad, Nena van As, Petter Bae Brandtzaeg

entry.summary: A qualitative study of 169 users examines why and how people customize social AI like chatbots, introducing an AI-individualism lens with seven motivations from emotional support to self-extension. It is an HCI-oriented analysis rather than a technical contribution.

entry.title: Reliable Remediation Impact Prediction for Black-Box Security Ratings

author.name: Nada Hanad, Mehdi Acheli, Ali NourEldin, Mohamed Sellami, Walid Gaaloul

entry.summary: This paper proposes a surrogate model for predicting how candidate remediation actions affect black-box security ratings while limiting information leakage about the hidden scoring engine. It explicitly models checkpoint applicability and reliability of predictions.

entry.title: Berkeley and Heiserman as an Unexhausted Architecture for Embodied Machine Intelligence

author.name: Christopher A. Tucker

entry.summary: This is a historical and conceptual essay revisiting Edmund Berkeley's writings on symbolic logic as a design language for machines that acquire and organize information over time. It argues his program offers an unexhausted architecture for embodied machine intelligence.

entry.title: AI 2027 as Sci-Fi

author.name: strangematterSF

entry.summary: This essay proposes reading the AI 2027 and AI 2040 forecasting narratives as hard science fiction to expose their load-bearing assumptions, such as the literal belief in recursive self-improvement leading to superintelligence. It is a literary-critical framing of prominent AI timeline scenarios.

entry.title: Agentic ERP: Multi-Agent Large Language Model Architecture for Autonomous Enterprise Resource Planning

author.name: Zhihao Liu, Tianyu Wang, Xi Vincent Wang, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.17331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems record transactions reliably but still delegate almost all operational decision-making to human specialists,...

entry.title: DeeperRadar: End-to-End MIMO Radar Design and Multi-Modal Fusion for Autonomous Vehicle Perception

author.name: Eli Goldenshluger, Barak Pinkovich, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.17351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DeeperRadar is a radar-centric, sensor-stack-conditioned framework that co-designs radar sensing and multi-modal 3D detection for autonomous mobility b...

entry.title: Self-Modifying Lean Proof Agents with Verifier-Grounded Benchmark Coevolution

author.name: Yuqing Li, Zeguan Wu, Yu Gan, Junyu Liu

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.17352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing effective Lean proof agents is a central challenge in formal mathematical reasoning. Beyond building stronger provers, recent work emphasizes...

entry.title: Quantifying Diversity of Thought: A Predictive Law of Weighted LLM Ensemble Lift

author.name: Junade Ali

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.17384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides an experimentally verified formal law for calculating the uplift that diversity of thought provides in Large Language Model (LLM) e...

entry.title: Intermittent Control Is Not Diluted Control: A Switching Effect in Artificial Agency

author.name: Veronique Ziegler

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.17432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive agents do not always regulate under the same timing conditions. Sometimes stabilization can begin before a disturbance has fully entered the i...

entry.title: Technical Design Review of Duke Robotics Club's Oogway & Crush: AUVs for RoboSub 2026

author.name: Patrick Zheng, Saagar Arya, Hung Le, Mathew Chu, Nathanael Ren, Niko Weaver, Isabella Chen, Jill Wang, Raine Cheng, Siddharth Kini, Avrick Altmann, Srinath Iyer, Ivan Chen, Ian Suh, Parker Jones, Pierson Jones, Sebastian deSouza, Suhaani Sriram, Suvas Aggarwal

entry.summary: This is a technical design review of the Duke Robotics Club's two autonomous underwater vehicles for the RoboSub 2026 competition, describing mechanical, electrical, and software improvements across movement, vision, manipulation, and acoustic tracking. It documents reliability investments such as added thrusters, a CFD-optimized case, and a redesigned acoustics system.

entry.title: Against the AI framing multiverse: Introducing AI StopWatch

author.name: tanagrabeast

entry.summary: Part of MIRI's comms team introduces AI StopWatch, an experimental newsroom aimed at countering the fragmented, contradictory framing of AI in mainstream media by grounding coverage in shared facts. It is a project announcement about AI communication.

entry.title: Stop doing decision theory without metaphysics

author.name: Elias Schmied

entry.summary: A rant arguing that debates over Functional Decision Theory in blackmail-style scenarios cannot be resolved without engaging underlying metaphysics, particularly for agents already being blackmailed or newly created AIs. It surveys several routes to justify FDT's recommendation.

entry.title: DMFNet: Dual-Backbone Multiscale Fusion Network for Urban Scene Classification

author.name: Anamitra Ghosh, Abhiroop Chatterjee, Susmita Ghosh

entry.summary: DMFNet is a dual-backbone multiscale fusion network with residual feature propagation and spatial attention for remote-sensing urban scene classification. It targets multiscale interaction and robustness under high intra-class variability.

entry.title: Copy of my FLF Epistemic Case Study Competition

author.name: Bruce Lewis

entry.summary: A contest submission to FLF's Epistemic Case Study Competition presenting a methodology and tool (Epistack-HowTruthful) with agent skills for ingesting and improving arguments so reasoning is easy to scrutinize. It is a competition entry describing an epistemic-tooling approach.

entry.title: The Infinity Fallacy

author.name: pvutov

entry.summary: This post names an 'Infinity Fallacy', the failure mode of endlessly accumulating resources without an adequate spending phase, illustrated with game strategy, effective-altruism pledges, resource extraction, and taxation timing. It is a general decision-making essay rather than AI research.

entry.title: Building a Neural Network from Scratch: Implementation, Evaluation, and Optimization

author.name: Yuanzhe Jia

entry.summary: This paper implements a self-contained neural network framework entirely from scratch without automatic differentiation or prebuilt modules, covering multilayer architectures, activations, regularization, and modern optimizers. It serves primarily as a pedagogical tool for understanding forward and backward propagation.

entry.title: Amazon Music's Artist Conflation

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A personal account of Amazon Music's poor recommendation and artist-conflation problems, noting that a small cheap LLM like Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite or Claude Haiku 4.5 could plausibly do better. It is anecdotal product critique.

entry.title: People might start believing in radical life extension soon

author.name: bits

entry.summary: The author speculates that public belief in radical life extension could flip suddenly, driven by trends like a widened Overton window, and that such a belief cascade would change behavior around retirement, investment, and childbearing. It concerns social expectation dynamics rather than AI.

entry.title: War – What is it Good For?

author.name: kqr

entry.summary: A review of Bruce Bueno de Mesquita's The War Trap, praising its expected-utility model of war as parsimonious, counterintuitive in its assumptions, yet empirically predictive. It is a book discussion about political science modeling, not AI.

entry.title: A requiem to the plan-vanilla Google search: On Sam Roweis, Mbappe and an Irish bar world cup watch party

author.name: Triadic diss-closures

entry.summary: A discursive personal essay laments the LLM-ification of Google search, arguing that prompt brittleness has bled into search-query brittleness, woven around anecdotes about a mentor, soccer, and a bar hallucination incident. It is reflective commentary rather than technical analysis.

entry.title: Adderall Tolerance: Much More Than You Wanted To Know

author.name: Kurt H. Pieper
