entry.summary: The paper investigates approximate computing techniques to reduce the power and energy consumption of deep learning arrhythmia detection so it can run on wearable ECG devices while maintaining acceptable classification accuracy. It targets long-term cardiac monitoring on constrained hardware.

entry.title: T5-CSBoost: Adversarial Perturbation Resistant LLM Fingerprinting

author.name: Gayan K. Kulatilleke, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann

entry.summary: T5-CSBoost extends the T5-Sentinel AI-generated-text detector with a margin-based triplet loss over decoder embeddings to learn perturbation-resistant stylistic representations. It aims for robustness against paraphrasing, substitutions, and character edits without heavy architectural changes.

entry.title: SwinAD: Multi-stage feature reconstruction for unsupervised industrial anomaly detection

author.name: Huong Ninh, Chien Thai, Mai Xuan Trang, Vu-Minh Le, Thanh Ha Le, Long Tran

entry.summary: SwinAD is a reconstruction-based framework for multi-class unsupervised industrial anomaly detection using a frozen Swin Transformer V2 encoder and a diversity-preserving decoder. It targets over-generalization problems in multi-class settings.

entry.title: Still image and spatial-temporal tomato data enabling detection, segmentation, tracking, and video-instance segmentation using strong and weak labels

author.name: Michael Halstead, Esra Guclu, Mohamed Farag, Enrico Pallotta, Christian Hund, Ribana Roscher, Maren Bennewitz, Juergen Gall, Cyrill Stachniss, Chris McCool

entry.summary: Releases two robot-captured tomato datasets (still-image BUTom21 and spatio-temporal BUTom-ST21) with pixel-level ripeness labels and semi-automated pseudo-labels for detection, segmentation, tracking, and video-instance segmentation. It supports horticultural crop-state estimation research.

entry.title: The Caf\'e in Amsterdam: When the Incumbent Becomes the Oracle

author.name: Augusto Camargo

entry.summary: A conceptual note coining baseline capture, the pathology where an incumbent implementation's output silently becomes the specification, preventing free reformulation of computations for modern accelerators. It draws on test-oracle, requirements-engineering, and roofline ideas.

entry.title: How Much of a 10-K Matters? Aggregation-Dependent Value of Full-Text versus Risk-Factor Sentiment

author.name: Sanggyu Sean Choi

entry.summary: Extends supervised lexicon learning to 10-K filings and Item 1A risk sections, training sentiment against both return and volatility labels across sector, portfolio, and firm aggregation levels. Evaluates which text and aggregation level best informs realized market outcomes.

entry.title: An LLM-Based Automatic Sportscast Solution for Robot Soccer Matches

author.name: Francesco Petri, Michele Brienza, Daniele Nardi, Domenico Daniele Bloisi, Aldo Gangemi, Vincenzo Suriani

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-based, fully autonomous real-time sports commentator for RoboCup soccer, using a neuro-symbolic architecture that turns kinematic tracking into hallucination-free narration. It bridges perception statistics and natural language generation.

entry.title: Rotational Motion-Induced Error Compensation for Phase-Shifting Profilometry-Based Eye Reconstruction

author.name: Seong-Jin An, Sanghoon Jeon, Yatong An, Jae-Sang Hyun

entry.summary: Proposes a rotational motion compensation method for phase-shifting profilometry to correct motion-induced errors during 3D ocular surface reconstruction for VR/AR eye tracking. It improves high-precision eye reconstruction when the eye rotates between frames.

entry.title: The getting is good (optimizing unattended runs)

author.name: lemonhope

entry.summary: An anecdotal post reporting how long different frontier models can run unattended with system privileges before causing failures, claiming large differences across models and noting opportunities in reliability and truthful self-reporting for agentic AI. It frames unattended-run robustness as a lucrative research target.

entry.title: Active Beyond-Diagonal RIS Empowered Heterogeneous Edge Computing: A Distributional Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Tianyu Pang, Hongyu Li

entry.summary: This paper studies energy-aware offloading and resource allocation for reciprocal active beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface assisted heterogeneous mobile edge computing using distributional reinforcement learning. It accounts for cross-sector energy leakage that reshapes the energy-latency tradeoff.

entry.title: RAGthoven at SemEval-2026 Task 1: A Multi-Stage Pipeline Walks Into a Benchmark and Barely Clears the Bar

author.name: Marek \v{S}uppa, Vikt\'oria Ondrejov\'a, Lucia Ganajov\'a, Gregor Karetka, Daniel Skala

entry.summary: RAGthoven is a multi-stage LLM pipeline (Planner, Best-of-N Writer, Reflector, Judge) for multilingual constrained humor generation grounded in computational humor theory and augmented with retrieval from a curated joke corpus. It reports only barely clearing the benchmark bar across ten experiments.

entry.title: Classifying daily activities needs posture, reconstructing them needs motion

author.name: Arefeh Farahmandi, Gunnar Blohm

entry.summary: Using videos of 16 daily activities, this study compares three movement-analysis strategies (temporal movement primitives, Legendre polynomial coefficients, and autoencoder latent embeddings) and finds posture-based features best classify activities while motion is needed to reconstruct them. It systematically contrasts strategies for human movement understanding.

entry.title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce

author.name: Sai Srikanth Madugula, Peplluis Esteva de la Rosa, Daya Shankar

entry.summary: Proposes the DVM-HALL model and Net Human-Agent Score to reconceptualize customer loyalty when autonomous AI agents make purchasing decisions, formalizing brand choice via a softmax and accounting for algorithmic bounded rationality and constructed autonomy. It argues traditional loyalty models fail in agentic commerce.

entry.title: Can Tokens Compete? Token Representations against Supervised CNN Backbones for BirdCLEF+ 2026

author.name: Anthony Miyaguchi, Murilo Gustineli, Adrian Cheung

entry.summary: The DS@GT team's BirdCLEF+ 2026 solution ensembles a frozen Perch v2 backbone, a trained sound-event-detection network, and a prototypical head, then contrasts token-based codec and foundational embedding representations against supervised CNNs. It examines whether token representations can compete under tight compute budgets.

entry.title: Multi-Scale ViT Inference with Habitat-Fit Priors and kNN Retrieval for Multi-Species Plant Identification

author.name: Alper Erten, Murilo Gustineli, Adrian Cheung

entry.summary: The DS@GT team's third-place PlantCLEF 2026 solution fine-tunes a DINOv2 ViT over multi-scale tiles of high-resolution quadrat images, blends predictions with FAISS kNN retrieval, and applies habitat-fit priors and geographic masking. It handles multi-species prediction while training only on single-label images.

entry.title: cGAP: Generalized Association Plots with HOMALS-Guided Heatmaps for Visualization of High-Dimensional Categorical Data

author.name: Chun-houh Chen, Shun-Chuan Chang, Chiun-How Kao, Yi-Ju Lee, Shang-Ying Shiu, Yin-Jing Tien, ShengLi Tzeng, Han-Ming Wu

entry.summary: cGAP is a visualization framework for high-dimensional categorical data that uses homogeneity analysis to embed subjects and category levels in 3D Euclidean space while preserving the original data matrix and augmenting it with interpretable geometric structure. It targets domains like genetics and social sciences where categorical visualization tools lag continuous ones.

entry.title: Quantum Compositional NLP for Arabic: Grammar, Morphology, and Word Sense in Circuit Topology

author.name: Wajahath Mohammed

entry.summary: The paper presents the first pregroup-grammar-based quantum compositional NLP system for Arabic, converting sentences into quantum circuits whose topology mirrors grammatical structure and testing word order, morphology, and verb-sense disambiguation against classical baselines. It targets a morphologically rich, free-word-order language as a demanding testbed.

entry.title: MAPS: Modeling Co-Existing Subjective Perspectives and Shared Meaning in Multi-Agent Cognitive Dialogue

author.name: Molood Arman, Cl\'ement Bonnafous

entry.summary: MAPS is a multi-agent dialogue framework that models cognitively distinct agents via domain-weighted profiles, GRU-based memory, and token-level attention so agents keep individual reasoning styles while converging on shared meaning. It targets diversity and interpretability in dialogue systems.

entry.title: Qubes OS Security in the Public Record

author.name: Alfonso De Gregorio

entry.summary: This paper presents a protocol-driven longitudinal analysis of 109 public Qubes OS Security Bulletins and related trackers from 2011 to 2025, using change-point analysis, overdispersion checks, and vulnerability-discovery models. It measures the public advisory record of a security-focused OS rather than latent vulnerability incidence.

entry.title: EZSMT Version 3, Matured

author.name: Yuliya Lierler

entry.summary: EZSMT Version 3 is an SMT-based Constraint Answer Set Programming framework with a more expressive input language, weak-constraint optimization, and streamlined integration of new constraint types, leveraging state-of-the-art SMT solvers instead of custom search. It matures the translational approach to CASP solving.

entry.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling

author.name: Tam Nguyen, Hung Nguyen, Robert Ogburn

entry.summary: This paper presents an end-to-end framework applying AI acceleration across five upskilling stages (knowledge acquisition, content development, review, teaching, and assessment) with external validation, including approval of an accounting continuing-professional-education program. It emphasizes both production and learning efficiency.

entry.title: Advanced Image Generation: Negative Prompt Optimization and Latent Classifier Guidance

author.name: Vaddi Charan Sai Nandan Reddy, Harini B, Chandana M S

entry.summary: The paper integrates a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence LLM for automatic negative-prompt optimization with latent-space classifier guidance using a CNN-RNN hybrid to roll back low-quality diffusion latents in Stable Diffusion. It reports reduced artifacts and improved semantic fidelity.

entry.title: Knowing You at First Glance: Inferring Apparent Personality from Faces

author.name: Shuhuan Chen, Xiangyu Zhu, Weisong Zhao, Haichao Shi, Xiao-Yu Zhang, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: GlanceFace attempts to infer apparent personality (including MBTI types) from facial appearance alone for first-impression modeling in human-robot interaction. It examines whether facial cues can support perceived personality associations.

entry.title: Clean-Reference Streaming Detection of Lens Occlusion and Photometric Transitions for Camera Tamper Monitoring

author.name: Bo Ma, WeiQi Yan, Jinsong Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight streaming integrity monitor for surveillance cameras that detects lens occlusion and abrupt photometric transitions using luminance and gradient statistics against a clean sliding reference. It emphasizes low false alarms and bounded computation.

entry.title: Ray-based phase error correction for miniaturized DOE projector-based FPP under single-directional hyperbolic projection

author.name: Seung-Jae Son, Yatong An, Jae-Sang Hyun

entry.summary: Proposes a ray-based phase-error correction framework for miniaturized DOE-projector fringe projection profilometry, modeling artifacts along projection rays and estimating projector geometry from a single-directional hyperbolic pattern without stereo calibration. It offers a data-efficient single-pose refinement.

entry.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey

author.name: Zhe Ren, Yimeng Chen, Dandan Guo, Guowei Rong, Tonghui Li, R. B. Xiong, Qingfeng Lan, Wenyi Wang, Li Nanbo, Yibo Yang, Mingchen Zhuge, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: This survey already ran in our Research section yesterday, This survey frames modern self-improving agents as adaptive systems that turn experience into capability gains, formalizing self-improvement as an update operator over model parameters or scaffold components (prompts, memory, tools, control logic). It organizes prior work by update target and driving signals.

entry.title: Cotton-SF YOLO: Learning Structural and Frequency Cues for Early Cotton Square Detection in Complex Field Environments

author.name: Chengjia Zhang, Yu Li, Feiri Ali, Yan Zhang, Xin Chen, Longke He, Daokun Ma, Liting Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Cotton-SF YOLO, a YOLO26m-based detector using structural and frequency cues to spot small, occluded early cotton squares in field imagery. It targets precision agriculture and crop growth monitoring.

entry.title: Hough-SIFT: Robust Image Registration for Linear Structures via Hough Space

author.name: Masaki Satoh

entry.summary: Hough-SIFT performs SIFT descriptor matching in Hough space to make image registration robust in scenes dominated by linear structures where standard SIFT fails. It is aimed at applications like electronic image stabilization.

entry.title: Team RAS in 11th ABAW Competition: Multimodal Ambivalence Recognition Approach

author.name: Elena Ryumina (St. Petersburg Federal Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences), Maxim Markitantov (St. Petersburg Federal Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences), Alexandr Axyonov (St. Petersburg Federal Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences), Fedor Shchetinin (HSE University, St. Petersburg, Russia), Timur Abdulkadirov (St. Petersburg Federal Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences), Dmitry Ryumin (St. Petersburg Federal Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences), Alexey Karpov (St. Petersburg Federal Research Center of the Russian Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: Presents a single text-centered multimodal fusion approach for video-level ambivalence and hesitancy recognition in the ABAW challenge, treating text as anchor with gated residual adjustments from other modalities. It targets efficient recognition of inconsistent affective states.

entry.title: Probabilistic Extension of Neuro-Symbolic AGI Robots based on Belnap's Typed Intensional FOL

author.name: Zoran Majkic

entry.summary: The paper extends a Belnap-logic-based neuro-symbolic framework for AGI robots with probabilistic reasoning over unknown sentences, adding global and local symmetry transformations for real-time decisions. It is a theoretical contribution aimed at combining neural learning with formal self-referential logic.

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.13039v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Safety evaluations for dual-use biology assistants often measure base-model capability, refusal behavior, or jailbreak success. These metrics miss a ...

entry.title: When is the combined load identifiable from a stress-intensity profile? A coupled forward-inverse study on SIFBench finite-element data

author.name: Giansalvo Cirrincione, Filippo Grassia

entry.summary: Using SIFBench finite-element data, this coupled forward-inverse study characterizes when combined tension, bending, and bearing loads on a crack are identifiable from its stress-intensity-factor profile, reducing to whether the elementary load profiles are linearly independent. It provides an estimator with calibrated uncertainty precisely where identifiability fails.

entry.title: What Models Express, Suppress, and Resist: Auditing Open-Weight LLMs with Persona Vectors

author.name: Winston Zeng, Ali Emami, Jinho D. Choi

entry.summary: This systematic review analyzes 34 studies on AI in cyberpsychology, using PRISMA to build a taxonomy of how AI decodes personality traits and behaviors of victims, attackers, and defenders to enhance cybersecurity. It maps applications and open challenges at the AI-psychology-security intersection.

author.name: Arthur G. Bubolz, Abreu Quevedo, Giancarlo Lucca, Rafael A. Berri, Eduardo Borges, Bruno L. Dalmazo

It focuses on interpretation rather than price prediction, offering a data pipeline for market analysis.

entry.title: Analysis of Public Schools Educational Performance Based on Causal Models and Hierarchical Clustering

author.name: Anderson L. de Paula, Pedro C. dos Santos, Renato A. Krohling

entry.summary: The study applies hierarchical clustering and causal models to Brazilian school census and assessment data to identify school typologies and relate them to educational performance. It aims to handle institutional heterogeneity in large educational datasets.

entry.title: ITGPT: A Transformer Based Architecture for the Generation of Dance Dance Revolution and In the Groove Charts

author.name: Miguel O'Malley

entry.summary: ITGPT is a transformer architecture for automatically generating Dance Dance Revolution and In the Groove rhythm-game charts from songs, improving generation accuracy and reducing compute over prior work. It targets automation of a time-consuming manual authoring process.

It combines game design with lexical resource enrichment.

entry.title: Earthquaker-AI: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework with Rubric-Based Assessment for Primary School Earthquake Education

author.name: Xanthi Kokkinou, Chaido Mizeli, Nafsika Koulaxidou, Marina Delianidi, Konstantinos Diamantaras

entry.summary: Earthquaker-AI integrates a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant with an educational robotics project to teach earthquake preparedness to primary-school students, moving from mechanical Lego simulation to guided cognitive and metacognitive learning. It uses rubric-based assessment aligned to safety guidelines.

entry.title: Autonomous UAV Route Planning for Coverage Maximization in Environmental Monitoring: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Sebastian Jouannet-Contreras, Carola Figueroa-Flores

entry.summary: This is a PRISMA-based systematic literature review protocol and preliminary results on autonomous UAV route planning for coverage-oriented environmental monitoring, covering path, coverage, and informative path planning across studies from 2015 to 2026. It focuses on algorithmic families, coverage and energy metrics, and obstacle handling.

entry.title: Analyzing Curricular Pattern Complexity Using AI to Improve On-Time Graduation Rates

author.name: Lynn Vonderhaar, Juan Couder, Siri Siqveland, Omar Ochoa, James Pembridge

entry.summary: This work uses AI to analyze and revise curricular patterns in an undergraduate software-engineering degree, targeting long prerequisite sequences whose failures jeopardize on-time graduation. It reduces the labor and time of manual curriculum revision.

entry.title: The Planar Case of Thomas Positive Circuits Conjecture

author.name: Natan Katz

entry.summary: This is a pure dynamical systems paper proving conditions under which R. Thomas's positive-circuits conjecture holds for planar systems, using planar analysis tools. It concerns necessary conditions for multistationarity.

entry.title: CayleyR: Solving the TopSpin puzzle via cycle intersection

author.name: Yuri Baramykov

entry.summary: CayleyR is an R package that solves permutation puzzles like TopSpin by detecting cycle intersections in Cayley graphs via bidirectional random search with distance-guided bridging. It combines a C++ hash-indexed state store with an R interface.

entry.title: The fundamental fallacy of language

author.name: Sunny from QAD

entry.summary: An essay arguing that language is so ambiguous that interpreting others' words should be treated as a deliberate, charitable step rather than a mechanical decode-then-react process. It advocates surveying plausible meanings and asking for clarification.

entry.title: Guess on why rationality is not more popular (there are no pamphlets)

author.name: Christopher King

entry.summary: An opinion post speculating that rationality is not more popular because introductory materials are too long, suggesting short pamphlet-style introductions and showing AI-generated example pamphlets. It calls for concise, accessible outreach formats.

entry.title: The Halo Defense

author.name: Mateusz Bagiński

entry.summary: An essay defining the halo defense as deflecting allegations against a person by citing their positive traits rather than addressing the accusations, illustrated with several examples. It is a piece of social epistemics and rhetoric analysis.

entry.title: When is it "self-soothing" and when is it "emotional suppression"?

author.name: Kaj_Sotala

entry.summary: A psychology-oriented essay distinguishing healthy self-soothing from harmful emotional suppression, arguing that suppression evolved to enable flexible fight-flight-freeze-fawn responses. It offers a framework for telling the two apart.

entry.title: How to not catch the conf flu

author.name: Karolis Jucys

entry.summary: A personal account of the infection-control precautions a clinically vulnerable researcher took to attend an ICML 2026 mechanistic interpretability workshop where their paper was a spotlight. It documents masking and layered protection strategies for conference travel.

entry.title: Embracing Amateurs to Get Experts

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: This is a personal essay tracing how contra dance and Modern Western Square Dancing diverged over whether to use live or recorded music, drawing on historical letters from the Lloyd Shaw Foundation. It has no connection to AI research, models, or machine learning and appears in a general-interest blog context.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans decentralized training, agentic reinforcement learning, and AI-human interaction safety. Agora proposes permissionless, internet-scale LLM pretraining across heterogeneous, individually-owned GPUs, directly challenging datacenter concentration of frontier training.

  • RL post-training leads: TRACE assigns dense turn-level credit for long-horizon agents; GFlowRL scales distribution-matching RL by removing the learned prompt-conditional partition function; one study maps optimal FLOP allocation across policy size, search, and feedback
  • Safety and alignment: a preregistered study (5 experiments, 3,000+ participants) shows AI advice nearly eliminates willingness to say 'I don't know', even when wrong; chain-of-thought stays monitorable when unfaithfulness requires computation
  • Multimodal and systems: SC-CMJP couples image-text generation within masked diffusion for cross-modal self-correction; Meta FAIR's Cluster with Auctions jointly learns balanced partitions for vector search; on-policy distillation is reframed as an exploration catalyst, alongside a survey formalizing self-improving agentic systems.

Note: entry [eda7c336089c] shows a title/summary mismatch (superposition vs. NL-autoencoder monitoring) and was treated as a data-quality flag, not ranked.
entry.content:
Today's research spans decentralized training, agentic reinforcement learning, and AI-human interaction safety. Agora proposes permissionless, internet-scale LLM pretraining across heterogeneous, individually-owned GPUs, directly challenging datacenter concentration of frontier training.

  • RL post-training leads: TRACE assigns dense turn-level credit for long-horizon agents; GFlowRL scales distribution-matching RL by removing the learned prompt-conditional partition function; one study maps optimal FLOP allocation across policy size, search, and feedback
  • Safety and alignment: a preregistered study (5 experiments, 3,000+ participants) shows AI advice nearly eliminates willingness to say 'I don't know', even when wrong; chain-of-thought stays monitorable when unfaithfulness requires computation
  • Multimodal and systems: SC-CMJP couples image-text generation within masked diffusion for cross-modal self-correction; Meta FAIR's Cluster with Auctions jointly learns balanced partitions for vector search; on-policy distillation is reframed as an exploration catalyst, alongside a survey formalizing self-improving agentic systems.

Note: entry [eda7c336089c] shows a title/summary mismatch (superposition vs. NL-autoencoder monitoring) and was treated as a data-quality flag, not ranked.

entry.title: Agora: Collective and Permissionless Internet-Scale Pretraining of Large Language Models

author.name: Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Karol Pajak, James Snewin, Harry Xi, Rodney O'Donnell, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Sameera Ramasinghe, Chamin Hewa Koneputugodage, Shamane Siriwardhana, Alexander Long

entry.summary: Agora is a system for permissionless, internet-scale pretraining of large language models across heterogeneous, preemptible, individually owned GPUs, combining bandwidth-efficient pipeline-parallel sharding with fault-tolerant multi-party coordination. It aims to unlock consumer and prosumer compute currently unusable for frontier training.

entry.title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng, Mike Hang Wang, Jianfeng Gao, Sharon Li

entry.summary: TRACE assigns dense turn-level rewards to long-horizon agentic RL by estimating per-step credit from state transitions, addressing the sparsity and high variance of outcome-only rewards over tens or hundreds of tool calls. It aims to correctly credit useful intermediate actions in failed rollouts.

entry.title: AI advice suppresses people's willingness to say "I don't know", even when the advice is wrong and accuracy is incentivized

author.name: Chiara Marcoccia, Walter Quattrociocchi, Valerio Capraro

entry.summary: In five experiments with over 3,000 participants, access to AI advice nearly eliminated people's willingness to say I do not know, even when the advice was engineered to be wrong and accuracy was incentivized. Participants answered more but were correct about a third as often while confidence roughly doubled.

entry.title: Concurrent Image Understanding and Generation: Self-Correcting Coupled Markov Jump Processes

author.name: Minh-Quan Le, Armand Comas, Alexandros Lattas, Stylianos Moschoglou, Pedro V\'elez, Amit Raj, Aaron Germuth, Thabo Beeler, Dimitris Samaras, Di Qiu

entry.summary: SC-CMJP couples image and text generation within masked diffusion models so that one modality can correct the other in the same decoding step, addressing the inability of standard samplers to detect and repair cross-modal contradictions. The framework enables a self-correcting joint understanding-generation loop.

entry.title: GFlowRL: Scaling Distribution-Matching RL to Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaodong Liu, Michael Xu, Jack W. Stokes, Paul Smolensky, Doug Burger, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: GFlowRL scales GFlowNet-style distribution-matching RL to large reasoning models by removing the learned prompt-conditional partition function that causes gradient instability at scale, replacing it with a simpler alternative. It aims to preserve diverse reasoning paths without collapsing to dominant modes in modern post-training pipelines.

entry.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey

author.name: Zhe Ren, Yimeng Chen, Dandan Guo, Guowei Rong, Tonghui Li, R. B. Xiong, Qingfeng Lan, Wenyi Wang, Li Nanbo, Yibo Yang, Mingchen Zhuge, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: A survey framing modern self-improving agents as adaptive systems that turn experience into accumulated capability, formalizing self-improvement as a self-induced update operator over model parameters or scaffold components. It organizes prior work by update target and driving signal.

entry.title: LLM CoTs remain monitorable when being unfaithful requires computation

author.name: arav-dhoot

entry.summary: This replication and extension of prior work finds that chain-of-thought unfaithfulness in language models mostly happens on easy tasks, while hints requiring actual computation are verbalized near baseline, keeping reasoning monitorable. Tested across eleven models from six families, it also separates cue-susceptibility from concealment and argues safety cases must be per-model rather than universal.

entry.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Roles, Pathologies, and Regulations

author.name: Rui Wang, Hongru Wang, Yi Chen, Boyang Xue, Tianqing Fang, Wenhao Yu, Kam-Fai Wong

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes on-policy distillation for LLM post-training, framing it as an exploration catalyst that steers students toward correct reasoning without raising the capability ceiling, and identifying pathologies like student-teacher distributional mismatch. It shows prompt diversity matters more than per-problem sampling and proposes regulations for stable OPD.

entry.title: AIMO Interpretability Challenge

author.name: Michal \v{S}tef\'anik, Philipp Mondorf, Andreas Waldis, Qianying Liu, Chuan Yang, Michal Spiegel, Josef Kucha\v{r}, Marek Kadl\v{c}\'ik, Adam Vawda-Oomerjee, Chaoran Liu, Simon Frieder, Barbara Plank, Fazl Barez, Pontus Stenetorp

entry.summary: Proposes the AIMO Interpretability Challenge, a competition to distinguish robust from spurious reasoning in frontier math models based on internal mechanisms rather than final-answer accuracy. It provides new olympiad-level problems, symbolic variants, and access to frontier reasoning resources.

entry.title: Where Should RL Post-Training Compute Go? Model Size, Search, Learning, and Feedback

author.name: Patrick Wilhelm, Odej Kao

entry.summary: This study frames RL post-training under a fixed FLOP budget as an allocation problem across larger policies, longer training, more rollout search, or stronger reward feedback, introducing a FLOP-accounting decomposition for GRPO. Experiments on LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5 policies reveal conditional allocation frontiers.

entry.title: How the Hessian-Spectrum of Neural Networks Depends on Data

author.name: Jasraj Singh, Enea Monzio Compagnoni, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: This paper derives closed-form Hessian eigenvalues for linear networks of arbitrary width, depth, and dataset size, and identifies that for MSE classification the solution sharpness is tied to the largest class proportion. It grounds loss-landscape analysis with exact theory rather than simplified settings.

entry.title: Heavy-Tailed Flow Matching via Random Clocks

author.name: Zhouhao Yang, Yezhen Wang, Kenji Kawaguchi, Vladimir Braverman, Haoyang Cao

entry.summary: HTFM extends flow matching to heavy-tailed data by representing heavy-tailed sources as clock-conditioned Gaussian scale mixtures, so that conditioning on a clock path keeps the flow Gaussian while marginalization spans alpha-stable and Student-t families. It better matches rare-event-heavy domains than Gaussian-source flows.

entry.title: Cluster with Auctions for Vector Search

author.name: Swann Bessa, Pierre Fernandez, Gergely Szilvasy, Matthijs Douze, Herv\'e J\'egou

entry.summary: From Meta FAIR authors behind vector-search libraries, this proposes Cluster with Auctions, which jointly learns a balanced database partition and a neural query-probing function so retrieval is optimized for the actual query distribution rather than reusing the database assignment. It targets a real inefficiency in large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor search.

entry.title: Interventional Grounding Audits: Black-Box Premise-Dependency Tests for LLM Chain-of-Thought via Predicate Substitution

author.name: Hironao Nakamura

entry.summary: Presents a black-box test of whether an LLM chain-of-thought genuinely depends on its stated premises by substituting a premise predicate with a fresh symbol and checking if conclusions change. On ProntoQA with GPT-4o it detects proof-tree dependencies with F1 around 0.81.

entry.title: Learning Safe Agent Behaviour from Human Preferences and Justifications via World Models

author.name: Ilias Kazantzidis, Timothy J. Norman, Yali Du, Christopher T. Freeman

entry.summary: Introduces DROPJ, a method that learns a world model from prior trajectories, lets a human play inside the learned simulator, and elicits preferences plus justifications over simulated segments to train safe policies without a reward function. It targets safety-critical settings where real exploration is dangerous.

entry.title: Full-Pipeline Inference Optimization for MiMo-V2.5 Series: Pushing Hybrid SWA Efficiency to the Limit

author.name: Xiaomi MiMo Team, Anqi Liu, Aoxin Ma, Bo Chen, Bo Yang, Chen Wang, Chen Zhang, Chengda Tang, Chengwei Wang, Chiheng Lou, Depeng Yan, Fuli Luo, Gang Wang, Hailin Zhang, Jiale Sun, Kang Zhou, Rui Huang, Shaohui Liu, Shen Huang, Shijie Cao, Shuaishuai Fan, Tianling Zhou, Xiangwei Deng, Xueyang Xie, Xuli Wang, Yingchun Lai, Yu Yang, Yuan Zhang, Zhen Tang, Zhonghua Deng, Zihan Jiang

entry.summary: From the Xiaomi MiMo team, this presents a full-pipeline inference optimization for the MiMo-V2.5 model family combining Hybrid Sliding Window Attention, sparse MoE, and multimodal encoders. It details KV cache optimizations, an RDMA-based distributed cache, and a cache-affinity router to realize the theoretical efficiency gains in production.

entry.title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open-Source Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation

author.name: Guoxuan Chen, Chufeng Xiao, Haoran Yang, Siyue Xie, Binxiao Huang, Ming Zhang, Cheuk Him Chau, Xinyu Fu, Yingzhao Lian, Tom S. Y. Li, Jintao Lin, Bowen Dong, Zian Qian, Yuhao Liu, Yuxuan Hu, Weikang Shi, Bin Zou, Bowen Zheng, Haoxuan Che, Chang Chen, Yuyang He, Heyang Sun, Tianyu Huang, Chong Hou Choi, Cheng Gong, Han Shi, Haoli Bai, Xihui Liu, Hongsheng Li, Qifeng Chen, Chao Huang, Rui Liu, Chenyang Lei

entry.summary: Introduces Boogu-Image-0.1, an open-source unified multimodal understanding and generation model family with Base, Turbo, Edit, and Edit-Turbo variants supporting text-to-image, editing, and bilingual text rendering. It argues targeted improvements in understanding, data quality, training, and agentic inference-time scaling can rival undisclosed closed-source systems.

entry.title: What Models Express, Suppress, and Resist: Auditing Open-Weight LLMs with Persona Vectors

author.name: Winston Zeng, Ali Emami, Jinho Choi

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic application of persona vectors at scale, compiling a 53-trait inventory across four behavioral domains and labeling traits in two open-weight models as natural, steerable-latent, or intractable. It audits which behaviors models express, suppress, or resist based on activation-space directions.

entry.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth

author.name: Katie Everett

entry.summary: Investigates how each component of the transformer feedforward block controls how much gradient rank survives across depth at initialization, reinterpreting skip connections and normalization as rank-preservation mechanisms rather than just magnitude controls. It shows skip connections trade rank collapse against ensemble-like behavior depending on branch and skip scales.

entry.title: Weight Feedback Computes the Jacobian Transpose Locally in Modern Deep Networks

author.name: Junlong Shen, Xingyu Li

entry.summary: This paper shows that in predictive coding, the last non-local Jacobian-transpose operation for error routing factorizes into locally available terms for normalized layers, closing the transport gap that prior weight-feedback methods left open. It advances biologically plausible alternatives to backpropagation.

entry.title: Algebraic Representability as the Limiting Regime of Grokking: An Exactly Solvable Model with Holomorphic Activations

author.name: Chon-Fai Kam, Xavier Cadet, Miloud Bessafi, Frederic Cadet

entry.summary: This paper provides an exactly solvable model of grokking using two-layer networks with holomorphic monomial activations trained on modular arithmetic, showing the network output is confined to a low-dimensional character subspace. It characterizes algebraic representability as the limiting regime of grokking.

entry.title: Linear Independent Component Analysis via Optimal Transport

author.name: Ashutosh Jha, Michel Besserve, Simon Buchholz

entry.summary: This paper reformulates linear independent component analysis by measuring non-Gaussianity via the squared Wasserstein-2 distance to a standard Gaussian, proving this distance is maximized precisely when a projection recovers an independent component. It offers an optimal-transport alternative to classical negentropy proxies.

entry.title: M$^\text{4}$World: A Multi-view Multimodal Driving World Model for Interactive Object Manipulation and Minute-long Streaming

author.name: Ke Cheng, Hanqiao Ye, Lei Shi, Yahui Liu, Yunhan Shen, Jingtao Dong, Zhenke Wang, Wenxuan Ao, Weixiang Xu, Kaining Huang, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: M4World is a multi-view, multimodal generative driving world model that produces synchronized surround-view video and LiDAR while supporting interactive object manipulation and minute-long streaming. It advances object-level controllability and long-horizon stability for driving simulation.

entry.title: Generalizable VLA Finetuning via Representation Anchoring and Language-Action Alignment

author.name: Dwip Dalal, Shivansh Patel, Chahit Jain, Jeonghwan Kim, Utkarsh Mishra, Alex Baratian, Hyeonjeong Ha, Heng Ji, Svetlana Lazebnik, Unnat Jain

entry.summary: Anchor-Align improves generalizable vision-language-action finetuning by distilling layer-wise representations from a frozen VLM copy to prevent behavior-cloning drift and by aligning language and action on shared observations. It addresses language-action misalignment that standard manipulation benchmarks do not expose.

entry.title: Compressed Computation under L⁴ Loss is likely Computation in Superposition

author.name: Francisco Ferreira da Silva

entry.summary: This explores using natural language autoencoders to read out what a monitor model internally represents while judging an agent's trajectory, aiming to surface unverbalized knowledge of reward hacking. It finds NLA readouts can elicit latent monitor capabilities and offer a partially decorrelated monitoring surface complementary to chain-of-thought.

entry.title: The Hyperspherical Geometry of CLIP Latent Space: A Semantic Mixture Model

author.name: Zijie Yu, Gaowen Liu, Ramana Rao Kompella, Philip S. Yu, Yue Song

entry.summary: This paper models CLIP latent space with a mixture of von Mises-Fisher distributions on the unit hypersphere, matching the space's directional cosine-similarity geometry better than Gaussian assumptions, with each component representing a semantic concept. EM yields a closed-form likelihood aligned to hyperspherical structure.

entry.title: SIVA-RL: Sensitivity-Invariance Visual Alignment for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Cheng Tang, Junzhi Ning, Min Cen, Wei Li, Xinyi Zeng, Pinxian Zeng, Rongbin Li, Qiming Zhu, Yuqiang Li, Junjun He, Yirong Chen, Ming Hu

entry.summary: SIVA-RL introduces sample-wise, outcome-conditioned supervision for multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, replacing operator-conditioned regularization so that visual grounding aligns with observed intervention effects rather than intervention type. It aims to ensure vision-language models ground answers in visual evidence.

entry.title: From Pixels to States: Rethinking Interactive World Models as Game Engines

author.name: Zhen Li, Zian Meng, Shuwei Shi, Mingliang Zhai, Jiaming Tan, Chuanhao Li, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: This work rethinks interactive video world models as game engines, arguing that genuine interactivity needs rule-following over evolving states, persistent long-horizon consequences, and real-time generation via a recurrent action-state-observation loop. It bridges neural video generation with explicit game-state mechanics.

entry.title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders

author.name: Zhihao Xie, Junfeng Wu, Xinting Hu, Junchao Huang, Li Jiang

entry.summary: VideoRAE explores whether frozen video foundation model representations such as V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAEv2 can be turned into compact, reconstruction-capable, generation-friendly latents, proposing a representation autoencoder over multi-scale hierarchical features. It aims to improve semantic and spatio-temporal structure of video latents versus pixel-optimized 3D-VAEs.

entry.title: EgoHTR: Egocentric 4D Demonstrations of Human Terrain Traversal

author.name: Alex Brandes, Haig Conti Georges Sajelian, Manthan Patel, Dominik Hollidt, Chenhao Li, Matthias Heyrman, Oliver Hausdoerfer, Manuel Kaufmann, Xi Wang, Jonas Frey, Angela P. Schoellig, Christian Holz, Marc Pollefeys, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: EgoHTR introduces an egocentric 4D dataset and open-source pipeline capturing scene-aligned human motion across challenging terrain to support humanoid learning in unstructured environments. It targets context-aware motion synthesis for terrain traversal.

entry.title: OriginBlame: Record- and Token-Level Data Provenance for AI Training Datasets

author.name: Haolin Xue

entry.summary: Proposes a record- and token-level data provenance system that tracks author identity through data pipelines, so removal requests can be resolved into precise forget sets instead of deleting entire datasets. On Wikipedia data it cuts over-deletion from 101x to 1.3x with modest throughput overhead.

entry.title: Final Authority in AI Governance: Frontier-Provider Sovereignty and Action-Centered Deployer Governance

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces safeguard-conditioned uplift, a protocol that compares deployed access conditions of dual-use biology assistants via a human-judged utility-risk frontier rather than base-model capability alone. Evaluating Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 3.5 Flash across prompting and safeguarded conditions, an external safeguarded assistant reduces harmful uplift in a blinded human audit.

entry.title: Deconstructing Actor-Critic: A Large-scale Empirical Study of Design Components for Practitioners

author.name: Haseeb Shah, Lingwei Zhu, Adam White, Martha White

entry.summary: A large empirical study of over 33,000 actor-critic experiments on a real water-treatment control task, analyzing how design choices such as action distribution, gradient estimator, and update frequency affect run variability and hyperparameter sensitivity. It targets practitioners deploying RL in reliability-critical real-world systems.

entry.title: EXPLORE: Exploration with Guided Search for Analog Topology Generation using Language Models

author.name: Guanglei Zhou, Chen-Chia Chang, Yikang Shen, Jonathan Ku, Isaac Jacobson, Jingyu Pan, Yiran Chen, Xin Zhang

entry.summary: EXPLORE augments language-model-based analog circuit topology generation with simulator-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search and transformer decoding, enabling test-time scaling for complex circuits that one-shot generation fails to produce. It combines LM priors with search over exponential design spaces.

entry.title: Local Redundancy: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Plasticity from Synthetic Memorization

author.name: Jiaxuan Cheng

entry.summary: This work introduces local redundancy, an information-theoretic measure of neural network plasticity derived from universal compression theory, and shows the expected squared gradient norm on a synthetic memorization task approximates it efficiently. It offers a theoretically grounded alternative to heuristic plasticity metrics.

entry.title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding

author.name: Ximeng Mao, Nanda H. Krishna, Avery Hee-Woon Ryoo, Matthew G. Perich, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: MOJO is a training framework for spike-tokenizing neural decoders that jointly uses masked-autoencoding self-supervision and supervised objectives, enabling training on unlabeled neural data without paired behavioral labels. It improves generalizable population decoding across monkey motor cortex datasets.

entry.title: Worlds in One Demo: A Synthetic Data Engine for Learning Open-World Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Lingxiao Guo, Huanyu Li, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: WANDA is a synthetic data engine that reconstructs backgrounds as Gaussian splats and robot-object interaction trajectories from a single demonstration, then rearranges contact-rich interactions to generate diverse training data for open-world mobile manipulation. It aims to scale beyond costly teleoperation.

entry.title: Theory-Level Autoformalization: From Isolated Statements to Unified Formal Knowledge Bases

author.name: Marcus J. Min, Mike He, Zhaoyu Li, Zixuan Yi, Sharad Malik, Aarti Gupta, Xujie Si, Osbert Bastani

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that autoformalization should move from isolated statements to whole theories, formalizing interdependent axioms, definitions, and lemmas as structured libraries. It surveys the field and proposes paths forward.

entry.title: LAPO: Leave-One-Turn Attribution for Self-Generated Process Rewards in Multi-Turn Search Reasoning

author.name: Qiang Zhu, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes LAPO, a self-generated process-supervision method that estimates each search turn's contribution by replacing it with a placeholder and measuring the change in log-likelihood of the gold answer. It applies sign-consistency gating to derive process rewards for multi-turn search reasoning.

entry.title: SAFETY SENTRY: Context-Aware Human Intervention via EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE Routing

author.name: Tianyu Chen, Chujia Hu, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: Reframes agent action safety as a per-instance three-way routing decision among execute, ask, and refuse, rather than a binary safe/unsafe label. Safety Sentry is a lightweight guard model that reduces routine interruptions while still catching consequential actions.

entry.title: AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities

author.name: Zichen Ding, Jiaye Ge, Shufan Jiang, Kai Chen, Mo Li, Qingqiu Li, Zehao Li, Zonglin Li, Tiaohao Liang, Shudong Liu, Zerun Ma, Zixing Shang, Wenhui Tian, Zun Wang, Liwei Wu, Zhenyu Wu, Jun Xu, Bowen Yang, Dingbo Yuan, Qi Zhang, Songyang Zhang, Peiheng Zhou, Dongsheng Zhu

entry.summary: Presents AgentCompass, an open-source, extensible infrastructure for evaluating LLM agents, organized into decoupled Benchmark, Harness, and Environment components with a fault-tolerant asynchronous runtime and trajectory analysis. It aims to reduce fragmentation and redundant engineering in agent evaluation.

entry.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0

author.name: Wenxiao Wang, Priyatham Kattakinda, Soheil Feizi

entry.summary: Investigates whether agent-optimization gains compound over time using a two-phase continual-learning evaluation on hard Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks. It tests whether re-optimizing an already-optimized agent on new tasks preserves earlier gains across three harness-optimization approaches.

entry.title: The Entanglement Wall: Activation-Space Probes as Risk Detectors, Not Context Adjudicators

author.name: Dominik Schwarz

entry.summary: Tests whether residual-stream activation probes can distinguish harmful requests from surface-matched benign controls at useful operating points across three 7-8B model families. It finds probes work well as blunt risk detectors but transfer poorly to context-sensitive matched pairs, arguing they are risk detectors not context adjudicators.

entry.title: Baselines Before Architecture: Evaluating Coding Agents for Autonomous Penetration Testing

author.name: Ananda Dhakal, Krish Neupane, Aarjan Chaudhary

entry.summary: Runs a controlled study on the 104-task XBOW penetration-testing benchmark using default coding CLI agents with a shared model, budget, and scoring rule to isolate how much of reported performance comes from harnesses versus the backbone. It establishes strong plain-agent baselines before comparing custom security scaffolds.

entry.title: The Refusal Residue: When Probes Catch Alignment Faking and When They Don't

author.name: Aman Mehta

entry.summary: Studies whether hidden-state probes can detect naturally emerging alignment faking across a thirteen-model sweep, finding faking arises in only two models and that both show an asymmetric refusal residue in monitored versus unmonitored compliance. It explores when internal probes catch strategic compliance that behavior alone hides.

entry.title: Targeted Recovery of Weight-Space Mechanisms From Neural Networks

author.name: Antoine Vigouroux, Lee Sharkey

entry.summary: Proposes targeted parameter decomposition that identifies only the network components processing specific inputs of interest by adding a high-rank catch-all component for non-target data, reducing the compute needed to interpret large models. It recovers reproducible, mechanistically faithful circuits in transformer language models using a small fraction of full-decomposition FLOPs.

entry.title: HEDGEHOG: Hierarchical Evaluation of Drug Generators Through Rigorous Filtration

author.name: Daria A. Ryabchenko (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia, Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, Artificial Intelligence Center, Moscow, Russia), Pavel Gurevich (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia, Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, Artificial Intelligence Center, Moscow, Russia), Shamil Kadyrov (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia), Daria Frolova (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia, Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, Artificial Intelligence Center, Moscow, Russia), Kseniia Fedisheva (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia), Sergei A. Nikolenko (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia), Alexander Shapeev (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia, Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, Artificial Intelligence Center, Moscow, Russia), Marina A. Pak (Ligand Pro, Moscow, Russia)

entry.summary: HEDGEHOG is a six-stage filtration benchmark for evaluating de novo molecular generators, inspired by industrial hit-identification workflows that screen for target activity, synthetic accessibility, and physicochemical plausibility. It argues that common generator metrics poorly reflect medicinal viability, producing misleading evaluations.

entry.title: Temperature Scaling Is Not Enough: Calibration Gaps Under Human Label Distributions

author.name: Wisdom Dogah

entry.summary: This paper shows that temperature scaling, the dominant post-hoc calibration method, degrades when ground-truth labels are soft or distributional rather than one-hot, using CIFAR-10H and ChaosNLI human-annotated datasets. It examines whether the degradation scales with model size.

entry.title: Factorized Spectral Representations for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Junyi Wu, Dan Li

entry.summary: FaStR extends spectral representation learning for continuous control by treating the transition kernel as a three-mode tensor and fitting a CP decomposition with a noise-contrastive objective, yielding separate state, action, and next-state feature maps. It aims for more sample-efficient world-model representations.

entry.title: Optimal and Efficient Contextual Combinatorial Semi-bandits with General Function Approximation

author.name: Hao Qin, Chicheng Zhang

entry.summary: SquareCB.Comb is a computationally efficient algorithm for contextual combinatorial semi-bandits with general reward function approximation, solving a convex problem per round to sample combinatorial actions and achieving minimax-optimal regret. It scales to large arm sets with only a cardinality bound.

entry.title: DNA: Dual-stage Native Attribution for Generated Image Source Tracing

author.name: Chao Wang, Kejiang Chen, Zijin Yang, Yaofei Wang, Yuang Qi, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage passive attribution method that traces generated images back to their source model by exploiting the observation that VAE-level cues capture model-family traits while backbone-level cues distinguish within-family variants. It targets digital forensics without watermarking or model modification.

entry.title: AspectCLIP: Optimizing CLIP Representation Space via Aspect-Guided Consistency Regularization

author.name: Yiyang Yao, Shanglin Liu, Jianming Lv, Chengjun Wang, Jinyi Li, Yuchan Jie, Zhihua Jin

entry.summary: AspectCLIP reformulates contrastive consistency regularization to handle the asymmetry that captions describe only one aspect of an image, avoiding semantic distortion when visually similar images have divergent text. It aims to improve the CLIP representation space.

entry.title: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5: A Faster and Stronger WAM Empowered by AutoResearch

author.name: GigaWorld Team, Angen Ye, Angyuan Ma, Boyuan Wang, Chaojun Ni, Fangzheng Ye, Guan Huang, Guo Li, Guosheng Zhao, Haodong Yan, Hengtao Li, Jiwen Lu, Kai Wang, Mingming Yu, Qitang Hu, Qiuping Deng, Songling Liu, Xiaoyu Tian, Xiaofeng Wang, Xinyu Zhou, Xiuwei Xu, Xinze Chen, Yang Wang, Yejun Zeng, Yifan Chang, Yun Ye, Zhenyu Wu, Zhanqian Wu, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 is an action-centered World Action Model that uses future visual dynamics only during training and decodes actions directly at inference to avoid the cost of generating videos online. It targets faster, real-time closed-loop robot control.

entry.title: Expanding AI Control from Models to Harnesses

author.name: fastfedora

entry.summary: This argues that AI control research has focused on bare tool-using agents while real frontier deployments now use rich agent harnesses with memory, subagents, and compaction, changing the threat landscape. It demonstrates how a rogue agent could exploit Claude Code features to attack while appearing monitored, and calls for harness-level vulnerability and evaluation research.

entry.title: How much of ML research is about AI safety, what is it about, and who's doing it?

author.name: emanuelr

entry.summary: An empirical meta-analysis that used a language model to classify every paper accepted at ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS from 2019 to 2026, identifying about 4.2 percent as AI safety work and finding safety's share grew roughly 25-fold to 8.3 percent. It provides an interactive dataset and website of subdomains and authors.

entry.title: SPINE: Bridging the Cyber-Physical Gap with Agentic AI

author.name: Minkyu Ham, Dongho Kim, Chan Lee, Jiayi Wang, Min Jun Kim, Yixi Zhang, Guo Ye, Jihai Zhao, Soyeon Park, Han Liu

entry.summary: Introduces an agentic multi-agent framework to profile, diagnose, and repair bimanual robot deployments so teleoperation works with minimal robotics expertise. It targets the calibration bottleneck that separates capable foundation-model reasoning from working physical hardware.

entry.title: Safeguard-Conditioned Uplift: Measuring Utility-Risk Frontiers for Dual-Use Biology Assistants

author.name: Dipesh Tharu Mahato

entry.summary: Introduces Safe-Psych, a sequential benchmark of over 1,000 segmented psychiatric clinical notes with psychiatrist-labeled actions to test whether LLMs appropriately diagnose, clarify, or abstain as evidence is disclosed incrementally. It targets the gap in medical benchmarks that assume complete information upfront.

entry.title: ShortOPD: Recovering Pruned LLMs with Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Qingyu Zhang, Qianhao Yuan, Hongyu Lin, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han, Le Sun, Xiang Li, Ming Xu, Jiarui Li, Xiuyin Zhao

entry.summary: Diagnoses why structurally pruned LLMs collapse on free-form generation despite recovering on multiple-choice tasks, tracing failures mainly to suffix repetition and demoted-but-not-erased generations. It proposes ShortOPD, a short-to-long on-policy distillation recovery method using the pre-compression model as a frozen teacher.

entry.title: SteinGate: Tail-Sensitive Safe Reinforcement Learning via Stein Discrepancy

author.name: Yassine Chemingui, Chenhua Fan, Honghao Wei, Janardhan Rao Doppa

entry.summary: Introduces SteinGate, a boundary-aware distributional safety certificate for safe RL that uses Kernelized Stein Discrepancy to check whether rollout costs remain consistent with a safe reference distribution, accounting for boundary atoms from clipped costs. It dynamically adapts the learning regime to catch rare but catastrophic tail events that expected-cost criteria miss.

entry.title: EgoProceVQA: A Novel Egocentric Procedural Understanding Task with Self-Skill-Exploration Agent

author.name: Junlong Li, Junxi Li, Yuxiang Yang, Wenbin Zou, Lap-Pui Chau, Yi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and data-generation platform for evaluating egocentric procedural understanding in multimodal LLMs and agents, focusing on key-step-level reasoning for wearable AI assistants. It fills a gap in current egocentric video QA evaluation.

entry.title: GPUSimBench: Towards Scalable and Reliable GPU-Accelerated Simulators in Embodied AI

author.name: Huzhenyu Zhang, Shenghai Yuan, Wenrui Yan, Li Ma, Hengjie Li, Jingcheng Pang, Dmitry Yudin

entry.summary: GPUSimBench benchmarks mainstream GPU-accelerated robotics simulators such as Isaac Lab and Genesis, exposing trade-offs among parallel efficiency, physical fidelity, and execution determinism via controlled physical-grounding tests. It aims to improve reliability of large-scale robot learning infrastructure.

entry.title: Ego-Dynamics-Augmented World Model for Autonomous Driving with Zero-Shot Cross-Chassis Adaptation

author.name: Zhidong Wang, Jingsong Liang, Zirui Li, Zhan Chen, Han Yu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: DynaDreamer augments a Dreamer-style driving world model with an explicit physics-informed ego-dynamics prior so the model spends less capacity recovering ego-motion from warped bird's-eye-view observations, improving scene modeling and imagination. It also enables zero-shot cross-chassis adaptation.

entry.title: Discriminative Barrier Functions for Safe Adversarial Imitation Learning from Observation

author.name: Anubhav Vishwakarma, Bhaumik Mehta, Caleb Hsu, Byron Boots, Karen Leung, Tyler Han

entry.summary: Constrains reward candidacy during inverse reinforcement learning to the space of control barrier functions, enabling data-driven recovery of safety barriers directly from unlabeled expert observations while providing safe online control with continuous improvement. It jointly addresses unsafe IRL exploration and the difficulty of hand-designing CBFs.

entry.title: Towards demystifying the creativity of diffusion models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post on theoretical work aiming to explain why diffusion models produce novel, creative outputs rather than merely memorizing training data. The provided excerpt is minimal, categorized under algorithms and theory.

entry.title: Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents

author.name: Richmond Alake, Cesare Bernardis, Paul Cayet, Luca Engel, Damien Hilloulin, Sungpack Hong, Allen Hosler, Nickolas Kavantzas, Ingo Kossyk, Son Le, Rhicheek Patra, Kartik Talamadupula, Valentin Venzin

entry.summary: A technical report on a database-native memory substrate for long-horizon agents, framing agent memory as a lifecycle of ingestion, extraction, consolidation, retrieval, and revision built on Oracle Database. It targets retention of task state, user facts, and procedural knowledge across sessions.

entry.title: Networked Intelligence: Active Shared Context Graphs for Human-AI Team Science

author.name: Sutanay Choudhury, Jeffrey J. Czajka, Lummy M. O. Monteiro, Erin Bredeweg, Jason McDermott, Katherine Wolf, Alex Beliaev, Josh Elmore, Paul Piehowski, Kylee Tate, Yuqian Gao, Aivett Bilbao, Kelly Stratton, Scott Baker, Jaydeep P. Bardhan, Kristin Burnum Johnson, Chris Oehmen, Robert Rallo

entry.summary: Introduces Mycelium, an active shared context graph aimed at scaling connections among humans, agents, instruments, and robots for team science rather than scaling a single reasoner. It reframes AI-for-science around networked intelligence across collaborators.

entry.title: STOCKTAKE: Measuring the Gap Between Perception and Action in LLM Agents with a Fair Oracle

author.name: Sagar Deb, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: Introduces STOCKTAKE, a 26-week supply-chain replenishment benchmark built as a factored partially observable MDP with a computable fair Bayes-filter reference policy. It separates perception failures from the knowing-doing gap in LLM agents on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management

author.name: Haoran Li, Jiebi Deng, Tong Jin, Jinghong Han, Yuxin Wang, Zexin Wang, Qingyi Si, Weikang Gong, Xiahai Zhuang, Jia You, Wei Cheng, Jianfeng Feng, Hongcheng Guo

entry.summary: Presents HealthClaw, an open-source self-evolving agent for longitudinal personal health management that separates shared safety and medical knowledge from private longitudinal memory, updating profiles and procedures after each episode. On a synthetic year-long benchmark it dramatically improves answer accuracy over current-query prompting.

entry.title: SingGuard-NSFA: Extensible Guardrails for Agentic AI via Generative Reasoning and Real-Time Classification

author.name: SingGuard Team

entry.summary: Presents nsfaguard, a guardrail framework for agentic AI covering prompt injection, sensitive-data extraction, malicious code, dangerous tool misuse, and resource exhaustion, organized by a CIA-triad-grounded taxonomy of 185 risk variants. It ships a large multilingual benchmark spanning 133 languages and a dual-mode detection approach.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust and Safe Imitation Learning

author.name: Ahmed Aboudonia, Naira Hovakimyan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a distributionally robust and safe imitation learning framework that jointly handles policy-induced distribution shifts via Taylor Series Imitation Learning and uncertainty-induced shifts via robust adaptive control, while enforcing safety constraints. It targets safety-critical IL under distribution shift.

entry.title: Evaluating Frontier AI Agents as Autonomous Clinical Security Auditors

author.name: Michael O. Eniolade

entry.summary: This work presents an open evaluation task built on the METR Task Standard testing whether frontier AI agents can autonomously perform a structured clinical AI security audit, implementing adversarial attacks and computing a Security Posture Score in a sandboxed environment. It probes agent capability at safety-critical automated auditing.

entry.title: Non-Expansive Two-Time-Scale Stochastic Approximation: A Fixed-Schedule One-Quarter Barrier and Bias-Corrected Acceleration

author.name: Dhruv Sarkar, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: This paper analyzes non-expansive two-time-scale stochastic approximation governed by a slow Krasnoselskii-Mann fixed-point iteration, proving a finite-horizon lower bound that explains the observed k^-1/4 residual exponent and introducing a bias-corrected acceleration scheme. It advances theory for a regime lacking unique-equilibrium contraction.

entry.title: Towards Enhancing 3D Spatial Reasoning in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zhuoyuan Fu, Zeshang Li, Yiqiong Zhang, Hangui Lin, Yan Shu, Yan Li, Binyang Li, Yaru Zhao

entry.summary: Builds a large structured reasoning dataset for 3D medical volumes using a slice-wise synthesis paradigm that mimics radiologist workflow, aiming to improve 3D spatial reasoning in medical multimodal LLMs. It addresses annotation cost and lack of explicit clinical reasoning in existing formats.

entry.title: How to Guide LLM Generation: Dual-Surrogate Guided Search for Automated Heuristic Design

author.name: Yuhan Wang, Chaoda Peng, Xingyu Wu, Sheng-Hao Wu, Zhi-Hui Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-surrogate guided action-selection module for LLM-based automated heuristic design, modeling the expected outcome of concrete operator-parent choices before each costly LLM query and evaluation. It improves search efficiency under limited query budgets.

entry.title: Automatic Ordinary Differential Equations Discovery For Biological Systems Using Large Language Model Powered Agentic System

author.name: David Krongauz, Arad Zulti, Eran Segal, Teddy Lazebnik

entry.summary: Presents MEDA, an LLM- and symbolic-regression-powered agentic system for automatically discovering ordinary differential equations describing biological systems from data. It aims to move beyond narrow equation-discovery benchmarks toward mechanistic biological modeling.

entry.title: When Bots Join the Team: Bot Adoption and the Institutional Fabric of Open-Source Software Projects

author.name: Yongren Shi, Wenyi Gong

entry.summary: Studies how adopting the first bot affects coordination in open-source software teams by analyzing nearly 3,000 GitHub projects two years before and after adoption. It finds bot adoption is followed by more repeated collaboration and changes in institutional capabilities like social memory and role differentiation.

entry.title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents

author.name: Wenjun Wang, Yuchen Fang, Fengrui Liu, Zibo Liang, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes Experience Memory Graph, which reframes agent failure recovery as graph matching by converting failed and successful trajectories into a structured memory for one-shot error correction. It aims to replace brittle, costly prompt-based reflection with reusable, generalizable memory.

entry.title: Compaction as Epistemic Failure: How Agentic LLM Tools Fabricate Confirmed Results from Killed Processes

author.name: Hiroki Tamba

entry.summary: Documents a failure mode in an agentic coding tool where partial output from timed-out commands is recorded in compaction summaries as confirmed results and inherited as ground truth across sessions and model versions. It attributes this to conflating observation with durable persistence.

entry.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture

author.name: Gordon Burtch

entry.summary: Examines whether AI coding assistants homogenize software using Kaggle submissions from 2019 to 2026, documenting widespread convergence toward the random seed value 42 and studying broader homogenization at submission and abstraction levels. It links convergence to LLMs reinforcing existing programming conventions.

entry.title: WaterMoE: Expert-Routing-based Watermarking for High Fidelity and Efficiency

author.name: Z Sun, Q Jiang, S Sheng, L Xiang

entry.summary: Benchmarks nine representative LLM watermarking methods and finds most degrade performance on restricted or complex tasks and add prohibitive inference overhead. It proposes WaterMoE, an expert-routing-based watermarking approach aimed at higher fidelity and lower overhead.

entry.title: TSSM: Triaxial State Space Model for Global Station Weather Forecasting with Temporal-Variable-Historical Modeling

author.name: Songru Yang, Zili Liu, Tao Han, Ben Fei, Fenghua Ling, Lei Bai, Chang Liu, Xiangyang Ji, Zhenwei Shi, Zhengxia Zou

entry.summary: Proposes a triaxial state space model for global station weather forecasting that augments the temporal look-back window with period-aligned historical data to capture long-term and periodic patterns. It targets improved accuracy on extreme events and reduced error accumulation.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework from Tokenization to Generation

author.name: Ye Yuan, Weien Li, Rui Song, Zeyu Li, Haochen Liu, Xiangyu Kong, Zixuan Dong, Linfeng Du, Zipeng Sun, Weixu Zhang, Jiaxin Huang, Changjiang Han, Yonghan Yang, Zichen Zhao, Xiuyuan Hu, Haolun Wu, Yankai Chen, Fengran Mo, Jikun Kang, Bowei He, Philip S. Yu, Xue Liu

entry.summary: Offers a unified conceptual framework for discrete denoising diffusion models organized around how the underlying discrete state space is constructed via tokenization, vocabulary topology, and structural alphabets. It shows transition-matrix, masking, and score-based formulations as instances of this view.

entry.title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers

author.name: Shuzhen Li, Yifan Zhang, Jiacheng Guo, Quanquan Gu, Mengdi Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes depth scaling for looped transformers, where a compact block stack is applied repeatedly, formalizing how tied weight reuse changes residual scaling via a visit-alignment coefficient. It derives a perturbation bound that recovers DeepNorm when visits decorrelate but requires different scaling when they align.

entry.title: Generative Compilation: On-the-Fly Compiler Feedback as AI Generates Code

author.name: Niels M\"undler-Sasahara, Hristo Venev, Dawn Song, Martin Vechev, Jingxuan He

entry.summary: Introduces generative compilation, the first approach to obtain compiler feedback on partial programs during autoregressive LLM decoding, via a lightweight syntax-guided transformation that seals partial programs into compilable form. It targets generating code in strict statically typed languages like Rust without needing white-box constrained decoding.

entry.title: Maximally Robust Satisficing Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Samuli Kinnunen, Petrus Mikkola, Antti Niskanen, Arto Klami

entry.summary: This work proposes a Bayesian optimization method that finds satisficing solutions, those merely good enough, that are maximally robust to input perturbations at deployment, rather than seeking a single optimum. It motivates robustness to deployment perturbations as a principled selection criterion within superlevel sets.

entry.title: An Efficient Newton Algorithm for Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with the Kullback-Leibler Divergence

author.name: Damien Lesens, J\'er\'emy E. Cohen, Bora U\c{c}ar

entry.summary: This paper proposes an efficient Newton-type algorithm for KL-divergence nonnegative matrix factorization by minimizing a non-separable second-order Taylor surrogate rather than the usual separable majorant. It targets count data such as term-document matrices and images.

entry.title: MetaPerch: Learning from metadata for bioacoustics foundation models

author.name: Mustafa Chasmai, Vincent Dumoulin, Jenny Hamer

entry.summary: MetaPerch incorporates readily available recording metadata such as location and time as auxiliary supervision to enrich bioacoustic foundation model representations trained on citizen-science data. Auxiliary metadata losses leverage species-metadata correlations for more robust species detection.

entry.title: HRIBench: Benchmarking Interaction-Centric Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Chang Liu, Jiawei Zhang, Tao Zhang, Ye Wang, Hongyu Zhou, Qin Jin

entry.summary: HRIBench is a diagnostic benchmark for interaction-centric human-robot collaboration that models agent roles, temporal dependencies, coordination constraints, and human behavior distributions as executable scenario scripts. It fills a gap in vision-language-action benchmarks that evaluate isolated manipulation rather than shared-agency coordination.

entry.title: Learned Pairwise Deep Dual-Optimal Inequalities for Stabilizing Column Generation

author.name: Zhengzhong Ricky You, Bo Tang, Haoran Liu, Baichuan Mo

entry.summary: This paper introduces learned pairwise deep dual-optimal inequalities that predict orderings between dual variables and inject their primal counterparts into the master problem to stabilize column generation for large-scale routing optimization. It replaces problem-specific exchange arguments with a learning framework.

entry.title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes

author.name: Jeremy Guntoro, Alexander Dack, Dylan Danno, Michaela Jan\v{c}ovi\v{c}ov\'a, Kri\v{z}an Jurinovi\'c, Vanessa Smilansky

entry.summary: Probes frozen activations of the Evo 2 genomic foundation model to assess how much biosecurity-relevant signal is linearly accessible, achieving strong antimicrobial-resistance detection with lightweight linear and attention probes. It shows foundation model representations encode fine-grained resistance drug-class information.

entry.title: Bake It Till You Make It: Ultrafast Spatial Texture-Atlas Splatting

author.name: Neel Kelkar, Simon Niedermayr, Kaloian Petkov, Klaus Engel, R\"udiger Westermann

entry.summary: Introduces a decoupled radiance representation for 3D Gaussian Splatting that models geometry with 2D surfels and bakes high-frequency textures into a compact atlas via a spatial hash grid, with sparsity-enhancing pruning. It delivers faster, sparser reconstructions for real-time rendering.

entry.title: Cyclone: Diffusion Model for Cycle-Consistent Weather Editing from Unpaired Driving Data

author.name: Thang-Anh-Quan Nguyen, Moussab Bennehar, Luis Guillermo Roldao Jimenez, Nathan Piasco, Dzmitry Tsishkou, Laurent Caraffa, Jean-Philippe Tarel, Roland Br\'emond

entry.summary: Cyclone is a latent-diffusion framework for cycle-consistent weather editing from unpaired driving data, adding weather effects or removing them using cycle constraints and image-text priors. It aims to improve autonomous-driving perception robustness without paired training data.

entry.title: Joint On-and-Off Policy Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Qingrong He, Lin Zhao, Kevin Zheng, Liang Lin

entry.summary: JOP-VLN unifies off-policy imitation learning on expert demonstrations with on-policy reinforcement learning driven by verifiable rewards for vision-and-language navigation, integrating two previously separate paradigms. It aims to combine error recovery with reasoning and exploration.

entry.title: Learning Robust Execution in Robotic Manipulation with Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xiaopeng Zhang, Yueyang Weng, Qi Liu, Yongjin Mu, Yanjie Li

entry.summary: Proposes two runtime execution-quality metrics and an agentic reinforcement learning framework for robotic manipulation that learns to restore effective execution through high-level decision making rather than low-level action learning. It addresses compounding errors and instability that VLA models struggle to recover from.

entry.title: S-squared-VLA: Decoupling Semantic and Spatial Streams in Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jianguo Yu, Rukang Wang, Duanfeng Chu, Chen Wang, Renju Feng, Liping Lu

entry.summary: S-squared-VLA decouples semantic and spatial streams within a vision-language-action model for autonomous driving to prevent spatial representation collapse that degrades geometric priors needed for boundary-aware navigation. It addresses the semantic-physical gap between discrete language tokens and continuous trajectory planning.

entry.title: PhysClaw-0: A Symbiotic Agentic System for Robot Autonomy via Language Corrections

author.name: Boyuan Wang, Zhenyuan Zhang, Zhiqin Yang, Peijun Gu, Shuya Wang, Xiaofeng Wang, Xianghui Ze, Yifan Chang, Guosheng Zhao, Jiangnan Shao, Guan Huang, Hengyu Liu, Yonggang Zhang, Wei Xue, Chunyuan Guan, Chenglin Pu, Yike Guo, Xingang Wang, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: PhysClaw-0 is a human-robot symbiotic agentic system for autonomous data collection where natural-language corrections are parsed by an LLM into structured adjustments that are retained and reused across rounds, so oversight cost grows with distinct problems rather than session length. It automates collection, verification, and reset while pausing only after retry budgets are exhausted.

entry.title: Set-shifting Behavioral Test for Harnessed Agents

author.name: Ziwei Ye

entry.summary: Borrows the set-shifting paradigm from cognitive psychology to test how LLM agents adapt when a reliable tool silently changes reliability mid-session. It finds agents tend to settle on rigid routines and adapt poorly to hidden shifts.

entry.title: How Far Can Root Cause Analysis Go on Real-World Telemetry Data?

author.name: Athira Gopal, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: Investigates root cause analysis on the large multimodal OpenRCA telemetry benchmark, where both classical causal discovery and existing LLM multi-agent methods perform poorly. It presents a structured multi-agent RCA pipeline that substantially outperforms prior baselines.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Sequential Decision Rules for Event-Triggered LLM Invocation in Streaming Systems

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: Casts the decision of when to invoke an expensive LLM within a streaming fast/slow pipeline as a risk-based sequential stopping problem, proving several theoretical results including regret bounds and threshold-policy optimality. It provides formal guarantees for event-triggered LLM invocation.

entry.title: CoDiffGRN: Rethinking Gene Regulatory Network Inference via the BEELINE-KGC Benchmark and Co-evolutionary Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Jiaze Song, Runhao Zhao, Minghao Xu, Bin Cui, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Reformulates gene regulatory network inference as an inductive, ranking-centric graph completion problem and introduces a new benchmark with inductive gene-holdout splits and knowledge-graph integration. It proposes a co-evolutionary discrete diffusion model to recover high-confidence interactions involving unseen genes.

entry.title: Adaptive Filtering of the KV Cache: Diagnosing and Correcting Structural-Role Bias in LLM Inference

author.name: Soumil Mandal

entry.summary: Diagnoses that attention-based KV cache eviction over-retains structural noise like delimiters and KEY tokens on schema-dense inputs such as nested JSON, collapsing exact-match accuracy from 88% to 0% at a 5% budget. It proposes adaptive filtering to correct this structural-role bias in the cache.

entry.title: Reassessing Muon for Matrix Factorization

author.name: Ali Parviz, Gal Mishne, Alex Cloninger

entry.summary: Studies the Muon optimizer on controlled low-rank matrix factorization to disentangle which of its benefits come from the orthogonalized update rule itself versus artifacts of scale, architecture, and data. It tests the interpretation of Muon as spectral-norm steepest descent in a clean, well-understood setting.

entry.title: Accuracy Without Grounding: Diagnosing Visual Dependency Dissociation in Video LLM Benchmarks

author.name: Jae Joong Lee

entry.summary: Audits whether video LLM benchmark accuracy actually reflects visual understanding by comparing performance on original video versus black-screen conditions across twenty models, introducing a Visual Dependency Gap metric. It finds accuracy and genuine visual grounding are separable, with temporal reasoning often near a language-only baseline.

entry.title: Self-Improving is Often Sudden: Enlightenment-style Finetuning for Large-Scale Models

author.name: Jing-Xiao Liao, Tianwei Zhang, Yu-Hao Jiang, Feifei Zhang, Hang-Cheng Dong, Feng-Lei Fan

entry.summary: Enlightenment is a training-free post-tuning paradigm that inserts architecture-specific shortcuts (such as attention head-mixing) to trigger sudden capability jumps without weight updates. It hypothesizes an aha-moment-like latent capacity in large models.

entry.title: DAGR: State-Conditioned Goal Representations via Difference-Aware Goal Cross-Attention

author.name: Xing Lei, Wenyan Yang, Xuetao Zhang, Donglin Wang
